title: How to control where semiconductor crystals start growing
abstract: Semiconductor crystals grow from tiny nuclei, but the position of these nuclei is difficult to control precisely and can affect the crystal’s properties. An approach using ‘etching flux’ has now been developed that constrains the position at which a nucleus forms, enabling spatially programmable growth of large single crystals of semiconducting material. Single crystals of a semiconductor can be formed in a spatially programmable way.

title: Retention and biosynthesis of diverse nitroarenes in Escherichia coli after combinatorial nitroreductase gene deletions
abstract: The instability of nitroaromatic compounds or nitroarenes in the presence of microbial cells has hindered the ability to biomanufacture these industrially and pharmaceutically relevant chemicals. Although nitroreductase (NTR) gene deletions have been linked to nitroarene stability, the extent of this effect is unclear. Here we perform a comprehensive analysis of bacterial NTR activity in cells by engineering strains of Escherichia coli that contain up to 15 knockouts of known and candidate NTR genes. We evaluate the stability of over 20 exogenously supplemented nitroaromatic compounds to wild-type and engineered strains. For several chemistries, such as di-nitro compounds and nitro-aldehydes, our engineered nitroaromatic reductase knockout strains enable retention of compounds. We leverage these tools and insights to improve or enable nitroaromatic compound biosynthesis, including the biocatalytic transformation of an amine precursor to a nitro compound, the biosynthesis of nitrobenzaldehydes and the combined semi-synthesis and site-specific incorporation of nitrophenylalanines from supplemented nitrobenzaldehydes. This work advances access to nitro functional group chemistry in cell-based biocatalysis, metabolic engineering and synthetic biology.

title: Evolution of dipole–dipole dynamics in cold ammonia collisions
last_author: Sebastiaan Y. T. van de Meerakker
abstract: Cold polar molecules offer fascinating prospects for ultracold chemistry and quantum physics. However, their inherent collision properties remain largely unknown, as it seems fundamentally impossible to reach sufficiently low energies by merging two beams of molecules with substantial dipole moments. Here we report measurements of state-to-state cross-sections for collisions between ammonia isotopologues at energies between 0.3 and 100 cm-1 using an advanced beam-merging protocol. We experimentally observed a local maximum in the cross-sections, which indicates that the dipole moments can switch off at low collision energies. Scattering calculations reproduced this maximum in good agreement and explained the observed scaling with the molecule's parity splitting energies. Measurements of the correlated energy transfer in both collision partners yielded direct evidence of the suppression of the dipole-dipole interaction at low energies. Our results demonstrate how collisions between an important class of polar molecules evolve from high temperatures towards the ultracold regime in a counterintuitive way, and offer distinctive opportunities to control cold molecular collisions with external fields.

title: Orthogonal nucleophile-ordered assembly for modular access to enantiopure 1,2-amino alcohols
abstract: The programmed assembly of multiple common chemicals with minimal reactivity differences into complex chiral architectures with high selectivity is a long-standing challenge in synthetic chemistry. Here we report a palladium-catalysed orthogonal multicomponent strategy that enables the sequential incorporation of two native N-H/O-H nucleophiles with similar reactivity into propargylic carbonates through a nucleophile-ordered assembly. Leveraging the tandem reactivity of the propargyl-palladium complex, this system functions as a sorting mechanism: stronger nucleophiles undergo outer-sphere addition to the propargyl-palladium intermediate, while weaker nucleophiles, guided by superior coordinating affinity, selectively attack the resulting allyl-palladium species through an inner-sphere mechanism. This strategy enables the precise recognition and ordered incorporation of diverse native nucleophile pairs, providing a platform and modular access to valuable chiral 1,2-amino alcohols and 1,2-diols with exceptional regio-, chemo-, Z- and enantiocontrol. This work demonstrates how subtle reactivity differences can be systematically harnessed for programmable complex synthesis from fundamental feedstocks.

title: Controlling reactions via nucleophile sorting

title: RNA catalysis emerges from dynamic structural ensembles
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The dynamic interplay between RNA structure and its associated Mg
                    2+
                    ions is central to RNA function yet remains poorly understood at a near-atomic level
                    1–4
                    . Here, using a heterogeneity-focused protocol for cryo-electron microscopy data analysis of conformationally flexible RNA particles, we determined the structures of RNase P RNA ensembles composed of 76 coexisting active and inactive conformers that differ in a transient tertiary interaction that is critical for activity. The binding of the accessory protein does not change the local structure but induces thermodynamic allostery that enhances catalysis by altering the dynamics of the tertiary interaction. Four distinct classes of Mg
                    2+
                    ions have critical roles in the structure, dynamics and catalysis of the conformational ensembles. Together, these findings establish a new paradigm in which catalysis is regulated through multimodal communications coupled with the dynamics of RNA–Mg
                    2+
                    conformational ensembles, rather than a single static catalytic structure in a single action mode.

title: Genetic encoding and mutagenesis of RNA droplet phenotypes
abstract:
Abstract
                  RNA droplets assembled from cotranscriptionally folded nanostructures have recently emerged as a promising platform for constructing protocells and minimal synthetic cell models. A custom-designed DNA template encodes an RNA nanostar that self-assembles into droplets by kissing-loop interactions. Here we show that such RNA droplets encapsulate their DNA template, creating a genotype–phenotype link. We find that low mutation rates in the DNA template increase the phenotypical and functional complexity of the RNA droplets. Surprisingly, mutagenesis leads to the formation of long-lived vacuoles. With theory and next-generation sequencing, we explain this emergent behavior. We identify mutant nanostars that facilitate the formation of vacuoles through altered interactions between nanostars. Strikingly, vacuolated droplets exhibit micrometer-scale movement driven by internal vacuole dynamics – an emergent function resulting from mutagenesis. Beyond motility, we show that the vacuoles can be used as subcompartments to store cargo in the RNA droplets. Our findings establish RNA droplets as self-contained, evolvable systems, opening new avenues for the bottom-up evolution of synthetic cells and origins-of-life research.

title: Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
abstract: Understanding and controlling valley-specific light-matter interactions and non-equilibrium microscopic coupling mechanisms lie at the heart of valleytronics. Due to their strong in-plane anisotropy, which enables polarization-controlled optical transitions to distinct non-degenerate valleys, group-IV monochalcogenides have been recently proposed as promising candidates for next-generation valleytronic materials. However, ultrafast non-equilibrium dynamics following the optical preparation of valley-polarized states have received limited attention in these systems. Here, combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with time-dependent Boltzmann equation simulations, we investigate ultrafast valley polarization dynamics following polarization-controlled photoexcitation in SnSe. We show that selective excitation to valleys at global conduction minima yields nearly unity and time-independent valley polarization. By contrast, photoexcitation to the other valley channel leads to ultrafast decay and reversal of valley polarization on subpicosecond timescales due to intervalley scattering mediated by strong electron-phonon coupling with an optical phonon mode. Our findings reveal strongly anisotropic and radically different non-equilibrium valley physics than in most common two-dimensional valleytronics materials.

title: Gene-driven self-morphing microtubule-based active matter
abstract: Materials that change shape or flow typically rely on external fields, photochemical cues or compositions fixed at assembly. Here we introduce a self-morphing active material whose mechanical behaviour is genetically programmed and executed autonomously. By embedding cell-free gene expression within a dense microtubule network, DNA instructions synthesize molecular motors, cross-linkers and transcription factors that continuously generate and regulate active stresses. This experimental platform enables gene-circuit architectures to directly program active-matter dynamics, producing steady, pulsed, arrested and oscillatory mechanical states from genetically encoded biochemical regulation alone. A coarse-grained reaction-mechanics model quantitatively captures these behaviours and shows how gene-circuit parameters, including expression rates, degradation kinetics and regulatory topology, govern the emergence and temporal evolution of active-matter states. Together, these results establish gene circuits as programmable control layers for active matter, providing a general strategy for engineering genetically encoded mechanochemical materials and autonomous active systems.

title: Magnetic control of an exciton–polariton condensate in a van der Waals magnet
abstract:
Abstract
                  Quasiparticle condensates are among the most striking solid-state manifestations of quantum physics. Coupling macroscopic real-space wavefunctions to additional degrees of freedom, such as the electron spin, would add valuable control knobs for quantum applications. While creating spin-carrying superconducting condensates has attracted enormous attention, condensates of light-matter hybrids known as exciton–polaritons have lacked an analogous spin-based perspective. Here we demonstrate magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr. Under photoexcitation, CrSBr microwires embedded in an optical cavity show the hallmarks of polariton condensation. Owing to the strong coupling between the spin order and excitonic correlation, the energy of the condensate can be tuned by up to 10.5 meV by an external magnetic field of 2 T. Our results establish CrSBr microcavities as a powerful platform for exploring magnetic control of polariton condensates and mark an essential step towards spin-controlled coherent quantum light sources.

title: Unanticipated intermediates during isopenicillin N synthase catalysis identified by time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Biosynthesis of penicillin and cephalosporin antibiotics involves the oxidation of the tripeptide δ-(
                    l
                    -α-aminoadipoyl)-
                    l
                    -cysteinyl-
                    d
                    -valine (ACV) to give the conformationally strained bicyclic penicillin ring system, as catalysed by the Fe(II)-dependent oxidase isopenicillin N synthase (IPNS). The structures of the precursors for the sequential β-lactam and thiazolidine ring forming steps in IPNS have remained elusive. Here we studied the reaction of anaerobic IPNS:Fe(II):ACV microcrystals with O
                    2
                    using time-resolved serial femtosecond crystallography and X-ray emission spectroscopy. High-resolution structures reveal that ACV cysteinyl oxidation produces a thioaldehyde that unexpectedly does not coordinate the iron centre. The use of deuterium-labelled ACV enabled the observation of a monocyclic β-lactam with restoration of the Fe–S bond. Together with mutagenesis, spectroscopic and computational studies, the results support Fe(IV)-mediated penicillin formation involving active-site water molecules. These findings provide structural insight into IPNS catalysis, inform on the wider Fe(II) oxygenase superfamily and highlight the power of X-ray free-electron laser methods for resolving transient enzymatic intermediates.

title: Reversible Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries
abstract: Aqueous batteries offer a relatively safe, energy-dense means to store electrochemical energy. Tin is a promising anode material, due to its potential four-electron redox-active states and lack of dendrite formation. However, the irreversible electrochemical behaviour of the Sn4+/Sn2+ couple have limited high-capacity anode development. Here we achieve the reversible Sn4+/Sn2+ conversion, enabling a Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries. We accomplish this by adding iodide to highly soluble SnCl4 solutions at ratios that form SnCl62- and SnI62- intermediate complexes. SnI62- reduces reorganization energy during the electrochemical reaction of Sn4+/Sn2+, ensuring reversibility. SnCl62- imparts anolyte solubility. The redox peak potential difference decreased from 978 mV (Cl-) to 97 mV (I-), with a substantial decrease to the electron transfer impedance decrease. Coupled with Br-/Br2, the assembled full battery showed 89% energy efficiency at 40 mA cm-2, 227 Ah l-1 anolyte capacity and 205 Wh l-1 anolyte energy density. Based on these studies, we developed a kilowatt-scale stack that can operate stably for over 1,000 h.

title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to < 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.

title: Simulating Chemical Reaction Dynamics Using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization: A Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Approach
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
last_author: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala
abstract: Abstract Quantum computers offer the potential to simulate chemical systems beyond the capabilities of classical computers. However, current quantum computing approaches to ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and vibrational analysis largely rely on the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), whose circuit depth, iterative optimization, and measurement overhead hinder the practical simulation of molecular systems. Here, we extend Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a quantum sampling-based electronic-structure method, to AIMD and vibrational analysis on noisy quantum hardware. The resulting framework enables nuclear forces and Hessians to be derived from quantum-computed electronic energies, facilitating molecular dynamics and characterization of potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate the approach using diverse molecular processes, including H2 bond vibration, the proton-exchange reaction (H+ + H2), the bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction (Cl– + CH3Cl), and proton-transfer dynamics between two water molecules involving transient formation of the Zundel cation (H2O···H+···OH2). Across these systems, SQD-AIMD trajectories and vibrational frequencies obtained with noisy quantum hardware/noise-models show excellent agreement with classical reference calculations and substantially improved accuracy relative to previously reported VQE-based simulations. Importantly, the SQD-based approach eliminates costly variational optimization and significantly reduces measurement requirements relative to VQE, enabling AIMD simulations spanning approximately 500 timesteps (∼200 fs), substantially longer than previously reported AIMD simulations on quantum hardware. These results establish SQD-AIMD and SQD-vibrational analysis as practical and scalable frameworks for simulating chemical reaction dynamics and elucidating reaction mechanisms on near-term quantum hardware, extending quantum computing applications beyond static electronic structure calculations.

title: In Situ Ion-Exchange-Mediated Dynamic Nanointerface Reconfiguration for Polarity-Switchable Photoelectrochemical–Photothermal Biosensing
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems typically rely on static semiconductor interfaces that merely translate biomolecular recognition into amplitude modulation of the pre-existing photocurrent, thus limiting their analytical robustness and self-validation capabilities. Herein, we report in situ ion-exchange-mediated dynamic nanointerface engineering to fabricate an analyte-programmed reconfigurable PEC–photothermal (PT) dual-mode biosensor for the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assay. The Z-scheme heterostructure of a plasmonic Au nanoparticle (NP) layer-supported BiOI/AgI/indium tin oxide glass (BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO) is constructed as the initial photoelectrode. In the sensing process, a CEA recognition event directly reshapes the phase composition of BiOI/AgI, charge-transfer behavior, and photoresponse polarity. The synergistic integration of the BiOI/AgI heterostructure and the close-packed layer of plasmonic Au NPs substantially enhance the light absorption, charge separation, and interfacial charge transfer, making BiOI/AgI/Au NPs/ITO a highly suitable photoelectrode for the PEC mode of the PEC–PT biosensor. This analyte-driven phase evolution reconstructs the semiconductor composition, band alignment, and charge-transfer pathways to switch the photocurrent polarity from cathodic to anodic. In addition, a photothermal imaging mode of the PEC–PT biosensor is triggered by regulating the Bi2S3 formation for intrinsic cross-validation. By integrating an artificial neural network (ANN)-assisted analysis, PEC–PT biosensors enable robust multimodal quantification and improved analytical reliability, achieving > 99.8% prediction accuracy in real-sample analysis. This is the first example of integrating a dynamic nanointerface-driven PEC–PT dual-mode biosensor with artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced multimodal analysis for CEA detection and provides a dynamic nanointerface-driven strategy for intelligent multimode biosensing.

title: Benzaldehyde Is the Redox Mediator for Aerobic C–N Cleavage in Epoxy Composite Recycling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chemical methods are promising avenues to recycle fiber-reinforced polymer waste. Here, we reintroduce tripotassium phosphate-mediated benzyl alcohol conditions for epoxy cleavage. While these conditions were developed in 2008 for anhydride-cured epoxy cleavage and have been applied to amine-linked epoxy cleavage, no account has been made of why these conditions should work with the latter, or why air exposure appears critical for their success. We now show how benzaldehyde, formed in situ from benzyl alcohol, plays the crucial redox role that enables selective C–N bond cleavage: tertiary amines are cleaved by a previously uncharacterized mechanism in which benzaldehyde facilitates iminium formation from the polymer’s C–N linkage. Subsequent hydrolysis and base-promoted elimination cleave the C═N and C–O bonds, respectively, enabling the recovery of bisphenol A and release of the linking diamines. Carbon fiber (CF) and even glass fiber (GF) fabrics are preserved, and recovered CF fabrics are remanufactured into second-generation composites with near-virgin quality and mechanical performance. These mechanistic insights may inform the future development of selective diamine recovery strategies from thermosets, which is a challenge when valorizing composites. Collectively, these results present promising recycling conditions with the potential to valorize matrices and fibers from a wide range of composites, spanning high-performance carbon fiber to widely used fiberglass.

title: High-frequency inductively heated molten salt bubbling beds for methane pyrolysis
abstract: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. This study shows that high-frequency magnetic induction directly and volumetrically heats molten salt bubbling beds with stable power delivery, providing a scalable route for methane pyrolysis while managing solid carbon formation. These principles have applicability more broadly to molten salt chemical conversion and thermal energy storage systems.

title: Light Ignites Lattice Oxygen in an Asymmetric Motif
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lattice-oxygen-mediated pathways bypass the energy-intensive steps that constrain adsorbate-mediated catalysis. Activating these pathways under mild conditions, however, means breaking metal–oxygen bonds that are, by design, strong. Asymmetric M1-O-M2 motifs, in which a bridging oxygen sits between two cations of different electronic character, decouple oxygen activation from oxygen release by distributing these functions across chemically distinct sites. Here, we show that a Cu-doped In2O3 system with a well-defined asymmetric Cu–O–In unit exhibits enhanced photoinduced lattice oxygen activity. Series (quasi) in situ spectroscopy captures the activation, consumption, and replenishment of lattice oxygen under illumination in real time. Photogenerated carriers populate around the Cu–O site preferentially, weakening the Cu–O bond enough to extract lattice oxygen at room temperature. The optimized material, Cui-In2O3, gives a response of 32.4 toward 5 ppm of H2S under visible light. The results connect local coordination asymmetry directly to photoinduced oxygen functionality and suggest a route toward photodriven catalysts built around asymmetric oxygen sites.

title: Single-Water Microsolvation Promotes Proton Sharing in a Neutral Formic Acid–Ammonia Complex
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Can single-water microsolvation promote proton sharing in a neutral acid–base complex? We address this question for formic acid–ammonia by isolating its monohydrated complex with broadband rotational spectroscopy and interpreting the resolved 14N hyperfine structure with calibrated high-level quantum chemistry. The observed complex is a single dominant HCOOH–NH3–H2O isomer with effective Cs symmetry, in which NH3 remains the primary proton acceptor, while water closes a cooperative hydrogen-bond cycle by accepting from NH3 and donating to the carbonyl oxygen. Rather than simply stabilizing the binary acid–base contact, this water molecule measurably increases its proton-sharing character. A resolved A/E tunneling pattern from NH3 internal rotation supplies the missing orientation needed to rotate the experimental 14N quadrupole tensor into the local ammonia frame, yielding an experimental χzz component and a quadrupole-derived Townes–Dailey ionicity of approximately 26%. High-level structures show the same directional response: O–H elongation, H···N contraction, and O···N contraction relative to HCOOH–NH3. Together, these results show that one water molecule can promote proton sharing in a neutral formic acid–ammonia complex without producing a separated ion pair.

title: A Multiscale Theoretical Framework of Piezocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical stimuli into chemical energy, holds significant promise for noninvasive medical therapies. In this process, ultrasonic frequency plays a dual role: it governs both the reaction rate and the electromechanical coupling efficiency, thereby serving as a critical bridge between microscopic and macroscopic physical processes. However, conventional theoretical models lack a multiscale description of coupled physical processes and thus fail to reveal how frequency dictates catalytic activity. Here, we develop an integrated multiscale framework that links, for the first time, macroscopic bubble cavitation dynamics, mesoscopic piezoelectric constitutive relations, and microscopic chemical reaction rate─with ultrasonic frequency as the unifying thread. Our model uncovers the complete frequency-dependent activity profile and elucidates the physical origin of an optimal frequency, predicting a volcano-shaped activity-frequency relationship that agrees well with a range of experimental reports. By reinterpreting piezocatalysis from a multiscale physical field perspective, this work establishes a new theoretical paradigm for the rational design of piezocatalysts.

title: An “Unachievable” Molecular Sieve with Sole Six-Membered Rings
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The frameworks of zeolite molecular sieves constructed from a sole type of ring, such as 6-membered rings (6MRs), are regarded as unachievable structures that would not even be found in hypothetical zeolite databases containing tens of millions of structures. Herein, we for the first time report a novel aluminophosphate ZJM-11 molecular sieve, with a fully 6-membered ring (6MR) framework, which was successfully obtained from topotactic transformation. The obtained structure, which possesses fully opened micropores, represents a rare case of a single-ring zeolite topology with an ultrahigh framework density, viewed from the perspective of conventional wisdom as an “unachievable” molecular sieve. Advanced characterizations unveil the dynamic framework reconstruction mediated by ZJM-9 and/or ZJM-10 intermediates, pinpointing this structural evolution as the essential step toward ZJM-11 formation. This work therefore delivers critical knowledge for the rational design of unconventional zeolite molecular sieves.

title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

title: Solvent-Dipole Deshielding of Hydrated Aluminum Lewis Acids for Enhanced 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Production from Biomass
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media. In water-rich AlCl3 solutions, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) exert dipole–dipole interactions with Al-coordinated water molecules through hydrogen bonding, distorting the [Al(H2O)6]3+ solvation shell and increasing access to the Lewis acidic Al center without directly coordinating to it. Spectroscopic measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal that weakening of the Al–O(water) interaction increases in the order of DMF < DMA < DMSO. This solvation-shell deshielding decreases the apparent activation energy for glucose-to-fructose isomerization from 96 to 79 kJ·mol–1 and enables an HMF yield of 90% from glucose at 150 °C. Glucose streams derived from sugarcane bagasse, poplar sawdust, and palm trunk sawdust afford HMF yields exceeding 80%, while the integrated sugarcane-bagasse route achieves a 49 mol % HMF yield based on the cellulose originally present in the biomass. These results establish dipolar cosolvent control of hydrated metal centers as a molecular design principle for homogeneous biomass conversion.

title: Cost effectiveness of synthetic fuel and CO2 removal for net-zero aviation
abstract: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. Comparing long-term costs of both approaches, we find DACCS is 49%–69% cheaper than synthetic fuels and needs far less renewable electricity, suggesting that current policy may be locking aviation into a costlier decarbonization path than necessary.

title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrate that the RNA sensor melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5) promotes immune evasion, and its high expression is strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity in preclinical models in female mice. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers unfolded protein response driven immunogenic cell death through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns, leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNF-α/IFN-γ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target.

title: Stabilization and Transformation of MXenes into Flexible and Thermal Oxidation-Resistant Non-van der Waals solids via Vapor-Phase Chemical Intercalation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) solids derived from MXenes exhibit attractive physical and chemical properties but are usually limited by the irreversible phase transformation of MXenes into rocksalt structures at high temperatures. Herein, we develop a vapor-phase chemical intercalation strategy mediated by high-vapor-pressure zinc (Zn) to efficiently stabilize the transition metals (Ti, Nb, and V) with unsaturated d-orbitals in MXenes. This stabilization facilitates subsequent interlayer bonding via reaction with various metal vapors (Al, Ga, and In) at elevated temperatures, yielding a family of well-defined non-vdW solids with ultrathin layered structures. Moreover, this strategy is readily scalable, enabling the fabrication of a continuous non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film featuring a heterogeneous architecture with a reconstructed MAX-like bonded region and a locally unbonded MXene region. These structural features endow the non-vdW Al–Ti3C2 film with exceptional mechanical flexibility, high-temperature oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air, and an electrical conductivity of ∼10 000 S cm–1. Consequently, the film demonstrates an electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness of up to 47.9 dB at a thickness of 5 μm, along with durable infrared stealth performance under prolonged exposure at 500 °C for 48 h.

title: Leveraging Cubenes to Access Highly Functionalized Fused Cubes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions. Further, experimental and computational studies for the generation and reactivity of unsubstituted cubene and new substituted cubenes are disclosed. These studies not only push the limits of strained intermediate chemistry but also provide an entryway to highly functionalized fused cubes, including new three-dimensional hybrid structures and other unprecedented chemical space.

title: Tailored ZnO/Cellulose Separator Reconfigures Solvation Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Magnesium metal batteries represent highly promising candidates for sustainable energy storage owing to their extremely high volumetric capacity (3833 mAh cm–3), abundant raw materials, and intrinsic safety. However, their practical viability is severely impeded by uneven Mg deposition, catastrophic interfacial side reactions, and continuous gassing behavior driven by uncontrolled electrolyte decomposition. Herein, we first report an inorganic inter-reinforced organic composite separator, fabricated by pairing cellulose with a zinc oxide (ZnO)-enhanced layer and designed to regulate the electrolyte solvation architecture by effectively anchoring solvent molecules. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that the electron-deficient Zn sites on ZnO enhance the solvent-capture ability of the polar hydroxyl groups on cellulose via bidirectional charge transfer. This interaction reconfigures the Mg2+ solvation sheath into a unique single-cluster structure, steering the formation of a dense, ultrathin, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that facilitates rapid Mg2+ desolvation while suppressing parasitic side reactions. Consequently, the as-assembled Mg||Mg symmetric cells deliver an exceptional cycling lifespan exceeding 2000 h with minimal overpotential and exhibit robust compatibility across diverse electrolyte systems. This inorganic inter-reinforced organic strategy for modulating solvation chemistry offers a generalizable avenue toward long-life and high-safety magnesium metal batteries.

title: Spin Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N2 Reduction on Chiral Mesostructured Bi2WO6
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

title: Designing dielectrics for microchip capacitors
abstract: The miniaturization of capacitors for advanced electronics requires dielectrics that balance high permittivity, low loss and stable temperature response. Now, a hierarchical machine learning approach is developed for the design of such materials. The resulting Bi–Ge co-substituted tungsten bronze ceramic exhibits balanced dielectric properties, enabling a substantial volume reduction of chip capacitors.

title: Dynamic Diels–Alder-Crosslinked Zwitterionic Polyurethane Coatings with Self-Healing, Antibacterial, and Antifouling Properties
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coatings used in marine and humid environments are simultaneously exposed to biofouling and mechanical damage, which progressively compromise their interfacial functionality and service stability. In this study, polyurethane resins bearing terminal maleimide groups and sulfobetaine moieties (ZPU-X) were synthesized and subsequently crosslinked with a tetrafunctional furan-terminated compound (TF) through reversible Diels–Alder (DA) reactions to produce dynamically DA-crosslinked zwitterionic polyurethane coatings (SA-X). The sulfobetaine groups promoted the formation of hydrated interfaces that reduced microorganism-coating interactions, achieving maximum antibacterial and antialgal rates of 96.7 and 99.7%, respectively, while effectively suppressing surface colonization by Aspergillus niger (A. niger). The reversible furan-maleimide crosslinks endowed the system with the capacity for segmental rearrangement and network reconstruction. After self-healing, the tensile strength and elongation at break of the coatings reached up to 25.69 ± 0.17 MPa and 1645.13 ± 54.27%, respectively. After 1000 Taber abrasion cycles, the coatings retained liquid-repellent behavior, demonstrating good surface functionality under wear. This work provides an effective strategy for developing functional polyurethane coatings that integrate antibacterial, antifouling, and self-healing properties.

title: PDEformer-2: a versatile foundation model for two-dimensional partial differential equations
abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) are fundamental to modeling physical systems. Traditional PDE solvers are often computationally expensive. Neural operators require independent training for different PDEs, and tend to be data-greedy when adapted to new scenarios. To this end, we introduce PDEformer-2, a versatile foundation model for solving diverse two-dimensional PDEs. The model receives the PDE form as input through a flexible computational graph representation and outputs solutions that can be queried at any spatio-temporal point. Pretrained on a 40 TB dataset spanning varied equation types, domains, boundary conditions, variable counts, and time dependence, PDEformer-2 enables instant zero-shot predictions for familiar PDEs and adapts faster to unseen ones than specialized baselines, achieving lower errors with limited samples. It also facilitates efficient inverse problem solving, successfully recovering unknown PDE parameters, including scalar coefficients and fields, in experiments.

title: Air-gap engineering enabled ultrafast 9-bit ferroelectric semi-gate transistor array for high-efficiency image denoising
abstract: The insufficient lateral electric field gradient limits the programming/erasing speed of conventional semi-floating gate transistors, while charge leakage leads to poor data retention and compromised operating characteristics. Here we design a ferroelectric semi-gate (FSG) transistor featuring a triangular air gap adjacent to the drain region. The device exhibits an as-programmed on–off ratio exceeding 107, remaining above 105 after 11 weeks, and a memory window of approximately 6 V. The localized lateral electric field accelerates program and erase operations to 60 ns and 75 ns, respectively. The spontaneous polarization field of the ferroelectric HfZrO layer strengthens charge retention in the HfO2 charge-trapping layer, enabling robust nonvolatile memory performance with a retention time exceeding 106 s. This synergistic integration of air-gap engineering and ferroelectric polarization yields an optimal trade-off between speed, retention and multilevel operation. By exploiting its superior multilevel capability with 9-bit distinguishable current states, we realize Ising-model-based image denoising using a 32 × 32 transistor array. These FSG transistors show promising potential for high-speed, low-power random-access memory applications.

title: Global hotspots and trends of ecological water scarcity in river basins
abstract: Healthy freshwater ecosystems are crucial for sustainable development, yet they face growing threats from unsustainable water use. However, current water scarcity metrics focus almost exclusively on human demand, overlooking whether sufficient water remains to sustain ecosystems. We address this gap by presenting the first evaluation of ecological water scarcity (EWS) across 1,182 river basins, introducing a novel indicator that recognizes ecosystems as legitimate water users to those of humans. Our findings reveal that in the 2000s, 412 basins (35% globally; 17% annual, 18% seasonal) experienced EWS, with affected areas expanding by 10 million km² since the 1950s. Human intervention intensified EWS in 13% of basins and caused 53% of seasonal and 60% of annual EWS cases. By the 2050s, affected basins range from 392 under RCP2.6–SSP1 to 416 under RCP8.5–SSP5, with persistent hotspots in regions of intensive water use. These findings show that climate mitigation can reduce future EWS risk, but environmental flow protection, water-use efficiency, water recycling, ecologically informed infrastructure operation and ecosystem restoration are also needed to safeguard freshwater ecosystems.

title: A Pathology-Responsive Hydrogel with On-Demand Ion Release for Microenvironment Remodeling and Diabetic Wound Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The healing of diabetic wounds is often impeded by severe bacterial infections, persistent inflammation, excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and abnormal matrix degradation. Although conventional free silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) possess broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, their inherent tendency to aggregate and inactivate, as well as its high cytotoxicity limits their clinical application. Moreover, a single bactericidal strategy is insufficient to completely reverse the complex pathogenic microenvironment of the wound. To address these challenges, this study developed a dual-polyphenol biomimetic extracellular matrix (ECM) composite hydrogel with matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) and pH-responsive properties, aimed at achieving spatiotemporal precision intervention and active microenvironment remodeling in diabetic wounds. This system employs caffeic acid-modified gelatin and dopamine-modified sodium alginate as a dynamically cross-linked scaffold, incorporated with AgNPs-anchored zinc–aluminum layered double hydroxide (ZnAl-LDH@Ag), that can precisely match the dynamic pathological evolution of the wound. The hydrogel exhibits pathology-adaptive behavior through two complementary mechanisms: gradual MMP-9-mediated remodeling of the gelatin network and infection-associated pH-responsive ion release. MMP-9-mediated degradation enables sustained exposure of ZnAl-LDH@Ag and prolonged matrix remodeling, whereas the acidic microenvironment promotes on-demand release of antibacterial Ag+ and regenerative Zn2+ ions. Additionally, polyphenol moieties provide antioxidant and anti-inflammatory regulation during wound healing. By integrating two-dimensional inorganic layered materials (ZnAl-LDH) with conventional metal nanocrystals (AgNPs), this strategy resolves the clinical paradox in silver-based therapies: the difficulty of balancing high bactericidal activity with low cytotoxicity. In summary, this pathology-driven therapeutic platform enables multimodal synergistic therapy for antioxidant protection, infection control, and tissue regeneration, providing a theoretical foundation and design perspectives for the development of advanced dressings for complex chronic wounds.

title: High-Fidelity Electrochemistry with Ultraclean Graphene Electrodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical performance of CVD graphene electrodes has remained inconsistent and often inferior to that of exfoliated graphene, limiting their utility in analytical applications. This variability is widely attributed to structural disorder, but the dominant source remains unclear. Here, we show that amorphous carbon contamination introduced during synthesis is the primary factor governing the electrochemical behavior of CVD graphene. By eliminating this disorder during growth through oxygen-free CVD (OF-CVD), we obtain graphene electrodes that exhibit intrinsic and highly reproducible electrochemical behavior. Compared with conventional and commercial graphene, these electrodes display substantially enhanced heterogeneous electron-transfer kinetics, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and improved detection limits across both outer- and inner-sphere redox systems. Notably, they exhibit consistent anodic peak potentials across wide concentration ranges, nearly eliminating the concentration-dependent potential shifts characteristic of both glassy carbon and commercial/contaminated graphene electrodes. Further, microelectrode array architectures fabricated from this material suppress non-Faradaic background currents and exhibit steady-state diffusion behavior consistent with electrochemical theory, with improved signal-to-noise ratios. Together, these results establish that extrinsic carbon disorder has limited the electrochemical performance of CVD graphene to date. The removal of amorphous carbon reveals defect-free graphene’s intrinsic electrochemical behavior and enables a reproducible, high-performance electrode platform, providing a clear pathway for reliable graphene-based electrochemical systems.

title: A Tumor-Activatable DNA Nanoengager That Orchestrates NK Receptor Clustering and Immune Checkpoint Blockage to Enhance Antitumor Cytotoxicity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager. This nanoplatform adopts a bilayered barrel architecture: the inner layer is functionalized with aNKp46, aPD-L1, and sialidase, while the outer layer is modified with the serum albumin-binding peptide ABD035 and a pH-sensitive i-motif switch. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, the DNA nanoengager undergoes specific dissociation of the outer protective layer, exposing the functional modules. These components concurrently bridge and activate NK cells, block the PD-L1 immune checkpoint, and specifically degrade tumor surface sialic acids, thereby reversing dual immunosuppression. This integrated DNA system enables synergistic integration of targeted activation, dual checkpoint blockade, and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, providing a novel smart nanoscale strategy to overcome multifaceted immune evasion in solid tumors and enhance the safety and efficacy of NK cell-based immunotherapy.

title: Rapid Joule-Heating Preparation of GO/GNs Graphene-Based Composite Films for Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional metal heat sinks are limited by moderate thermal conductivity, high density, and poor flexibility, which restrict their use in compact and lightweight electronics. Graphene films offer high in-plane thermal conductivity, but rapid reduction of graphene oxide (GO) releases gases from oxygen-containing groups and can generate pores, interlayer damage, and poor film densification. Here, we report a precursor-design strategy that combines reduced graphene oxide nanosheets (GNs) with carboxylated cellulose nanofibers (CNFs). The composite films (GO/GNs-X) were prepared by blade coating, hot-press carbonization, and secondary Joule-heating graphitization. The combined precursor was designed to mitigate gas-release-induced damage and support carbon-network reconstruction during high-temperature treatment. The optimized GF, with a thickness of approximately 25 μm, reached an in-plane thermal conductivity of 950.5 ± 20 W m–1 K–1 and an electrical conductivity of 2.31 × 105 S m–1. At a comparable thickness, this thermal conductivity was 26.6% higher than that of an additive-free RGO-2600-ref film prepared without GNs/CNF modification. In LED heat-dissipation tests, the surface-centre temperature decreased from 83.7 to 40.4 °C. Because individual-additive controls were not included, the respective contributions of GNs and CNF could not be separated. These results establish combined precursor modification as a route to thin, lightweight graphene heat spreaders. Such films may be useful for thermal management in compact electronics, foldable devices, and aerospace systems.

title: Topological Chemistry of PtPb4 Surfaces under Reconstruction and Hydrogen Adsorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Topological materials have recently been proposed as promising catalysts owing to the presence of robust topological surface states (TSSs). However, the microscopic role of TSSs in catalytic processes remains elusive. In particular, it is unclear how TSSs can simultaneously remain robust against chemical perturbations while actively participating in surface reactions. Here, we address this question through a combined study of the bulk topology, surface structure, and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) behavior of PtPb4, a valence analogue of a known topological catalyst PtSn4. We show that PtPb4 is a topological semimetal with non-trivial ℤ2 indices under spin-orbit coupling. This nontrivial band topology originates from a band inversion between two Pb-derived states near the Fermi level. Surface calculations reveal well-defined TSSs on the (100) surface, a surface that also exhibits potential HER properties. Hydrogen binding is primarily achieved by the deep H-1s/Pt-d bonding state located well below the Fermi level, while the TSSs play only a secondary, perturbative role in adsorption. By continuously tracking the evolution of the surface bands during adsorption, we demonstrate that the topological order is preserved despite substantial energy shifts, charge transfer, and hybridization in surface states. Our work provides a qualitative picture of how the TSSs of PtPb4 respond to hydrogen adsorption while the global topology of the surface remains inherently robust.

title: Environmental performance of energy consuming port activities based on a life cycle assessment
abstract: Fossil fuels are the primary energy source for logistical, energy intensive port operations, while being a major contributor to climate change, necessitating transition towards renewable and low emission energy sources. The issue is relevant given the expected growth in international maritime trade, resulting in increased port activities. This study uses life cycle assessment (LCA) to assess emission reduction potential in a Nordic container and cargo port when hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) and/or electricity is used instead of fossil fuels to power transportation, cargo handling equipment (CHE) and hoteling container vessels in the port. Additionally, the impact of replacing grid electricity and natural gas with on-site solar power (complemented with wind power from the grid) and biomethane in the port area is assessed. The novelty of the study lies in its comprehensive inclusion of port activities in the Nordic context and also includes CHE fleet production. Powering transportation and CHE fleet with HVO or grid electricity reduces port climate change impact (excluding biogenic emissions) nearly 60%. On-site photovoltaics and biomethane production, complementing needed electricity with wind power, and powering transport and cargo handling with HVO and electricity can result up to 78% reduction. Electrification demonstrated lower impacts compared to HVO scenario for climate change (incl. biogenic emissions), fine PM formation and terrestrial acidification impact categories. However, HVO outperforms electrification in eutrophication due to differences in equipment production. The findings indicate that electrification and HVO use enable significant emission reductions in the port and can be complemented by on-site energy production.

title: Flexibility technologies in clean energy systems
abstract: The transition to clean energy systems is increasing the need to balance variable supply and demand across timescales and sectors. This Review describes different technologies that can enable flexibility in energy systems and assesses trends in their global deployment.

title: BODIPY-Based Fluorescent Probes for Selected Hazardous Chemicals: Multilevel Regulation of Sensing Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid and reliable detection of hazardous chemicals in complex environments remains an important challenge in fluorescence sensing. BODIPY dyes and related boron-difluoride fluorophores have attracted considerable attention because of their excellent photophysical properties and highly tunable molecular structures. However, sensing performance depends not only on analyte recognition but also on excited-state processes, intermolecular interactions, aggregation behavior, analyte transport, and practical signal readout. This review examines BODIPY-based fluorescent sensing of selected hazardous chemicals at the molecular level, supramolecular and aggregated-state level, and sensing material and device level, focusing on how regulation at different levels addresses different performance limitations. At the molecular level, recognition unit design, conformational regulation, and boron-center transformation regulate analyte recognition and signal transduction. At the supramolecular and aggregated-state level, noncovalent interactions, aggregation-state regulation, and molecular packing influence emission behavior and signal stability. At the sensing material and device level, interfacial and transport regulation, sensing material construction, and device integration and signal readout improve analyte accessibility and practical detection performance. This review provides a systematic framework for understanding the factors that govern BODIPY-based fluorescence sensing. This multilevel classification facilitates the identification of major factors limiting sensing performance and the corresponding regulation strategies, thereby providing guidance for the rational design and optimization of BODIPY-based fluorescent sensing systems.

abstract: Concerns about privacy, reproducibility and cost are prompting scientists to use models on their computers rather than in the cloud.

title: A comprehensive review on accurate numerical simulation of proton exchange membrane fuel cell
abstract: PEMFCs involve strongly coupled electrochemical reactions and transport processes of gas, water, charge, and heat. Numerical simulation is therefore an important tool for understanding internal transport phenomena, predicting performance, and supporting PEMFC design and operation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative PEMFC numerical-simulation studies identified primarily through topic-specific manual searches of the Web of Science database. While many earlier reviews focus on individual processes, components, scales, or modeling routes, the present review connects numerical models from the MEA to macro-scale and multi-scale single-cell models, stack models, operational-process models, system temperature-control models, and efficient-study models based on artificial intelligence and similarity theory. The principal modeling approaches are compared in terms of their physical descriptions, applicable scales, computational costs, validation approaches, and suitable applications. The review shows multi-physics and multiscale models are essential for resolving coupled internal processes, but their effectiveness is constrained by uncertain transport and kinetic parameters, coupling methodology between scales, limited validation data for local physical fields, and high computational cost for large stacks. AI-assisted and reduced-order approaches can improve computational efficiency, but their prediction capability and applicable scale require further development. The review provides a structured summary and outlooks for selecting and improving PEMFC numerical models.

title: Does the decline of book reading mark the end of rational thinking?
abstract: Smartphones and artificial intelligence are undermining our ability to follow a complex argument, with grave consequences.

title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. Using the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset, we examine how plant invasions influence multi-scale stability of total community abundance (used total community cover) via altering community functional diversity, as well as growth and dispersal strategies. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities.

title: The VPS33B-VPS16B protein complex facilitates Golgi ribbon formation and Golgi-endosome trafficking
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Loss of expression of VIPAS39/VPS16B or the Sec1/Munc18 (SM) family protein VPS33B causes early lethal ARC syndrome in humans. These proteins have been shown to form a complex containing 2 opposed VPS33B molecules known as VPS33B-VPS16B. ARC patient-derived fibroblasts have dispersed Golgi elements and absence of ribbons, an abnormality also observed in VPS16B-knockout HEK293 cells. These observations indicate that VPS33B-VPS16B is involved in Golgi formation/stability. Immunofluorescence microscopy studies showed colocalization of VPS33B-VPS16B with several Golgi-associated proteins, and co-immunoprecipitation studies indicated interactions involving the Golgi tethering factor GRASP55/GORASP2. Interactions were also detected involving VPS33B-VPS16B and VPS51 and VPS53, components of the Golgi-associated retrograde protein (GARP) and endosome-associated recycling protein (EARP) complexes. Abnormalities were observed in retrograde trafficking of mannose-6-phosphate receptors, and of cathepsin B between Golgi and endosomes in VPS33B-VPS16B deficient cells, along with abnormally large late endosomes/lysosomes. These observations suggest that VPS33B-VPS16B has previously unreported roles in key aspects of Golgi apparatus formation/stability, Golgi-endosome trafficking, and perhaps lysosome dynamics.

title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks.

title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls (Tyto alba) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

title: Metabolite-mediated reversal of motor hyperactivity restores ciliary function
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hyperactive missense mutations can produce phenotypes that are difficult to predict from sequence alone. Here, we dissect such a discrepancy in Caenorhabditis elegans, where the kinesin mutant osm-3(A340V) shortens sensory cilia despite exhibiting elevated in vitro motility. A forward genetic screen identified osm-7, a hypodermal secreted protein, whose loss restored ciliary architecture by elevating intracellular glycerol over 100-fold. Glycerol supplementation alone recapitulated this rescue, re-establishing intraflagellar transport in neurons and modulating OSM-3(A340V) motility in vitro. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that A340V restricts neck-helix relaxation, a defect reversed by glycerol-induced conformational tuning. Our study indicates that impairment of neck-helix flexibility leads to kinesin hyperactivity in vitro and motility defects in vivo, and that metabolite-mediated conformational tuning represents a mechanism for reversing such motor defects.

title: KMT2B facilitates long-range gene regulation through LINE1 elements
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transcriptional regulation is tightly linked to chromatin organization, with H3K4me3 marking active and bivalent promoters. In embryonic stem cells, KMT2B deposits H3K4me3 at bivalent promoters, yet loss of H3K4me3 at these sites leaves developmental gene transcription largely unaltered. Here, we show that, in both mouse embryonic stem cells and during differentiation, the primary role of KMT2B is not to counteract Polycomb-mediated repression at bivalent promoters. Instead, we uncover a distinct regulatory function for KMT2B at the CG-rich 5’UTR of young LINE-1 elements. KMT2B binds LINE-1 5’UTRs and maintains their active chromatin state (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H4K16ac) while preventing repressive H3K9me3 accumulation. Using complementary genomic methods and targeted deletions, we show that KMT2B-bound LINE-1 elements act as enhancers modulating neighboring gene expression in embryonic stem cells and, particularly, during differentiation. Our findings define KMT2B regulatory functions at LINE-1 repeats and highlight transposable elements as key components of long-range gene expression control.

title: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-molecule techniques provide exceptional resolution of biomolecular dynamics but are limited by low throughput. Here, we present a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel kinetic profiling of multiple protein variants in a single experiment. Each protein is covalently linked to a unique DNA barcode, decoded through transient hybridisation of fluorescent probes distinguished by colour and binding duration. Applied to a library of 16 ClpS variants, this approach revealed ~5-fold variation in dissociation kinetics and uncovered previously unrecognised bimodal binding behaviour arising from distinct structural subpopulations. By enabling scalable, multiplexed functional characterisation at the single-molecule level, this platform provides a general framework for protein engineering, directed evolution and the development of next-generation single-molecule technologies.

title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria
abstract: Defense-associated reverse transcriptases (DRTs) employ diverse and distinctive mechanisms of cDNA synthesis to protect bacteria against viral infection1. However, the functions and mechanisms of many DRTs remain unknown2. Here we identify a new antiviral defense system, DRT10, that associates with a noncoding RNA (ncRNA) to catalyze processive, protein-primed synthesis of tandem-repeat DNA. Reverse transcription is templated by a defined ncRNA region with a characteristic sequence pattern and template boundary elements, both of which are conserved and essential for DNA repeat addition. Cryo-EM reconstructions reveal an unanticipated 2:1 architecture, wherein two RT monomers bind opposite sides of a pseudo-symmetric ncRNA. Biochemical experiments further demonstrate that each RT monomer reverse transcribes the template encoded on its respective side of the ncRNA, but only one generates the long repetitive product, whose template is defined by the distance between two flanking stem-loop anchors. This mode of iterative, boundary-delimited cDNA synthesis exhibits direct parallels to the mechanism of telomeric repeat addition by eukaryotic telomerase, and phylogenetic analyses of RTs across domains of life place telomerase in a monophyletic clade with the DRT family, suggesting a common origin for their DNA polymerization activities. Together with earlier studies of DRT2, DRT3, and DRT93–5, our findings identify a conserved mechanistic logic underlying RNA-templated DNA repeat addition across diverse DRTs, despite vastly different architectural solutions, and expand the repertoire of reverse transcription-based strategies for antiviral immunity in bacteria.

title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

title: Tracing missing copper: ultrapotassic rocks record isotopic evidence of crustal Cu depletion
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Post-subduction reactivation of metasomatized lithospheric mantle generates high-K shoshonitic magmas in the continental crust and has been suggested to be potentially associated with porphyry Cu mineralization, yet its role in the continental crustal Cu budget remains ambiguous. Here, we use Cu isotope analyses and geochemical modeling of Cenozoic ultrapotassic rocks from southern Tibet to show that variations in Th/La record a transition from mantle partial melting to magmatic differentiation, during which Cu behavior was controlled by sulfide retention in the source and fluid activity, respectively. During partial lithospheric mantle melting, residual solid sulfide phases retain Cu in the mantle source, generating Cu-depleted melts with slightly heavier δ⁶⁵Cu and potentially contributing to the Cu depletion of continental crust. Subsequently, exsolved fluids preferentially scavenge isotopically heavy Cu, causing both Cu contents and δ⁶⁵Cu values to decrease in the residual magmas. The Cu isotopic evolution of these ultrapotassic magmas differs from that of ore-bearing porphyries in the belt, potentially reflecting differences in magma source or evolutionary history.

title: Hysteresis of extreme precipitation in East Asia under various CO2 removal pathways
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO2 removal scenarios remains limited. Focusing on East Asia, a region highly vulnerable to monsoonal dynamics and anthropogenic influences, here we assess the hysteresis of extreme precipitation responses under four CO2 concentration thresholds and two emission reduction rates using climate model simulations. The extreme precipitation indices based on intensity and frequency exhibit an increase during the CO2 peak, but fail to fully return to their initial states even after CO2 levels decline to their initial levels. This hysteresis behavior is amplified by delayed and slower emission reductions. The hysteresis is linked to increases in mean monsoon precipitation associated with hysteresis in tropical Pacific warming patterns and subsequent atmospheric teleconnections. Moisture budget analysis further indicates that enhanced precipitation is attributed to increased moisture transport into East Asia, driven by early-summer rises in specific humidity (thermodynamic factor) through mean circulation and late-summer intensification of monsoon circulation (dynamic factor). These findings reveal the mechanisms shaping East Asian extreme precipitation under different carbon removal pathways and highlight the critical role of both timing and pace of emission reductions in determining regional climate outcomes.

title: Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI-, B(C2O4)2-, or BF4-) for 1700 nm excitation PAI.
