Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

title: DigiDent: integrated bristle-level sensing and AI for contact-aware toothbrushing assessment
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing, the most common preventive practice, remains largely unguided and unquantified, contributing to the global burden of oral diseases. Current smart toothbrush systems fundamentally fail to capture the critical fine-scale biomechanics at the bristle-tooth interface, which is essential for evaluating clinical adherence and preventing gingival damage. Here we present DigiDent, an AI powered sensing to interpretation system that renders brushing micro-biomechanics computationally interpretable by measuring in-situ contact dynamics at bristle-tooth interface with an embedded E-Bristle sensor. DigiDent fuses bristle-level contact sensing with inertial sensing through a dual-stream neural inference architecture, converting contact-rich brushing behavior into quantitative and interpretable metrics of force, duration, contact-motion pattern, and fine-grained coverage. In validation experiments, DigiDent achieved >99% recognition of motion-contact patterns and 99.84% classification accuracy across 21 brushing subregions. Pilot user-operation verification further demonstrates the feasibility of DigiDent for real-use brushing monitoring and quantitative feedback. These results establish embedded co-deformation sensing and AI-based interpretation as a technical foundation for future personalized toothbrushing assessment and coaching.

title: Deep profiling of lysine methylation by covalent enrichment-enhanced proteomics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lysine methylation is a classic posttranslational modification, yet most studies focus on histone methylation. Although emerging evidence demonstrates the significance of nonhistone lysine methylation, current approaches that investigate individual proteins of interest are relatively low throughput. Proteomics provides an ideal strategy for comprehensively studying cellular posttranslational modifications, but current enrichment methods typically allow the identification of only a few hundred methyllysine sites because of insufficient enrichment efficiency for low-abundance methyllysine-containing tryptic peptides. Here we report a comprehensive lysine methylation profiling method based on covalent enrichment-enhanced quantitative proteomics, termed DEKmeP. In practice, DEKmeP enables systematic nomination of candidate substrates and their monomethylation sites regulated by lysine methyltransferases. Through subsequent biochemical and cellular experiments, we validate dozens of nonhistone substrates of lysine methyltransferases. Moreover, we characterize the functional effects of SMYD2-mediated c-Jun K288 methylation. Therefore, DEKmeP may shift lysine methylation studies from the investigation of individual proteins of interest to systematic exploration of the methyllysine proteome, thereby expanding the understanding of lysine methyltransferase catalysis and nonhistone lysine methylation.

title: Anomalous spin–lattice coupling in a 2D antiferromagnetic semiconductor revealed by surface acoustic Rayleigh waves
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils.

title: Exocomets in a planet nursery
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Evidence for exocomets has been found in PDS 70, a young planetary system where planets are still forming. The discovery extends exocomet studies into an earlier stage of planetary evolution, when planets, planetesimals and protoplanetary discs coexist.

title: Global rise of a wheat pathogen through two-stage evolutionary emergence coupled with aerial dispersal
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rise of plant pathogens following crop domestication and their subsequent global spread pose persistent threats to food security, yet the mechanisms underlying host jumps and rapid adaptation in obligate biotrophs remain unclear. Using 319 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst) genomes and virulence phenotypes of 234 isolates across six continents, we construct its origin and global dissemination. Our analyses support a two-stage emergence model: P. striiformis sensu stricto originated and diversified in the Himalayan region, subsequently a P. striiformis s. str. lineage jumped to domesticated wheat in the Fertile Crescent, giving rise to epidemic lineage (Pst) and spreading worldwide with wheat cultivation. This host jump triggered demographic expansion and selective sweeps, while GWAS identified region-specific virulence loci shaped by resistant cultivars. Overlay of air trajectory and dispersal simulations identified atmospheric corridors consistent with genomic migration patterns, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport in the pathogen’s global spread.

title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages adopt suppressive states, but how tumor stress installs these programs remains unclear. Here, we identify syndecan-3 (SDC3) as a macrophage-intrinsic mechanosensory regulator by integrating in vivo functional screening, single-cell and spatial profiling, and genetic and pharmacological perturbation. SDC3+ macrophages accumulate in hypoxic, stiff tumor niches and suppress antitumor cytotoxic T-cell responses. Matrix stiffness increases mechanical loading on SDC3, reorganizes an SDC3-associated scaffold and opens suppressive chromatin loci. This program engages a CDK7–MAFB relay to induce TREM2, which functions as a required suppressive effector in mice. Human-cell assays support a species-specific TREM2-associated inhibition mechanism. Naldemedine engages TREM2, restores cytotoxic T-cell activity, improves tumor control and enhances immune-checkpoint blockade in vivo. These findings define a targetable SDC3–CDK7–MAFB–TREM2 axis linking hypoxia and tissue mechanics to macrophage-mediated immune evasion.

title: Applications of Single-Atom Alloys in Thermal, Electro, and Photo Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.

title: Nonaqueous Redox Flow Batteries: Opportunities and Challenges for Sustainable Energy Storage
abstract: Abstract Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.

title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c + ), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c + . Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

title: Grid integration of bidirectional dynamic wireless charging for electric vehicles: A review on grid-side challenges and opportunities
abstract: Dynamic Wireless Charging (DWC) enables electric vehicles to charge while in motion, alleviating range anxiety and reducing the need for large onboard batteries. Bidirectional Dynamic Wireless Charging (BDWC) extends this concept by allowing moving vehicles to both draw energy from and return energy to the grid, positioning them as mobile distributed energy storage resources. Realising this potential requires a thorough understanding of the grid-side impacts that arise when vehicle mobility, bidirectional power flow, and traffic randomness interact on distribution networks. Existing reviews have addressed wireless power transfer hardware, grid impacts of unidirectional charging, or bidirectional converter design as separate topics, but none has examined how these aspects interact under bidirectional dynamic conditions. To fill this gap, this paper presents a structured review of the relevant literature, organised around four research questions spanning unidirectional DWC grid impacts, static wireless vehicle-to-grid technology, the challenges specific to bidirectional dynamic operation, and the modelling gaps that remain. By bringing together perspectives from power electronics, power systems, and transportation engineering, the review reveals that while unidirectional grid impacts and static bidirectional power transfer are individually well characterised, their combination under dynamic conditions has not been quantified. Major conclusions are therefore classified by evidence level to separate demonstrated findings from projections that still require validation. Practical implications for distribution network planning and regulatory adaptation are discussed, three primary research gaps are identified, and an analytical framework linking traffic variability, grid impact assessment, and ancillary service provision is proposed to guide future research.

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

title: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Influenza inflicts substantial burden of disease, but current vaccines have limited breadth of protection against strains and subtypes not in the vaccine. BPL-1357, a whole-virus, inactivated vaccine containing four wild-type, low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses has demonstrated remarkable protection in animal models against a wide range of influenza viruses. In this phase I trial, forty-five healthy participants were randomized to receive BPL-1357 intramuscularly (IM), intranasally (IN), or placebo, in a prime and boost strategy, 28-days apart. The primary endpoints consisted of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) from enrollment through 28 days after the boost. The secondary endpoints were AEs and SAEs through 182 days after the boost and measurement of serum IgG and nasal IgA titers against hemagglutinin and neuraminidase vaccine antigens. Adverse effects were mostly mild and, other than mild injection-site pain more frequently observed in the IM group, occurred in a minority of patients. IM BPL-1357 induced higher serum IgG titers against H3, H5, and H7 relative to placebo, with 71.4%, 71.4%, and 85.7% of participants demonstrating a response. IM BPL-1357 vaccinated participants also experienced serum neutralizing and NA-specific responses, but no mucosal IgA responses against HA or NA. Subtle mucosal and serum responses were observed after IN vaccination, similar to preclinical experiments. These results suggest that BPL-1357 is well tolerated and immunogenic, particularly when given IM, but more work is needed to assess other dose levels, further characterize induced immunity, and evaluate efficacy against influenza infection and disease (NCT05027932).

title: Advances in self-reconstructing stainless-steel electrocatalysts for water splitting: surface activation, alloy engineering, stability, and DFT insights
abstract: Stainless steel (SS) is emerging as a promising, earth-abundant platform for replacing precious-metal and pure-Ni electrodes in water electrolysis. Yet, it is still often treated as inert hardware rather than an active catalyst. Under HER/OER conditions, however, the classical Cr-rich passive film on Fe-Cr-Ni alloy SS is driven beyond its stability window. It can reconstruct into porous, Ni/Fe-rich (oxy)hydroxide layers that provide genuine catalytic activity while remaining anchored to a robust metallic backbone. This review consolidates evidence on how such self-reconstruction can be intentionally controlled and engineered to convert commercial SS into efficient, durable electrodes for overall water splitting. We first summarize the evolution of SS from a structural material to a self-reconstructing electrocatalyst, and critically discuss surface-activation strategies, including electrochemical activation (potential cycling, anodization, and cathodization), thermal oxidation, and hydrothermal/corrosion-engineering routes that drive Cr depletion and Ni/Fe enrichment. We then introduce the Ni-Fe-Cr-X reservoir concept to bridge the gap between traditional corrosion science and modern electrocatalysis, rationalizing how bulk alloy composition and microstructure govern reconstruction behavior, secondary passivation, and stability across alkaline and chloride-containing environments. Emphasis is placed on long-term durability, including self-replenishing Ni-rich electrodes that operate at ampere-level current densities, and on the limited but growing density functional theory (DFT) literature that links passive-film chemistry and electronic structure to HER/OER mechanisms. Finally, we outline key research directions, including multi-scale operando characterization, composition-designed SS, and specific DFT/ML frameworks needed to move from empirical activation toward rational, mechanism-guided design of SS-based electrocatalysts.

title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Protein palmitoylation covalently attaches the energy metabolite palmitate to target proteins, yet how it is regulated by nutrient status remains elusive. Here, we identify the palmitoyltransferase DHHC12 as a critical nutrient-responsive switch, coupling amino acid availability to insulin secretion. Amino acid deficiency activates the kinase GCN2, which phosphorylates COPA at Thr777, enabling its function as an adaptor for the CRL4 E3 ligase complex and leading to ubiquitination of DHHC12 on two critical cysteine residues (Cys127 and Cys133, with Cys127 within the catalytic DHHC motif) and its subsequent degradation. In male mice, loss of Dhhc12 impairs insulin secretion and causes glucose intolerance. DHHC12 palmitoylates SYT7 to promote glucose-stimulated insulin exocytosis. The physiological relevance of this pathway is underscored by two human DHHC12 variants: the hypoglycemia-associated L196P mutant evades degradation, whereas the hyperglycemia-linked N238I mutant is constitutively degraded. Together, our findings establish the GCN2-COPA-DHHC12 axis as a direct nutrient-sensing mechanism that couples amino acid availability to systemic glucose homeostasis.

title: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Genome stability is essential for cellular viability yet constantly threatened by DNA-damaging agents. Among these, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are particularly harmful and in S/G2 phases are faithfully repaired through homologous recombination (HR). The RAD51 recombinase forms nucleoprotein filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that performs critical functions in HR. The efficiency of HR depends on precise regulation of RAD51 filament dynamics by accessory factors, including RAD54B, a double-strand DNA-dependent ATPase. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays, we show that RAD54B stabilizes RAD51–DNA filaments, inhibits RAD51 ATPase activity, and promotes D-loop formation and strand exchange. RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β-domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B’s ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells. Our findings uncover a modular architecture and mechanistic framework for RAD54B’s critical role in genome maintenance.

title: More-efficient water splitting utilizing heated-cooled active pure water with reduced hydrogen bonds
abstract: Within the realm of renewable energy technologies—particularly those centered on hydrogen evolution reactions (HERs) and oxygen evolution reactions (OERs)—noble metals have long been regarded as the archetypal catalytic materials. In recent years, however, research efforts have pivoted toward earth-abundant, cost-effective catalysts featuring diverse compositional and structural motifs. A seminal development occurred in 2014 with the introduction of plasmon-activated water (PAW), an innovative system engineered through hot electron transfer (HET) from gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In this review based on our published papers, we put forward an alternative paradigm aimed at enhancing HER and OER efficiencies by redirecting the focus onto water itself—specifically, a condensed water derived from Au-free processing of heated PAW containing trace amounts of Au. Relative to active PAW, this condensed form exhibits a diminished electron-doping character alongside more-pronounced disruption of hydrogen-bonding networks. Notably, its emergent properties are critically governed by the heating rate applied during PAW boiling. Analogous behaviors were observed in cooled active water, where the cooling rate during post-boiling treatment of deionized water (DIW) played a similarly decisive role. Remarkably, when employed in HER and OER applications, the heated-cooled active pure water—whether derived from PAW or DIW—consistently outperformed pristine DIW, a fact attributable to its distinctive features: reduced hydrogen-bond connectivity and a modified electron-doping state. Moreover, the latter property conferred upon the prepared active water a pronounced capacity for scavenging 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) free radicals. Even after several days of aging, both the unique physicochemical characteristics and the corresponding electrochemical activities showed only marginal attenuation, underscoring its viability for real-world deployment. Collectively, our findings establish this stable active water as a promising green solvent platform capable of enabling more-efficient HERs and OERs in electrochemical systems.

title: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Investigation of crosstalk between antagonistic pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines has focused on mechanisms and functional consequences of cross-inhibition. Here, we investigate cross-regulation between proinflammatory tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and anti-inflammatory interleukin-4 (IL-4) in primary human monocytes and in a skin wound-healing model. Surprisingly, TNF functioned mainly as a costimulator of IL-4-induced gene expression, whereas IL-4 selectively inhibited the TNF-induced IFN response, leaving inflammatory gene expression mostly intact. TNF and IL-4 synergistically induced gene sets that are important in the regulation of inflammation and tissue repair, which were highly induced during the phase of wound healing when these cytokines are co-expressed. Crosstalk between TNF and IL-4 was mediated by epigenetic chromatin-mediated mechanisms associated with cooperation between NF-κB and STAT6 transcription factors, erasure of negative histone mark H3K27me3, and selective inhibition of IRF1. These results identify a mechanism for expansion of the IL-4 response and highlight the complexity of crosstalk between antagonistic cytokines, including cooperation for select gene responses that are important for immune responses and tissue repair.

title: Computational design of water splitting electrocatalysts: From d-band center to machine learning descriptors
abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is critical for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its commercial viability is limited by the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions (HER and OER). Computational chemistry has accelerated catalyst discovery through predictive activity descriptors. However, early descriptors are predominantly single-valued and static, built upon idealized models that omit dynamic surface reconstruction, electrolyte effects, and the coupling between multiple reaction pathways. These oversimplifications impair their capacity to break intrinsic scaling relationships and capture operando conditions, which has motivated a paradigm shift toward multidimensional, time-resolved frameworks. This review tracks the evolution of descriptors, from conventional volcano plots to machine learning-driven dynamic descriptors, and elaborates on how modern approaches capture structural evolution under operating potentials, bypass scaling constraints, and align theoretical model systems with realistic solid-liquid interfaces. Finally, we discuss prospective research directions, highlighting the integration of high-precision dynamic modeling, multi-objective optimization (which balances activity, stability, and mass transport), and closed-loop automated platforms to facilitate the on-demand design of robust electrocatalysts for industrial applications.

title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

title: Addressing the Zinc Corrosion Conundrum: The Vital Role of Resting-State Kinetics
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have emerged as a highly desirable system for grid storage applications due to low-cost, high-energy density, and safe operating conditions. While AZMB studies often focus on functional mitigation of dendrite formation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), corrosion remains a more ambiguous yet crucial limiting factor in anode performance. Specifically, recent work points to persistent chemical corrosion as a major source of resting capacity loss in AZMBs. In this work, we present a wide-ranging mechanism for galvanic corrosion based on fundamental electrochemical thermodynamics and kinetics, highlighting the key roles of battery components, electrolyte conditions, and other contributing factors. Importantly, this mechanistic framework also applies when plating and stripping Zn on the anode, offering additional insight into the ever-elusive mechanistic origins of HER during those operating regimes. We then propose several promising avenues of inquiry and methods for further predicting, understanding, and mitigating corrosion in AZMBs.

title: Metal-Dependent Magnetic Exchange Topology as a Fingerprint of N2 Binding in Isostructural MOF Nodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triangular metal-oxo nodes are widely employed as catalytic motifs in metal–organic frameworks. Photocatalytic N2 fixation using the all-iron nodes can be switched off by replacing them with all-chromium nodes. However, the two nodes bind N2 in the opposite order to their activity. The present contribution shows that the electronic structure of the metal, which governs the small-molecule binding to the framework, determines the magnetic exchange topology of the [MIII3(μ3-O)] node. Combining broken-symmetry and non-collinear DFT, Hamiltonian-based reconstruction of Mössbauer spectra, and quantitative modeling of temperature-dependent magnetic susceptibility, one finds that FeIII exhibits a genuinely frustrated triangle of comparable antiferromagnetic interactions, whereas CrIII features an asymmetric dimer-plus-monomer governed by unusually strong biquadratic interaction, placing it outside the conventional Heisenberg regime. The distinct electronic structure is reflected in markedly different magnetic topologies and N2 binding strengths, rationalizing the contrasting photocatalytic activities of the two frameworks. These results establish magnetic exchange topology as an experimentally accessible descriptor of chemical function in trinuclear MOF nodes.

title: A comprehensive review of machine learning in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells: From materials to intelligent systems
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is rapidly transforming proton-exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) science by enabling advances across materials design, multiscale modeling, diagnostics, and intelligent control. Persistent barriers to widespread PEMFC deployment—including high cost, limited durability, and complex multiscale transport phenomena—arise from nonlinear interactions that conventional modeling and experimentation struggle to resolve. This review presents a comprehensive synthesis of ML approaches tailored to the PEMFC value chain, showing how numerical, experimental, imaging, and hybrid datasets support surrogate models that reduce Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) computational costs by orders of magnitude while maintaining physical consistency through physics-informed and multi-fidelity learning. ML-guided optimization accelerates the rational design of catalyst layers, membranes, gas-diffusion media, and bipolar plates, uncovering non-intuitive structure–property relationships. Deep-learning-based diagnostics and hybrid residual frameworks significantly improve fault detection, state-of-health estimation, and remaining-useful-life prediction. At the system scale, ML-enhanced model predictive control and deep reinforcement learning enable adaptive, autonomous operation under dynamic conditions, while emerging digital-twin architectures integrate physics-based solvers with real-time data assimilation to deliver predictive, self-correcting fuel-cell management. By unifying methodological advances, cross-scale opportunities, and critical challenges, this review establishes ML as a foundational enabler for the next generation of high-performance, durable, and economically viable PEMFC technologies.

title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD.

title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNAIle complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

title: Optimal inertia allocation in networked DC microgrids with guaranteed steady-state and small-signal stability
abstract: DC microgrids (MGs) are considered an efficient solution for integrating distributed energy sources. In these networks during dynamic power imbalances, the stored energy in the capacitor of DC bus provides the natural tendency to resist voltage changes, equivalent to the physical inertia of rotating machines to resist frequency changes in AC networks. However, the limited capacitance of the DC bus leads to an intrinsic low-inertia, which threatens the voltage security under frequent disturbances. Although inertia emulation strategies have been developed in DC grids to mitigate the above, there is a lack of virtual inertia allocation method for complex networked DC MGs, resulting in a potential system instability and undesired costs. To address this gap, a steady-transient-coordinated bi-stage optimization framework is proposed to enhance the grid performance during different periods. To guarantee the steady state operational requirements of DC MGs, a mixed-integer conic programming is developed in the first stage to design the damping constant, providing equilibrium points for small-signal modelling. On this basis, an ℋ 2 -index-based stability-constrained optimal inertia allocation model is established to enhance global voltage dynamics under disturbances. To capture the implicit feature of the stability constraints, a data-driven method is employed to learn and reformulate the model in a tractable mixed-integer linear manner. Case studies on a 9-bus DC-powered trolleybus system, a 14-bus radial DC microgrid and a 30-bus network are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Architecting Anode Current Collectors for Practical Anode-Free Alkali Metal Batteries
abstract: Anode-free alkali metal batteries (AFAMBs) are emerging as a compelling strategy to surpass the cell-level energy density limits of Li-ion batteries while simplifying battery configuration. In these systems, the working anode forms in situ on a bare current collector and is continuously reshaped during cycling with a limited alkali metal inventory. As a result, the anode current collector is not merely a passive electron conductor, but a multifunctional interfacial platform that governs alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution. This review examines the fundamental differences among anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium systems and highlights key performance metrics for practical AFAMBs. Recent current collector engineering strategies developed for these chemistries are then summarized. Essential parameters shaping current collector design are identified, including electronic conductivity, alkali metal affinity, collector morphology, and interphase stability. Finally, practical design principles are presented to balance electrochemical performance with manufacturability under realistic operating conditions. This review aims to clarify the alkali metal-dependent design logic of current collectors and to provide guidance for the practical development of next-generation anode-free batteries. Highlights:1 A systematic comparison of anode-free lithium, sodium, and potassium battery systems, emphasizing their distinct energy density, volume change, and interfacial instability.2 A current-collector-centered analysis of anode-free alkali metal batteries, highlighting how current collectors govern alkali metal nucleation, growth, stripping, and interphase evolution under limited alkali metal inventory.3 A practical framework for the development of anode-free alkali metal batteries, integrating performance metrics, current collector design parameters, and manufacturability constraints.

title: Sparse Electromagnetic-Compatibility Flexible Electrodes for High-Accuracy, Fast-Recognition Human–Computer Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface electromyography (sEMG) gesture recognition technology offers significant potential for enhancing human-computer interaction and rehabilitation engineering by providing an intuitive and noninvasive method of engagement. However, challenges such as electromagnetic interference (EMI), signal feature processing, and adaptability to individual variability remain prevalent. To address these issues, this paper presents a comprehensive framework that encompasses material selection, device design, feature selection algorithms, integration strategies, and system layout to create a skin-integrated electronic system functioning as a wireless control interface between humans and machines. This system features a flexible electrode that incorporates fractal design elements, serpentine structures, honeycomb configurations, and multilayer graphene, along with an efficient feature selection algorithm grounded in data dispersion principles. It is characterized by enhanced resistance to EMI, conformal attachment capabilities, rapid motion recognition, and high accuracy. Our work stands out with a dramatically higher shielding efficiency of 99.98% and a classification accuracy rate of 97.8%. This methodology significantly enhances the performance of sEMG-based human-computer interfaces, emphasizing rapid recognition speeds and high accuracy in real-time applications such as remote-control systems and virtual reality environments, thereby broadening its applicability across diverse contexts.

title: Gate-Programmable Spectral Plasticity in Nanoporous Vertical Organic Synaptic Transistors for Adaptive Neuromorphic Vision
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial vision systems capable of dynamically adapting to changing spectral environments are essential for next-generation intelligent perception but remain fundamentally constrained by the fixed spectral responsivity of conventional photodetectors. While narrowband photodetectors effectively suppress optical background interference, their spectral selectivity is generally predetermined by material composition or device geometry, preventing adaptive spectral perception within a single hardware platform. Here, we report a nanoporous vertical organic synaptic transistor based on a highly diluted P3HT:PC61BM (100:1) blend that enables gate-programmable spectral plasticity, allowing reversible electrical switching between wavelength-selective narrowband detection and broadband panchromatic perception. Unlike conventional planar phototransistors, the vertically configured transport architecture spatially decouples optical absorption from electrostatic channel modulation, thereby overcoming the long-standing incompatibility between the thick photoactive layers (1.5 μm) required for charge-collection narrowing and the ultrathin semiconductor channels necessary for efficient gate control. By electrically reshaping the interfacial energy landscape and carrier collection length, gate modulation dynamically regulates the extraction of photogenerated carriers across different penetration depths, producing adaptive spectral responses without altering either the material composition or device structure. Quantitatively, the device achieves a competitive R of 41.7 A/W, a shot-noise-limited D* of 2.7 × 1013 Jones, and an EQE of 8.3 × 103%. Beyond spectral reconfigurability, the thick active layer naturally introduces persistent photoconductivity arising from trap-mediated carrier relaxation, enabling biologically analogous excitatory postsynaptic current generation together with paired-pulse facilitation (reaching an index of 290%), spike-number-, spike-duration-, and spike-intensity-dependent plasticity, as well as programmable transitions from short-term to long-term plasticity. These multidimensional synaptic dynamics provide intrinsic temporal information processing directly at the sensor level, eliminating the need for separate sensing and memory units. Furthermore, experimentally acquired synaptic conductance characteristics are integrated into convolutional neural networks through a hardware–algorithm codesign strategy to emulate adaptive retinal signal preprocessing. System-level simulations demonstrate that electrically programmable spectral weighting significantly improves both broadband image recognition and monochromatic color discrimination by dynamically matching spectral perception to different visual tasks. This work establishes a general strategy for integrating adaptive spectral sensing, electrically programmable phototransistors, and neuromorphic information processing within a unified vertical organic transistor architecture, providing a versatile materials platform for intelligent optoelectronic systems.

title: Ultrahigh-speed chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Despite these advancements, the imaging capability of time-resolved SS-FPP is still limited by the flexibility and speed of both pattern projection and image acquisition, as well as by the duration of the observation time window. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara’s fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. These results highlight C-BLIP’s promise for continuous-streaming, ultrahigh-speed 3D metrology in industrial inspection, bionics, and data security.

title: Coupling the Spin State Switching and CO2 Adsorption Operating at Different Temperatures in a Breathing Metal–Organic Framework
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Gas-responsive magnetic response arising from spin-crossover (SCO) phenomena is rare yet highly attractive for molecular sensing and spintronics. However, it remains unclear how gas uptake influences SCO behaviour when the two phenomena occur in separate temperature regimes. Herein, we report a strong influence of CO2 adsorption on the SCO behaviour of a Hofmann clathrate, [FeII(epac)2(PtII(CN)4)]·nEtOH (1·nEtOH, n ≤ 2), despite the two effects occurring at different temperatures. Complex (1·2EtOH) exhibits highly cooperative SCO with a hysteresis width ∼65 K and preserves the framework topology upon desolvation (1). However, hysteresis reduces to 30 K in the guest-free phase (1), underscoring the critical role of lattice solvent in mediating cooperativity. Complex (1) selectively adsorbs CO2 through a gate-opening mechanism at temperatures substantially higher than the SCO region. Despite this mismatch in operating temperatures, increasing CO2 loading progressively stabilizes the low-spin state and shifts the transition temperature (Teq) by ∼20 K. These findings support a delayed guest-mediated coupling mechanism where CO2 first enters the framework at elevated temperatures and subsequently modifies spin-state energetics only after immobilization within the host lattice at lower temperatures. This study establishes that gas adsorption and SCO need not occur within overlapping temperatures to remain strongly coupled.

title: Spray-Freezing-Engineered Cuttlebone Architectures Enable Multiscale Mechanical Reinforcement in Graphene–Cellulose Aerogels
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Graphene–cellulose aerogels offer lightweight and multifunctional platforms, yet their limited mechanical robustness restricts practical deployment. Herein, we report a bioinspired strategy that integrates novel spray-freezing fabrication with a cuttlebone-mimetic wall–septa architecture to achieve multiscale mechanical reinforcement in graphene–cellulose aerogels. The spray-freezing method allows for scalable production, and the resulting aerogels exhibit an ultralow density of 0.077 g/cm3 while achieving a specific strength of 14.80 kN m/kg and specific modulus of 4.51 kN m/kg at 80% compressive strain, corresponding to 4.95 and 4.96 times those of conventional freeze-dried counterparts. Multiscale simulations reveal that the enhancement arises from two primary mechanisms. At the nanoscale, borax-mediated crosslinking enhances cellulose network integrity, while the bending and load redistribution of graphene nanosheets introduce additional energy dissipation pathways within the lamellar framework. At the mesoscale, horizontal septa in the structure effectively relieve stress concentration during high strain compression. The synergistic coupling of molecular reinforcement and architectural stress redistribution establishes a structure-property paradigm for mechanically resilient cellular nanocomposites. This work provides mechanistic insights into bioinspired multiscale reinforcement and offers a scalable platform for engineering high-performance, lightweight graphene-based aerogels, which is expected to be applied in the thermal and fire prevention fields.

title: Multivariate Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework Derived Hollow NiCo2O4 for Selective Alkene Oxidation by Oxygen Vacancy Engineering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective oxidation of alkene to valuable chemical feedstocks is challenging due to the seesaw effect between conversion and selectivity. Here, multivariate zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) are transformed into bimetallic oxides with varied morphologies via tannic acid (TA) etching and calcination. Impressively, TA etching results in the formation of oxygen vacancies and pore expansion, and the hollow architecture is generated after pyrolysis, favoring the exposure of more active sites and rapid mass diffusion, as well as inducing prominent void-confinement effects. Besides, the incorporation of nickel ions can introduce an additional type of Lewis acid sites into the resulting bimetallic oxides. The obtained Co3Ni1-TA1.4-10-400 exhibits an effective styrene-to-benzaldehyde oxidation with nearly total conversion and a 99% yield (5 h, 90 °C), approximately 1.9 and 8.3 times higher than those of Co3Ni1-TA1.4-10 (51%) and Co3Ni1-O (12%), respectively. Mechanistic investigations for the conversion of styrene to benzaldehyde further indicate that the reaction possibly proceeds via a synergistic mechanism involving both a metal-peroxide pathway and a free-radical pathway. Furthermore, in the presence of sodium bicarbonate, Co3Ni1-TA1.4-10-400 can prove effective in catalytic epoxidation of styrene. This study provides a valid approach for the construction of ZIF derivatives with abundant oxygen vacancies and unsaturated metal sites as promising catalysts for fine and commodity chemical production.

title: Bioengineered Hybrid Nanovesicles Modulate the Immune Microenvironment with Targeted Drug Delivery for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Combining chemotherapy and immunotherapy shows great promise for treating esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but its effectiveness is hindered by the immunosuppressive tumor environment and challenges in drug delivery. Recent research has focused on cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for targeted drug delivery, leveraging their ability to evade the immune system while selectively targeting tumor cells. In this study, we developed a biomimetic hybrid nanoplatform based on cell membranes to combine molecular chemotherapy and improve the effectiveness of immunochemotherapy in treating ESCC. The nanoplatform is coated with a membrane fusion of activated neutrophils and ESCC cells and loaded with paclitaxel (PTX) and small interfering RNA targeting EFNA1 (siEFNA1), a molecule linked to ESCC metastasis. By exploiting the homologous targeting properties of ESCC cell membranes and the tumor-homing ability of neutrophil membranes, the platform effectively targets ESCC tissues and delivers siEFNA1 and PTX. This allows for a synergistic treatment approach, combining EFNA1 gene silencing with PTX-induced cytotoxicity to target ESCC more effectively. Crucially, the nanoplatform reprograms tumor-associated macrophages from the pro-tumor M2 phenotype to the anti-tumor M1 phenotype while boosting T cell-mediated cytotoxicity and remodeling the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Overall, this strategy presents a promising approach for the targeted treatment of ESCC.

title: Phenolic Additive-Doped Cathode Interlayer for High-Efficiency Organic Photovoltaics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The cathode interlayer (CIL) is crucial for the development of organic photovoltaics (OPVs). However, the widespread use of CILs based on perylene diimide and naphthalene diimide is constrained by their strong intrinsic aggregation tendency. Herein, benzoic acid (BA) and its derivatives bearing different quantities of hydroxyl groups (BA-OH, BA-2OH, and BA-3OH) are used as additives to modify NDI-Ph, a naphthalene diimide-based cathode interlayer. Systematic studies reveal that the dipole moment of additives rises with the increasing number of hydroxyl groups, which further facilitates intermolecular interactions with interfacial materials. Benefiting from the enhanced electrical conductivity, optimized interfacial contact, and suppressed charge recombination, the NDI-Ph modified by BA-3OH delivers a champion efficiency of 19.20% in D18:L8-BO-based devices, exceeding the 18.25% efficiency of the control device. Furthermore, with 2PACz as the hole transport layer, the device achieves a high PCE of 20.09%. This strategy has also been proven effective for PDINN- and PNDIT-F3N-based CILs. This work verifies that modulating the number of hydroxyl groups in benzoic acid derivatives can rationally regulate the performance of CILs and prescribes a facile and effective strategy to develop high-efficiency OPVs.

title: Broadband Electro-Thermal Full-Space Modulation in Freeform VO2 Metagrating in the Telecom Band
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrically tunable metasurfaces for free-space light modulation have been widely studied, with VO2-based phase-change metasurfaces standing out for their large, broadband material tunability and reliable electrical modulation. However, simultaneously modulating both transmitted and reflected beams across a broad bandwidth is a multi-objective problem that is difficult to satisfy with intuitive metasurface designs built on one or a few eigenmodes, calling for complex multimode structures accessible only through inverse design. Here, we demonstrate broadband electro-thermal modulation of both reflected and transmitted beams in an adjoint-optimized freeform Au–VO2 metasurface on sapphire, operating as an amplitude modulator across the telecom bands (1200–1600 nm), with the Au layer serving as both electrode and plasmonic field concentrator. Measurements reproduce the simulated complementary switching of the two channels, yielding band-averaged modulation depths of ∼0.4 (transmittance) and ∼0.7 (reflectance) and optical efficiencies of ∼0.18 (transmittance) and ∼0.15 (reflectance) for y-polarized incidence. A coupled Bloch mode analysis then uncovers how the optimizer meets these competing objectives, the origins of the polarization selectivity, and the broadband nature of the switching. This work establishes adjoint optimization combined with multi-mode analysis as a framework for VO2-based active metasurfaces, opening a route toward compact full-space light modulators for optical communications, interconnects, and free-space optical computing in the telecom bands.

title: A Carboxymethyl Cellulose Hydrogel Switch Enabling pH-Responsive Fertilizer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Green Revolution boosted crop yields with synthetic fertilizers, but their high solubility causes environmental pollution and poor synchronization with crop nutrient demands. To address this problem, we developed green intelligent fertilizers (GIF) using a pH-responsive material to enable root-fertilizer feedback. An ultra-sensitive and biodegradable pH-responsive material (pH-B) was synthesized by coordinating carboxymethyl cellulose with Ca2+ and cross-linking, with H+ sensitivity at 10–4 mol L–1. We then constructed a smart release system by embedding this pH-B switch into a 5% polyurethane coating to encapsulate diammonium phosphate (DAP) granules. In this design, the polyurethane matrix impedes the contact between DAP granules and soil water and thus minimizes phosphorus solubilization, leaching, and fixation, while the pH-B switch acts as an acidity-activated gatekeeper whose shrinking enables water penetration through the coating material. In acidic soil, the shoot P content of faba bean increased significantly (by 37–61%) in the treatment with pH-responsive fertilizer compared with DAP. Consequently, in calcareous soils, these fertilizers release nutrients specifically in response to rhizosphere acidification caused by proton exudation from phosphorus-deficient plant roots. This mechanism precisely synchronizes nutrient supply with crop demand. Our work provides a novel strategy for enhancing nutrient-use efficiency and promoting sustainable agriculture.

title: Nanostructured Quercetin-Lipid Carrier on 3D Printed Scaffolds for Improved Bone Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Musculoskeletal defects remain difficult to treat because current grafts often have limited supply, donor-site morbidity, risk of immune reaction, or insufficient local biological stimulation. To address this problem, this study developed 3D-printed β-tricalcium phosphate (TCP) scaffolds loaded with quercetin-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (Que-NLCs) to combine an osteoconductive ceramic structure with local delivery of a natural osteogenic and anti-resorptive compound. Que-NLCs provided controlled release for up to 21 days and reduced the initial burst release compared with free Que at both pH 5.0 and 7.4. At pH 5.0, release was ∼40% for Que and ∼33% for Que-NLCs, while at pH 7.4, release was ∼32% for Que and ∼26% for Que-NLCs. In vitro studies showed that Que-NLC-loaded scaffolds increased osteoblast viability by ∼28.6%, increased alkaline phosphatase activity by 33% by day 11, and reduced osteoclastic activity by 56% by day 21. RT-qPCR further showed up to 4-fold increases in osteogenic markers and up to 60% reduction in osteoclastogenesis-related genes. In a 6-week rat distal femur model, Que-NLC scaffolds increased new bone formation by ∼1.9-fold compared with TCP. These results show that Que-NLC-TCP scaffolds provide a localized, controlled drug-delivery platform to improve bone regeneration in non-load-bearing defects.

title: Photo-/Electrothermally Gated Slippery-Pore Surface for All-Weather Anti-/De-icing and Meltwater Drainage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Icing threatens the safe operation of aircraft, power facilities, wind turbine blades, and other engineering surfaces. Although existing superhydrophobic, photothermal, electrothermal, and drainage surfaces can individually delay freezing, actively melt ice, or transport liquids, most of them are static designs and therefore cannot simultaneously meet the conflicting requirements of water-repellent anti-icing before freezing and rapid drainage after ice melting. Here, we propose a slippery-pore-based photo–electro dual-mode gated anti-/de-icing surface, termed the porous epoxy actuated electrothermal superhydrophobic (PEAES) surface. In the closed state, the surface maintains superhydrophobic anti-icing properties. Under photothermal or electrothermal stimulation, the PI/graphene scales undergo thermally induced bending and expose the underlying slippery pores, enabling low-residue meltwater drainage. When the pores are blocked by ice, the embedded multiwalled carbon nanotube electrothermal layer can further restore the drainage pathway. The PEAES scales achieved reversible opening within 11 s under 1 sun irradiation and within 8 s under a 5 V electrothermal input. At –10 and –20 °C, PEAES exhibited prolonged freezing delay and a low ice adhesion strength of approximately 6 kPa. Under photothermal, electrothermal, and photo–electro synergistic modes, ice melting was completed within 11, 6, and 3 s, respectively. More importantly, PEAES reduced the residual meltwater after ice melting to nearly zero and decreased the secondary icing area ratio to 0%. This work coordinates anti-icing, de-icing, drainage, and recovery through gated state switching, providing a new structural strategy for adaptive anti-/de-icing and meltwater management across multiple energy-input conditions and successive icing stages.

title: Interfacial Cofactor Recycling Electroenzymatic Platform for Endergonic CO2 Reduction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract To overcome the thermodynamic barrier of “NADH-dependent CO2 reduction”, we developed a bioelectrosynthesis platform via the co-immobilization of CO2 reductase (CR) and diaphorase (DP) on a graphite electrode. A strategic protein engineering approach, utilizing carbon-specific solid-binding peptides (SBPs), enabled oriented enzyme assembly to facilitate efficient interfacial electron transfer. Among the variants, the dual-functionalized system—comprising C-terminal SBP-fused CR and N-terminal ferredoxin (Fd)/SBP-fused DP3—exhibited superior bioelectrocatalytic synergy, achieving a current density of –193.35 µA cm–2. At –0.5 V (vs Ag/AgCl), this integrated interface effectively drove the endergonic reduction process, maintaining continuous cofactor regeneration with an electron transfer efficiency of 39.2%.

title: Resolving the LiFePO4 Battery State beyond Voltage-Based Diagnostics Using Surface-Scan MRI
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Reliable assessment of state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH) in commercial batteries remains a major challenge because their closed architecture obscures the underlying electrochemical, structural, and thermal processes, while existing diagnostic methods often provide only indirect, spatially averaged, voltage-based information about battery operation and degradation. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) is among the most widely deployed cathode materials due to its low cost, long cycle life, and high thermal stability; however, its characteristically flat voltage profile fundamentally limits the information content of conventional diagnostics. In this work, we exploit the large magnetic-susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases and the lithiation-dependent evolution of their phase fractions for accurate and time-efficient determination of SoC in commercial pouch cells and battery packs. Surface-scan magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides new SoC and SoH metrics through quantitative inside-out measurements of battery-induced magnetic field perturbations. LFP is a cathode material particularly well suited to this approach because its biphasic FP/LFP regime spans a large fraction of the usable SoC window while generating substantial magnetic susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases. Under the biphasic approximation, the average magnetic susceptibility follows the lever rule, predicting a linear relationship between the induced magnetic field offset and SoC. Surface-scan MRI experiments confirm this prediction over a broad SoC range. We further establish a framework for spatial mapping of SoC and SoH heterogeneity in multi-cell architectures representative of practical battery packs. Despite minimal voltage differences between cells, the method enables quantitative visualization of charge imbalance and structural heterogeneity on the timescale of seconds.

title: Trace Bifunctional Diboron Additive Enables Robust CEI/SEI Interphases for Long-Cycling 4.5 V Li||NCM811 Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing efficient, low-cost, multifunctional additives that require small amounts and can simultaneously protect both the cathode and anode remains a major challenge for the practical application of lithium batteries. Herein, bis(2,4-dimethylpentane-2,4-glycolato)diboron (B2hmp2) was introduced to construct a greatly Li+-conductive cathode electrolyte interphases (CEIs) at the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) surface together with robust solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Using a common electrolyte with 0.2 wt % B2hmp2, the Li||Li cells deliver markedly enhanced long-cycling stability, sustaining stable operation for 500 h at 0.5 mA cm–2. Furthermore, following 350 cycles at 0.5 C, the capacity retention of 4.5 V Li||NCM811 cells was elevated from 57.2 to 83.6%. Experimental results reveal that the thin, uniform, boron-rich CEI generated by B2hmp2 effectively mitigates particle microcracking and restrains the dissolution of transition metal ions. Interface analysis reveals that the modified SEI film enriched with B–O species and LiF facilitates uniform Li plating/stripping without dendrite formation and reduces the continuous parasitic decomposition of electrolyte solvents. This article highlights the value of trace diboron for forming desirable electrolyte interphases to obtain the wonderful long-term cycle performance and rate performance of Li||NCM811 cells.

title: Defect Engineering in β -Ga2O3 Schottky Barrier Diodes via Proton Irradiation and Subsequent Low-Temperature Supercritical Fluid Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a defect engineering strategy that combines low-fluence proton irradiation for leakage current (Jr) suppression and subsequent low-temperature supercritical fluid (SCF) treatment for forward conduction characteristic restoration in β-Ga2O3 Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) with and without NiO guard rings. Mechanistically, the results reveal that proton irradiation and subsequent SCF treatment are not the inverse of each other, as the former primarily introduces gallium vacancies (VGa), whereas the latter mainly passivates oxygen vacancies (VO). On the one hand, for proton irradiation, the introduction of VGa reduces the net carrier concentration (ND – NA), leading to a significant decrease in Jr, accompanied by an increase in specific on-resistance (Ron,sp). On the other hand, for subsequent SCF treatment, the passivation of VO effectively enhances electron mobility rather than substantially restoring ND – NA, thereby maintaining Jr at the irradiated level and considerably reducing Ron,sp. Consequently, through the above defect modulation in bulk β-Ga2O3, SBDs simultaneously achieve a decrease in Jr from 1.16 × 10–5 to 2.01 × 10–8 A·cm–2 at –200 V, a moderate increase in Ron,sp relative to their unirradiated counterparts, and a higher on/off current ratio from 2.28 × 107 to 5.69 × 109 at –200 V. Furthermore, this strategy substantially diminishes the effectiveness of the NiO guard ring in reducing Jr. These findings highlight the potential of this defect engineering as an effective strategy for fabricating high-performance β-Ga2O3 SBDs.
