title: The honey bee stinger: An unusual pump with collapsible double pistons
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Most stinging animals deliver venom by contracting muscles around a venom reservoir, but honey bees employ a fundamentally different strategy. The stingers of worker bees have the unique ability to autotomize, separating from the body, to continue to sting independently. Despite more than a century of anatomical descriptions, the mechanics of venom pumping have remained unresolved due to the challenges of observing them in action. We recorded high-speed videos of active, autotomized stingers, combined with micro computed tomography-based three-dimensional reconstruction to characterize the biomechanics of stinging in the honey bee
                    Apis mellifera
                    . We reveal that the stinger functions as a unique double-piston micro-pump. Two lancets, each possessing a deformable valve, slide in antiphase within a bulb chamber. These valves dynamically deform to alternately form a seal during the downstroke and collapse during the upstroke, enabling pressure generation for pumping while potentially minimizing backflow during refilling. The inverted tear-drop shape of the bulb facilitates refill even while pumping proceeds. We explored valve deformations and flow behavior by constructing a dynamically scaled physical model of the bulb chamber confirming key features of the pumping cycle and propose mechanisms for valve deformations. The double piston design adds significant design complexity but enables continuous venom delivery in a compact, autonomous unit. These findings provide deeper understanding of venom pumping in honey bees and other Hymenoptera. This study also provides evidence of an axial piston pump within a biological system and offers inspiration for the design of microfluidic pumping devices.

title: AI-generated language remains systematically distinguishable from human communication
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in the social sciences to simulate human behavior and communication, yet validation methods for these applications remain limited. Existing evaluations often rely on human judgments of plausibility, a coarse, difficult-to-scale, and often unreliable benchmark for distinguishing AI-generated from human text. As a result, researchers lack robust tools for assessing the realism of LLM-generated language and for calibrating models to real-world data. We address this gap in two ways. First, we introduce the Conversational Human Authenticity Test (CHAT), a validation framework that combines aggregate metrics of detectability and semantic similarity with interpretable linguistic features, including stylistic markers and topical patterns, to assess how closely LLMs approximate human language in a given dataset. Second, we benchmark nine open-weight LLMs across five calibration strategies, including fine-tuning, stylistic prompting, and context retrieval, on user interactions from X, Bluesky, and Reddit. We find that even after calibration, LLM outputs remain clearly distinguishable from human text, especially in affective tone and emotional expression. Instruction-tuned models generally underperform base models, and larger models do not obviously improve human-likeness. We also identify a trade-off between realism and semantic fidelity: methods that make outputs seem more human often move them further from the content of human responses. Together, these results provide a scalable framework for validation and calibration in LLM-based social simulation while underscoring current limits in reproducing human communication.

title: Interfacial microenvironments enable abiotic ribonucleoside formation in micro- and nanoscale compartments
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The abiotic emergence of ribonucleosides remains a central challenge in origin-of-life research because ribonucleosides form inefficiently and are often unstable under prebiotically plausible conditions. Here we show that interfacial microenvironments within aqueous micro- and nanoscale compartments containing D-ribose, phosphoric acid, and nucleobases promote ribonucleoside formation by creating reaction-permissive physicochemical conditions independent of the specific compartment type. Across a diverse range of compartmentalized systems, including gas–oil–water micro/nanobubbles, gas–water micro/nanobubbles, microscale lipid-bilayer vesicles, and oil–water emulsion systems, ribonucleosides form abiotically in the absence of enzymatic catalysis. Under selected interfacial conditions, multiple ribonucleosides, including cytidine, are generated without added catalysts. Comparison among these systems reveals that interfacial architecture and coupled physicochemical properties strongly influence both reaction efficiency and product stability. CO
                    2
                    -based micro/nanobubbles support sustained cytidine accumulation, highlighting the importance of coupled gas–liquid and liquid–liquid interfaces. Ribonucleoside synthesis also depends on compartment size, whereas variations in oil content within micro/nanobubbles selectively modulate inosine formation, underscoring the sensitivity of nucleoside chemistry to interfacial properties. These findings identify interfacial microenvironments within micro- and nanoscale compartments as a general physical framework for ribonucleoside emergence and suggest that ubiquitous compartmentalized interfaces on early Earth could have provided robust settings for prebiotic ribonucleoside chemistry.

title: Antiferromagnetism and tightly bound Cooper pairs induced by kinetic frustration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Antiferromagnetism and superconductivity are often viewed as competing orders in correlated electron systems. Here, we demonstrate that kinetic frustration in hole motion facilitates their coexistence within the square-lattice repulsive Hubbard model. Combining exact analytical solutions on tailored geometries with large-scale numerical simulations, we reveal a robust pairing mechanism: Holes on opposite sublattices behave as if they carry opposite effective charges due to spin singlet formation from kinetic frustration. This emergent property suppresses phase separation and fosters a coherent
                    
                      
                        d
                      
                    
                    -wave superconducting channel embedded within a long-range antiferromagnetic background. Our findings establish a minimal yet broadly applicable framework for stabilizing strong-coupling superconductivity in doped Mott insulators.

title: Molecular Architecture of Non‑Fullerene Acceptors Balances Homo‐ and Hetero‐Intermolecular Interactions to Enhance Thermal Stability of Organic Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐efficiency organic solar cells require optimal donor‐acceptor heterojunctions to facilitate efficient charge generation, separation, and collection. These bulk‐heterojunction (BHJ) blends are typically kinetically quenched in nonequilibrium morphologies, contributing to device degradation over time. Yet how acceptor molecules govern homo‐ and hetero‐intermolecular interactions to confer thermal stability to BHJ blends remains elusive. Herein, we present experimental and theoretical studies of 28 distinct non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) to elucidate the relationships between molecular structure, intermolecular interaction, and morphological stability of BHJ blends, covering the well‐known indacenodithieno[3,2‐ b ]thiophene‐based (ITIC‐series) acceptors, indacenodithiophene‐based (IEICO‐series) acceptors, and state‐of‐the‐art Y‐series and dimer/trimer acceptors. We demonstrate that structural modifications of NFAs not only modulate the homo‐interaction energies between acceptor molecules but also fine‐tune their hetero‐interaction energies with donors, thereby governing the stability of BHJ nanostructures. Thermally stable BHJ blends necessitate strong homo‐interactions while minimizing hetero‐interactions to suppress NFA diffusion within the blends. The proposed intermolecular interaction effect on thermal stability is further validated by 13 literature‐reported NFA blends, demonstrating the broad applicability. These findings underscore the pivotal role of NFA structural engineering in regulating intermolecular interactions and offer valuable insights into balancing homo‐ and hetero‐interactions for the rational molecular design of thermally stable organic semiconductor blends.

title: Gravity‐Differential Modulated Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Continuous and Stable Energy Harvesting From Disordered Vibrations
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐frequency, random, and intermittent vibrational energy is an important energy source for self‐powered sensing systems in engineering environments. However, the high dependence of triboelectric nanogenerators on periodic excitation limits their continuous energy output. Here, a gravity‐differential modulated triboelectric nanogenerator (GDM‐TENG) is proposed to transform intermittent vibrations into a continuously enhanced energy conversion process. Through the synergistic effect of mechanical rectification, inertial energy storage, gravity‐driven propulsion, and differential motion amplification, the GDM‐TENG directionally transmits and delays the release of discrete vibrational inputs, thereby forming a more continuous and higher‐frequency relative sliding motion at the triboelectric interface and improving the effective charge transfer rate per unit time. Compared to the single pendulum system, the double‐sided pendulum shortens the energy storage time by 64.2%, compressing the energy response to the millisecond level, while increasing output power by 2.81 times and capacitor charging rate by 2.55 times. After 216,000 cycles, the voltage output of the GDM‐TENG remains almost unchanged, indicating its excellent long‐term operational stability. Furthermore, combined with a power management circuit, the GDM‐TENG can stably charge a 1000 µF capacitor and power warning lights and acoustic flame sensors. This work provides a design idea for distributed self‐powered sensing systems toward the infrastructure monitoring.

title: Photoelectrochemical Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion: Cocatalyst Design Principles and Mechanistic Insights from Electrocatalysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO 3 RR) offers a solar‐driven route to NH 3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value‐added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO 3 RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO 3 RR research has produced an extensive library of high‐performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO 3 RR, spanning light‐absorber engineering, photoelectrode–cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO 3 RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge‐transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH 3 synthesis.

title: Spatially Decoupled Cascade Oxygen Reduction on Bi Single‐Atom and Cluster‐Hybrid Sites for Hydroxyl Radical Generation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) for H 2 O 2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O 2 activation and H 2 O 2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade‐off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand‐exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal–organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co‐anchored on B‐doped TiO 2 . The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H 2 O 2 ‐to‐·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free‐energy diagrams indicate that H 2 O 2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p‐band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h −1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3–9). Moreover, it enables broad‐spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow‐cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid interfaces.

title: Dual‐Encrypted Ultraviolet Optical Communication Driven by Opto‐Piezoelectric Coupling in Two‐Dimensional Flexible Ferroelectric Single‐Crystalline Thin‐Films
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high‐security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual‐wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software‐based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware‐level security. Herein, we report a dual‐encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system based on BA 2 EA 2 Pb 3 Br 10 ( 1 , where BA is n‐butylamine and EA is ethylamine) ferroelectric single‐crystalline thin‐films (SCFs). The 1 ferroelectric SCFs show a photoresponsivity that reaches 230% of the original level under +1.13% tensile strain. Notably, we innovatively define the strain‐ratio key (ε 1 /ε 2 , ε 2 /ε 3 , ε 3 /ε 4 ) induced by distinct bending states as the intrinsic unclonable hardware secret key, and construct a 4‐bit combined coding scheme based on four distinguishable photocurrent levels modulated by these strain ratios to realize secure transmission of the message “FJIRSM.” This strain ratio‐based system avoids complex optical modulation, ensuring ultrahigh security, and expands the application of two‐dimensional ferroelectrics in advanced encrypted optoelectronics.

title: Time‐Resolved Physically Unclonable Functions Enabled by Solvent‐Free Scalable Boron‐Based Ultralong Phosphorescent Systems for Machine‐Learning‐Resilient Optical Encryption
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Anti‐counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time‐resolved physically unclonable function (TR‐PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high‐dimensional temporal encoding. Central to this approach, boron‐based room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials are developed via covalent coupling with coumarin derivatives using a solvent‐free strategy that is readily scalable to kilogram‐level production, exhibiting a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of over 2 s, an ultralong afterglow visible for up to 30 s, and color‐tunable emission. The formation of rigid B‐O‐C linkages spatially isolates emissive centers, suppressing energy transfer and preserving temporally independent decay channels–an essential prerequisite for high‐entropy time‐resolved encoding. Randomly embedding these multi‐emissive RTP units into a polymer matrix forms a complex encryption structure that enables a dual‐entropy encoding mechanism with both spectral and temporal dimensions, generating dynamic time keys for authentication. Moreover, we propose a matched time‐gated authentication framework that achieves >99% identification accuracy within 1.2 s while exhibiting resistance against the tested generative machine‐learning attacks. This work proposes a practical materials platform and a time‐gated authentication strategy, offering a scalable technological path for the development of dynamic optical encryption tags.

title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

title: Integrated Electromicrobial Production of Itaconic Acid From CO2 at Liter‐Scale Using Komagataella phaffii
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling electrochemical CO 2 reduction showing high selectivity with microbial biosynthesis offering metabolic versatility offers a promising strategy for converting CO 2 into value‐added products. We present proof‐of‐concept of electromicrobially producing the platform chemical itaconic acid (IA) from CO 2 using a robust yeast chassis. The hybrid systems integrates in a single reactor electrochemical CO 2 reduction with microbial synthesis using a synthetic autotrophic Komagataella phaffii strain. Thereby CO 2 serves as carbon source while electrochemically generated formate from CO 2 provides reducing power to sustain microbial growth and drive IA production, reaching average titres of 110.1 mg·L −1 . While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO 2 conversion using industrial yeast and highlight critical parameters for process intensification.

title: Unlocking the Interfacial Activity of Insoluble Lithium Salts for Stable Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li + sites directly onto an aramid‐scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution–diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li + solvation and enhanced anion‐derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6 Li/ 7 Li isotope tracing identify Li 2 SO 4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP‐LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP‐LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO 4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll‐to‐roll manufacturing across diverse Ah‐level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m −2 . This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries.

title: Strain‐Controlled Pt Single‐Atom Catalysts on Crumpled MXene Supports for Highly Active Hydrogen Evolution
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Strain engineering offers a powerful means to regulate the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of active metal sites, yet a general framework linking strain to electrocatalytic performance remains elusive beyond the conventional d‐band model. Here we report crumpled double‐transition‐metal MXene nanosheets (Mo 2 TiC 2 T x ) decorated with Pt single atoms, in which a tunable strain field is introduced through a physical diaphragm balloon method. The resulting cMo 2 TiC 2 T x ‐Pt SA catalyst exhibits outstanding alkaline hydrogen evolution performance, requiring overpotentials of only 24.9 and 75.5 mV to reach 10 and 50 mA cm −2 , respectively, together with a mass activity of 11 859 mA mgPt −1 , around 178‐fold higher than commercial Pt/C, a Tafel slope of 31.61 mV dec −1 and excellent durability. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations show that the ordered long‐range strain field around isolated Pt sites accelerates interfacial water activation while preserving near‐optimal H adsorption, thereby facilitating H 2 release. The resulting catalyst delivered a high current density of 3 A cm −2 at a low voltage of 1.98 V and maintained stable operation at 1000 mA cm −2 for over 500 h. These performance metrics underscore the potential of cMo 2 TiC 2 T x ‐Pt SA for industrial applications.

title: Nickel‐Free Perovskite Solar Cells Enabled by Self‐Assembled Monolayers: A Pathway to Efficient and Recyclable Devices
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High efficiency inverted perovskite solar cells often rely on nickel‐containing hole‐selective interfaces such as NiOx. However, the use of nickel presents sustainability challenges, as the material is inherently toxic and cross‐contamination during end‐of‐life processing can compromise material recovery and recyclability. Here, we develop a nickel‐free hole‐selective interface material based on phenyl‐substituted phosphonic‐acid carbazole self‐assembled monolayers (Ph‐nPACz). Candidate molecules were identified through rational structure‐property screening of the substituents of the carbazole core, anchoring groups and linkers. Among this molecular family, Ph‐5PACz delivers the best overall performance, offering improved interfacial wettability and enhanced buried‐interface stability compared to the NiOx/Me‐4PACz reference. Devices incorporating Ph‐5PACz achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.3%, compared to 21.7% for the control, driven by a higher fill factor and efficient charge extraction. The chemical robustness of the nickel‐free interface enables a closed‐loop recycling route unavailable to nickel‐based devices, with recycled‐ITO devices retaining close to 98% of their initial performance. Coupled life‐cycle and techno‐economic analyses further indicate substantial sustainability gains, including reduced energy demand, markedly lower raw metal usage and toxicity‐related impacts, and a generalized reduction of up to 29% across ReCiPe endpoint indicators.

title: Jahn–Teller Distortion of MnO6 Octahedra Enhances Piezoelectric Polarization and Lattice Oxygen Activation of BaTiO3 for Efficient Piezo‐PEC Water Splitting
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Piezo‐photoelectrochemical (Piezo‐PEC) water splitting enables efficient solar conversion, yet its practical implementation is limited by an insufficient piezoelectric polarization field and sluggish water‐splitting kinetics. Herein, we firstly propose a Jahn–Teller effect‐driven strategy to regulate the local B‐site octahedral structure of perovskite BaTiO 3 for efficient Piezo‐PEC water splitting. By introducing Mn 3+ ions with asymmetric e g orbital occupancy (t 2g 3 e g 1 ), a local MnO 6 octahedral coordination environment is constructed and pronounced Jahn–Teller distortion is induced. Experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Jahn–Teller distortion drives the cooperative displacement of Ti and O atoms and enhances crystal non‐centrosymmetry, thereby generating a stronger piezoelectric polarization field under mechanical stress. Meanwhile, the introduction of Mn 3+ strengthens Ti─O bond covalency, thereby activating lattice oxygen species and promoting the water‐splitting pathway from the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) toward the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), thus accelerating reaction kinetics. Under coupled ultrasonic vibration and illumination, the optimized BTMO‐6 photoanode delivers a high photocurrent density of 2.18 mA cm −2 at 1.23 V RHE and exhibits a piezoelectric coefficient (d 33 ) of 52.3 pm V −1 . This work reveals that Jahn–Teller distortion simultaneously enhances piezo‐polarization and tunes reaction pathways, offering new insights for robust Piezo‐PEC water‐splitting systems.

title: Dual Descriptor‐Guided Design of Hydrated Eutectic Electrolytes for Stable Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries promise large‐scale storage, yet anode irreversibility remains the principal barrier. Eutectic electrolytes, comprising hydrogen‐bond donors (HBDs) and acceptors (HBAs), can suppress H 2 O activity and regulate Zn 2+ desolvation through hydrogen‐bond networks, offering a promising remedy. However, the screening of polyol‐based HBDs still relies on empirical trials, lacking quantitative molecular criteria. Herein, two orthogonal descriptors, effective hydroxyl density (EOD) and minimum electrostatic potential (MEP), are proposed based on the saturation and directionality of hydrogen bonds to evaluate polyols from two aspects of hydrogen‐bond network formation and Zn 2+ coordination. A series of C 2 –C 6 polyols are explored for hydrated eutectic electrolytes, revealing inconsistency between bulk hydrogen‐bond strength and battery performance. Erythritol (Ery, C 4 , EOD = 0.022 Å −3 , MEP = −1.73 eV) optimizes interfacial adsorption stability and desolvation kinetics. It constructs an Ery‐enriched interfacial layer to induce preferred (101) Zn texture. The symmetric cell stably cycles over 6740 h at 2 mA cm −2 with 1 mAh cm −2 , and the Zn||I 2 full cell exhibited 11 400 cycles at 10 C. This work establishes theoretical design principles for the selection of polyol HBDs when keeping the HBA component fixed as a zinc salt, shifting the paradigm from trial and error to rational design.

title: Pore‐Stitching Engineering of Biomass‐Derived Hard Carbon for Enhanced Sodium‐Ion Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass‐derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising and cost‐effective anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). Prior to carbonization, biomass precursors are commonly subjected to acid/alkali purification to remove metallic and non‐metallic impurities. However, the accompanying ionic etching process often generates abundant through‐pores and disrupts the carbon framework, leading to increased irreversible capacity loss. Herein, we propose a “pore stitching” strategy using hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) as a functional reconstruction precursor. The hydroxyl‐rich HEC is proposed to interact with oxygen‐containing sites in the demineralized precursor and to be retained within accessible pore regions during mixing and drying. During subsequent carbonization, HEC‐derived carbon contributes to the reconstruction of the disrupted carbon framework, resulting in reduced open surface exposure and a redistributed micro/ultramicroporous architecture while preserving favorable Na + storage domains. Consequently, the optimized HC delivers a high reversible capacity of 375.3 mAh g − 1 at 20 mA g − 1 . A 700 mAh pouch cell pairing this HC with sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 , NFPP) delivers 150 Wh kg − 1 based on the combined active‐material mass of both electrodes and retains 97.8% capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a viable route for converting impurity‐rich agricultural waste into high‐performance HC anodes for practical sodium‐ion energy storage.

title: A Quasi‐n‐i‐p Architecture Realized by Sequential Lamination Delivers 20.58% Efficiency in Inverted Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Inverted organic solar cells (OSCs) are promising for their enhanced operational stability; however, their power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) have lagged those of conventional devices, largely due to interfacial losses at the active layer/metal‐oxide interface. Here, we develop a sequential lamination strategy to construct a quasi‐n‐i‐p active layer comprising an acceptor‐rich layer, a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) core, and a donor‐rich layer. This vertically engineered architecture establishes cascade energy‐level alignment and preserves interfacial integrity, thereby facilitating efficient charge extraction and suppressing recombination losses. As a result, the optimal device achieves a PCE of 20.58%, with a certified efficiency of 20.07%, placing it among the highest reported for single‐junction inverted OSCs. This architecture was successfully fabricated with different donor‐rich layers, BHJ cores, and acceptor‐rich layers, demonstrating broader material applicability across multiple material combinations. Interfacial adhesion and vertical compositional control improve electrical continuity, enhance charge generation and transport, and reduce trap‐assisted and bimolecular recombination, leading to higher open‐circuit voltage, short‐circuit current density, and fill factor. This work provides a scalable route to active‐layer engineering in inverted OSCs and offers a general strategy for high‐performance organic photovoltaic fabrication.

title: Pre‐Intercalated Cation Optimizing Proton Topochemistry for High‐Performance Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Cation pre‐intercalated oxides have been widely explored as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Although the influence of intercalants on the material structure and Zn 2+ storage capacity has been adequately studied, an in‐depth understanding of the influence of intercalants on proton storage is still lacking. Especially, proton transport exhibits ultrafast kinetics as an ideal charge carrier, playing a crucial role in the performance of AZIBs. We show that pre‐intercalated K + in K 0.5 V 6 O 13 (KVO) not only reinforces the [VO] framework but also optimizes the hydrogen‐bonded network composed of confined lattice water, achieving ultrafast proton transport. Benefiting from the optimization of proton topochemistry, the capacity, rate performance, and cycling stability of KVO improve significantly. KVO delivers a high reversible capacity of 462.9 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 and 82.3% retention after 20000 cycles at 20 A g −1 . Even with the high mass loading of 19.2 mg cm −2 , a KVO||Zn pouch cell with 539.2 mAh capacity can achieve stable cycling for more than 300 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . This work provides new insights into how pre‐intercalated cations affect the proton topochemistry and electrochemical performance of inorganic cathodes.

title: Asymmetric‐Isomerization Dimer Acceptors via Modular Molecular Design Enable Highly Efficient Binary Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Dimer acceptors are attractive for organic solar cells (OSCs) owing to their combination of stability and high efficiency, yet the efficiency of dimer‐based binary devices has long stagnated below 20%. The limitation stems from weak intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) and poor locally excited/charge‐transfer (LE/CT) state hybridization, which are direct consequences of the canceled dipole moments in symmetric dimer architectures. In this work, we adopt an asymmetric‐isomerization strategy to design two novel dual‐asymmetric isomeric dimer acceptors QCl‐YF and QF‐YCl. Compared with QCl‐YF, QF‐YCl exhibits an enhanced ICT effect as evidenced by a larger electron‐hole spatial separation, which promotes LE/CT hybridization and enables more efficient carrier dynamics. Moreover, the stronger electrostatic potential and dipole moment of QF‐YCl enhances the intermolecular interactions to improve donor/acceptor compatibility and film‐forming process in blend film, consequently leading to more ordered film morphology. Consequently, the QF‐YCl‐based device achieves a record PCE of 20.23% (vs. 19.60% for QCl‐YF), achieving the highest efficiency for dimer‐based binary OSCs. This work demonstrates that asymmetric‐isomerization is a precise and effective design strategy for high‐performance dimer acceptors.

title: A 3D‐Printed Biochemical–Mechano–Thermally Responsive Multicellular Tumor Organoid Platform Decodes Biochemical‐Physical Regulation of Cancer–Immune Crosstalk and Chemoresistance
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Oral tumors are not shaped by biochemical signals alone; they also evolve within mechanically active and thermally fluctuating microenvironments that critically regulate malignant progression, immune remodeling, and therapeutic resistance. Here, we develop a dynamic bioorthogonal organoid platform that couples a 3D‐printed photothermal elastic scaffold with an interpenetrating hydrogel network derived from decellularized oral mucosa extracellular matrix, enabling the reconstruction of in vivo‐like structural support, matrix‐derived biochemical cues, spatial cellular compartmentalization, and dynamic physical stimulation. Through click chemistry‐mediated cell anchorage and hydrogel encapsulation, oral cancer cells and macrophages are spatially organized into a compartmentalized cancer–immune niche. Under cyclic mechanical stretch and near‐infrared‐triggered periodic photothermal stimulation, dynamic culture markedly enhances cancer cell proliferation and glycolytic reprogramming while concomitantly polarizing macrophages toward a pro‐tumoral M2 phenotype. In both monoculture and coculture settings, biochemical–mechano–thermal stimulation substantially increases cancer cell chemoresistance. Mechanistically, these biochemical‐physical cues activate stress‐adaptive and survival programs while enriching cancer stem‐like populations. In a xenograft mouse model exposed to in vivo biochemical, mechanical and thermal stimulation, dynamic conditioning markedly accelerates tumor progression, enhances metastatic potential, and confers pronounced chemoresistance. Together, this study establishes a biomimetic multicellular tumor platform for uncovering how dynamic biochemical‐physical cues orchestrate cancer–immune crosstalk and therapeutic failure.

title: Electronic effects on sputtering of fusion materials under light ion impact
abstract: Understanding material behavior under ion bombardment is a crucial aspect in predicting material surface modification and the lifetime of plasma-facing materials in fusion devices. Atomistic simulations are commonly employed to calculate key ion irradiation outcomes such as sputtering and reflection yields. However, within this simulation framework, the energy dissipation of ions in the electronic system is often neglected or treated using a simple velocity-dependent friction force. Although this approximation can be adequate for slow heavy ions, light ions in the sub-keV range lose a substantial fraction of their energy to electronic excitations, requiring a more realistic energy transfer description. Here, we incorporate trajectory-resolved electronic stopping obtained from ab initio calculations into molecular dynamics simulations of hydrogen and helium irradiation of tungsten and iron. We show that density-dependent electronic stopping leads to systematic variations in sputtering yields, especially for tungsten and lower impact energies, whereas reflection yields are found to be largely insensitive to the model choice. Material-dependent features are identified and mainly attributed to different relative contributions of projectile and recoil electronic energy loss. This work provides a physically motivated approach to improve the accuracy of the sputtering data used in plasma-surface interaction modeling.

title: Disruption halo currents and voltages measured on the HBT-EP tokamak
abstract: This paper presents measurements of disruption halo currents on the High Beta Tokamak—Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) experiment using 4 high-field side (HFS) tile arrays spaced at equal intervals of toroidal angle. Current flow through the tiles is measured using Rogowski coils external to the tokamak vessel. Tiles can also be operated as floating probes measuring their voltage with respect to the local chamber. Poloidal and toroidal distributions of halo currents are presented, along with a description and explanation of voltage measurements for both axisymmetric and rotating halo currents. Arcing on tiles generates current to components that greatly exceeds ion saturation current limits in the presence of an intact sheath. Furthermore, arcing is observed to occur more frequently as halo current magnitude increases. Measurements of voltages by operating tiles in floating configuration are found to be consistent with the halo voltage generation model presented in Boozer (2013 Phys. Plasmas20 082510). The dependence of tile polarity on poloidal position as well as halo current peak shape are explained using tile voltage measurements.

title: Calculation of the electromagnetic radiation emitted from the D–T fusion process in tokamak reactors
abstract: In the deuterium tritium (D–T) fusion reaction an alpha particle is released with the kinetic energy . Since the fusion reaction is governed by the strong interaction, the alpha particle is almost instantaneously accelerated to the final state with its kinetic energy . According to the classical electrodynamics, electromagnetic radiation should be emitted in such an acceleration process. In this work, we calculate the electromagnetic radiation in the D–T fusion process using both the classical electrodynamics and the quantum mechanical models. The radiation is compared with the radiation from the core plasma bremsstrahlung for pure D–T plasmas in large tokamaks. The ratio between the radiation from the D–T fusion reaction and bremsstrahlung depends only on the plasma temperature. The radiation from the D–T fusion reaction is stronger than that from bremsstrahlung if the frequency is higher than a critical value. Although the predicted radiation is much weaker than its high frequency counterpart, it is still possible to be detected in the high fusion gain reactors under some circumstances. Its effect should also be taken into account if one uses the gamma-ray emission spectrum to diagnostic for plasma profiles in tokamaks.

title: A novel high-performance confinement regime in a tokamak driven by tearing mode locking and rotation shear
abstract: In magnetically confined fusion plasmas, tearing mode (TM) locking is conventionally regarded as detrimental, often halting rotation and triggering disruptions. Contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate that locked TMs can enhance confinement by inducing an internal transport barrier (ITB). Specifically, the interaction between a locked outer plasma region and neutral beam injection (NBI)-driven core rotation generates a broad and intense toroidal velocity shear layer, which suppresses turbulence and improves core confinement. Beam emission spectroscopy and charge exchange recombination spectroscopy confirm a substantial reduction in turbulent transport and a rise in core ion temperature exceeding . This phenomenon—termed the Locking-Induced Flow and Transport (LIFT) mode—transforms a traditionally disruptive mechanism into a confinement enhancement strategy.

title: Donor-Acceptor Radicaloid Materials with Enhanced Nonradiative Decay Enable Efficient Solar-Thermal Conversion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic photothermal materials are promising for solar-driven water purification and thermoelectric energy harvesting, yet their practical deployment is frequently limited by insufficient solar utilization, suboptimal photothermal conversion, and photobleaching under prolonged irradiation. Here, we report TBT–ThT–O, a donor–acceptor small molecule in which a strong D–π–A–π–D framework, π-bridge extension, and radical character act cooperatively to enhance intramolecular charge transfer and suppress radiative decay, thereby favoring nonradiative heat dissipation under sunlight. TBT–ThT–O exhibits broadened solar absorption extended to 2000 nm and excellent photothermal stability. When immobilized in porous polyurethane foam to construct an interfacial evaporator, TBT–ThT–O@PU achieves a high evaporation rate of 1.356 kg m–2 h–1 and a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 93.05% under 1 sun. As a photothermal coating coupled with a thermoelectric module, the system delivers a voltage of 245 mV and an output power density of 3.936 W m–2 under 1 sun. Furthermore, a lens-assisted hybrid platform is demonstrated to intensify outdoor solar flux for simultaneous freshwater production and electricity generation. This work demonstrates that D–A radicaloid molecular engineering provides a viable route to stable, high-performance organic photothermal materials for integrated solar desalination and power generation.

title: Theoretical Insights into Stepwise NH3 Oxidation on Pocket-Reconstructed Cu/CeO2(100) under Oxygen-Rich Conditions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cu-modified CeO2(100) (Cu/CeO2(100)) has been widely studied for NH3-selective catalytic oxidation (NH3-SCO), although most previous theoretical studies considered predefined Cu single atoms, Cu clusters, or CuOx species, leaving the oxygen-induced reconstruction of the active Cu/CeO2 surface and its catalytic effect unclear. Here, we employ density functional theory calculations with on-site Coulomb interaction corrections (DFT + U) to identify the stable reconstructed Cu/CeO2(100) under O2-rich conditions and elucidate the complete NH3 oxidation pathways. The calculations reveal that the unique “pocket-like” reconstructed CeO2(100) surface can drive the aggregation of the isolated Cu atoms into a stable Cu3O2 cluster within the pocket area. This restructuring generates active motifs comprising geometrically flexible CuO4 units and adjacent Ce3+ sites, and each CuO4 unit can facilitate the heterolytic NH3 dissociation to NH2*, while the Ce3+ site can activate O2 into superoxide (O2–) species. The activated O2– species then reacts with NH2* to form stable NH2O* and O* intermediates. Moreover, a cooperative dynamic restructuring between NH2O* and nearby O* species gives rise to a distinctive Ce─O─NHx···O five-membered ring. This unique configuration enables a nearly barrierless (0.02 eV) proton transfer to produce NHO* and OH* species, ultimately driving the deep oxidation to form NO* and H2O*. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized pocket-confinement effect on Cu aggregation and redox-site cooperation on Cu/CeO2(100), providing mechanistic guidance for the rational design of Cu/CeO2-based NH3-SCO catalysts under oxygen-rich conditions.

title: VYQFF Peptide-Modified Brucine Liposomes: Antitumor Activity in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Mechanistic Insights
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains difficult to treat, and conventional chemotherapy has limited efficacy and substantial toxicity. We developed a VYQFF peptide-modified brucine liposome (Bru-VYQFF-Lip) and characterized its particle size, zeta potential, polydispersity, encapsulation efficiency, and drug loading. Bru-VYQFF-Lip showed greater uptake in Trop2-high HSC3 cells than in HOK cells and inhibited HNSCC-cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. After intratumoral administration, the VYQFF-modified formulation showed greater local fluorescence retention than the NHS-bearing, non-peptide comparator; this experiment does not establish systemic tumor targeting or direct Trop2-specific recognition. Bru-VYQFF-Lip also suppressed tumor growth in a nude-mouse xenograft model. Terminal serum chemistry and organ histology did not reveal overt hepatorenal or histopathological injury, although the safety assessment was limited by the absence of complete longitudinal and hematological evaluation. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses identified INHBA as a candidate mediator associated with poor prognosis. Mechanistic experiments were consistent with suppression of the INHBA/TGF-β/Smad axis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. These findings support further evaluation of VYQFF-functionalized brucine liposomes, including physicochemically matched controls, receptor-blocking studies, systemic biodistribution experiments, and comprehensive toxicology.

title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
abstract: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling
abstract: Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

title: Molecularly Anchored n-Type Quinone/Graphene Heterostructures Enabling High-Capacity and Ultra-stable Proton Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quinone-based organic electrodes are attractive for aqueous proton batteries owing to their fast and reversible proton-coupled redox chemistry. However, their practical application is largely restricted by severe dissolution in acidic electrolytes, poor structural stability, and low electronic conductivity. Herein, we report a molecularly anchored n-type quinone/graphene heterostructure constructed by integrating tetraaminobenzoquinone (TABq) with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) through a facile solvothermal strategy. Strong π–π stacking, hydrogen-bonding interactions, and covalent linkages effectively immobilize TABq molecules on the conductive rGO framework, thereby suppressing active-material dissolution, enhancing electrode integrity, and constructing efficient electron/proton transport pathways. The open heterointerface and abundant redox-active sites further promote rapid proton uptake/release and accelerate charge-transfer kinetics. Benefiting from this rational heterostructure design, the optimized TABq/rGO electrode delivers a high specific capacity of 349.78 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1, remarkable rate capability of 131.12 mAh g–1 even at 100 A g–1, and excellent cycling durability. When coupled with a 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic dianhydride anode, the full cell achieves a reversible capacity of 129.03 mAh g–1 at 0.75 A g–1 and maintains 75.43% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. Moreover, TABq/rGO-based symmetric proton battery exhibits outstanding long-term stability, retaining 74.17% of its capacity after 10,000 cycles. Experimental characterizations combined with density functional theory calculations reveal that the TABq/rGO heterointerface regulates charge distribution, stabilizes the quinone redox centers, and lowers the kinetic barrier for proton storage. This work highlights an effective molecular anchoring strategy for developing high-capacity, high-rate, and durable organic electrodes for advanced aqueous proton batteries.

title: Tailoring Localized High-Concentration Electrolytes for Wide-Temperature Operation of High-Voltage Full Cells with Graphite Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Localized high-concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) using a 1,1,2,2-tetrafluoroethyl-2,2,3,3-tetrafluoropropyl ether (TTE) diluent provide improved performance for high-voltage lithium (Li) metal batteries. However, the performance of LHCEs in high-voltage full cells with graphite anodes remains underexplored. In this regard, we systematically investigated the effect of chemical composition of LHCEs by varying TTE content and employing a lithium difluorophosphate (LiPO2F2) additive on physicochemical properties and electrochemical performances. Raman spectroscopy confirms that TTE dilution preserves anion-dominated solvation structures. Among LHCEs with TTE contents from 0 to 100 vol %, half and full cells with Li- and Mn-rich (LMR) high-voltage cathodes demonstrated optimal cycle life within the 20–40 vol % TTE. Adding 1 wt % LiPO2F2 to the LHCE with 30% TTE improves full-cell performance across the entire temperature range investigated (0, 25, and 45 °C). Postmortem analysis revealed the formation of LiF- and phosphate/fluorophosphate-rich interphases on both electrodes, originating from LiPF6 and LiPO2F2 decomposition. As a result, the LHCE with 30% TTE and 1 wt % LiPO2F2 additive effectively suppressed the transition-metal (TM) dissolution (mainly Mn and Ni) from LMR cathodes at 50 °C for 3 weeks. These results demonstrate that coupling LHCE solvation chemistry with LiPO2F2-derived interphase engineering provides a promising pathway for stabilizing high-voltage full-cell performance across wide temperature ranges.

title: Mixed –N/–O Surface Terminations Enable Fast Ammonium-Ion Storage in Ti3C2T x MXene
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous ammonium-ion batteries are promising for safety, low cost, and fast energy storage. However, the influence of electrode surface chemistry on NH4+ storage remains poorly understood. Two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXene, with metallic conductivity, tunable interlayer spacing, and abundant surface terminations, serves as an ideal platform to elucidate NH4+ storage mechanisms. Herein, the role of MXene surface termination in regulating NH4+ storage behavior is systematically investigated using density functional theory calculations and experimental validation. The calculations reveal that the –N terminations offer moderate NH4+ adsorption and high electronic conductivity for rapid charge transfer and ion transport, whereas the –O terminations exhibit stronger ion affinity and enhanced surface stability. Importantly, the mixed –N/–O terminations effectively balance adsorption strength and transition-state stabilization, resulting in the lowest NH4+ migration barrier among the modeled pathways. The calculations employ idealized vacuum-separated surfaces with isolated NH4+ and do not explicitly include solvation or electrolyte effects. Guided by these findings, a mixed –N/–O terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene is constructed via a urea-assisted hydrothermal strategy. The optimized NTC-20 electrode delivers 107 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1, retains 67% capacity at 10 A g–1, and maintains 91% capacity after 10,000 cycles. Ex situ XRD, XPS, and FTIR analyses are consistent with reversible NH4+-associated changes in the local chemical environment and possible storage involving Ti–N···H–N and Ti–O···H–N interactions. Furthermore, the NTC-20//MnO2/CNTs full cell achieves an energy density of 26.7 Wh kg–1 at 1.3 kW kg–1. The results support a dominant role for mixed –N/–O terminations in regulating NH4+ adsorption and diffusion, providing insights into surface-termination engineering for high-performance AAIBs.

title: Nanoscale Analysis of Large Deformation of Tough Microparticle-Based Polymer Films Revealed by Atomic Force Microscopy and Small-Angle X-ray Scattering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract For understanding the mechanical properties of polymer materials and establishing design guidelines, elucidation of nanoscale structural changes under deformation is crucial. This study focused on microparticle-based polymer films exhibiting high fracture energies of several tens of MJ/m3 without additives, and the influence of intraparticle crosslinking on nanoscale deformation was investigated using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The improvement of an AFM equipped with a stretching device enabled nanoscale observation of films under strain conditions of up to 700%. As intraparticle crosslinking increased, a trade-off was observed in which the Young's modulus increased while the fracture strain decreased. AFM observations showed that, although the increase in intraparticle crosslinking density did not significantly affect the deformation of each microparticle or particle clusters constituting the assembly, their surface roughness increased with increasing crosslinking density. SAXS measurements under tensile deformation revealed that the strain-induced structural anisotropy decreased with increasing intraparticle crosslinking density, suggesting suppressed nanoscale deformation within highly crosslinked microparticles. These results suggest that the trade-off in macroscopic mechanical properties is associated with a change in nanoscale deformation, from smooth elongation to surface roughening, highlighting that particle design is an important factor contributing to tough microparticle-based film properties.
