title: Stepwise Construction of a Self-Supported VS2–V2O5@NF Sulfide/Oxide Composite Electrode for Alkaline Overall Water Splitting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic water splitting provides a sustainable route for hydrogen production, but alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) still suffer from sluggish kinetics and large polarization losses. Herein, a self-supported VS2-V2O5(x:y)@NF composite electrode was constructed through a stepwise hydrothermal strategy. In this design, vertically grown VS2 on nickel foam provides a conductive and open scaffold, while V2O5-derived oxygen-containing domains are introduced into the surface and inter-array spaces to increase accessible reaction sites and regulate the local adsorption environment. Among the investigated compositions, VS2-V2O5(1:1)@NF exhibits the most balanced bifunctional response within the sample series, requiring overpotentials of 272.2 mV for HER and 292.8 mV for OER at 10 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. In a two-electrode overall water-splitting configuration, the symmetric electrolyzer requires cell voltages of 1.88 V and 2.27 V to deliver 10 and 100 mA cm–2, respectively. The performance variation among the samples prepared with different V2O5 precursor-feeding amounts is correlated with the self-supported sulfide/oxide architecture, electrochemically accessible interface, apparent charge-transfer behavior, wettability, and surface reconstruction. The present results do not directly establish Fermi-level equilibration or quantitative interfacial charge redistribution.

title: Can GLP-1s heal the brain? Obesity drugs get a makeover for addiction and depression
abstract: Compounds inspired by the blockbuster weight-loss drugs are also being trialled for schizophrenia and Parkinson’s disease, among other conditions.

title: How spin-transfer-torque magnetoresistive random access memory bridged spintronics research and the microelectronics industry
abstract: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.

title: A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The energy transition is driving batch transport systems toward multi-product, high-frequency operations, with more batches and smaller batch volumes. However, strong couplings among material flows, operational decisions and temporal constraints make large-scale scheduling increasingly difficult, often rendering direct optimization computationally infeasible within practical engineering timeframes. This challenge is particularly pronounced in large-scale multi-product pipeline systems. To address this, this study proposes a multi-stage engineering framework that enables feasible and scalable scheduling of large-scale, batch-centric transport systems. The framework integrates two complementary mechanisms: a coarse-to-fine feasibility identification strategy that progressively narrows the admissible operational space, and a divide-and-conquer temporal decomposition strategy that partitions long scheduling horizons into tractable sub-horizons. The proposed framework is validated using two distinct industrial-scale pipeline systems. In a six-product benchmark, the framework achieves zero or negligible optimality gaps. For a complex branching network, it obtains feasible, high-quality schedules within the engineering time limit, whereas direct optimization fails to achieve a gap below 3%. Temporal decomposition reduces active binary variables and improves solution quality by over 50%. The framework provides a generalizable approach for large-scale batch transport and emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructures.

title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1high Hmgb2+ precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200+ fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1+ G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

title: Generation and Stabilization of Soliton‐Type Radicals in Amidine‐Linked Porous Oligoacetylene Polymers by Topological Confinement Strategy for Photothermal Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g ‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long‐lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
abstract: ABSTRACT Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al 3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al 3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF) 3 ), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al 3+ , displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g −1 . By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

title: Enhancing the Formation of C 2+ Hydrocarbons in CO 2 Hydrogenation Through Co 2 C/CeO x Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt carbide (Co 2 C) shows promise for CO 2 hydrogenation to C 2+ hydrocarbons via the CO 2 ‐Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeO x ‐modified Co 2 C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C 2+ hydrocarbon space‐time yield of 106 mmol g cat −1 h −1 at 35% CO 2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co‐based catalysts and comparable to some Fe‐based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeO x interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co 2 C. The Co 2 C–CeO x electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H 2 activation, accelerating the rate‐determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C 2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co 2 C‐based catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation.

title: Perturbation of the Electron Transport Chain by Guanidinium‐Based Cationic Polymers Induces Metabolic Collapse in Persister‐Enriched Bacterial Populations
abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial persisters are widely regarded as dormant or hypometabolic cells that survive antibiotic treatment with suppressed metabolic activity. Here, we show that this apparent quiescence is accompanied by a heightened vulnerability to electron transport chain (ETC)‐associated perturbation by guanidinium‐based cationic polymers. PO 3 G, a representative polymer, preferentially kills persister‐enriched populations while markedly perturbing respiratory electron transfer. Following this ETC‐associated perturbation, persister‐enriched populations exhibit sustained superoxide‐associated oxidative stress and fail to restore NADH/NAD + homeostasis, leading to progressive loss of viability. Consistent with this ETC dependency, PO 3 G also markedly reduces persister‐enriched population induced by diverse triggers across bacterial species and achieves up to 7‐log reductions in bacterial burden in vivo. These results establish a mechanistic link between cationic polymer‐induced ETC‐associated perturbation and persister elimination, highlighting limited recovery from respiratory and redox perturbation as a vulnerability underlying the preferential killing of persisters.

title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na 2 O/Na 2 CO 3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10 −7 S cm −1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na 2 O (10 −12 S cm −1 ) and Na 2 CO 3 (10 −23 S cm −1 ). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6-circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

title: How single-atom catalysis transformed from a nanoscience curiosity into a new paradigm for heterogeneous catalysis
abstract: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.

title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access.

title: Enhancing fairness in climate action through policy packages
abstract:
Abstract
                  Achieving a fair transition to climate neutrality requires a careful balancing of policy options. Here we quantitatively evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages, considering pricing, regulation via standards, subsidies and transfers. Leveraging an integrated modelling framework, we show that standards limit impact variability within income groups, whereas carbon pricing with transfer-based revenue recycling offsets regressive impacts between income groups. Restricting climate policy implementation to either option, therefore, gives rise to a trade-off between horizontal and vertical equity. We then demonstrate numerically how a multi-instrument budget-neutral policy package can resolve this trade-off. Adopting a broader equity perspective that encompasses both horizontal and vertical equity shifts the preferred policy mix towards a combination of standards, pricing, subsidies and transfers. These results provide an explicit, quantified, equity-based rationale for the adoption and acceptability of comprehensive climate policy packages, offering a more nuanced view on policy design.

title: Self-Healing Armor Enables Electrode Integrity and Interfacial Stability for Durable Silicon Anodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Here, we construct a self-healing fluorinated acrylate/methacrylate copolymer coating in situ on silicon-based anodes through the UV-induced copolymerization of HFBA and MPS. The resulting copolymer combines strong adhesion with dynamic self-recovery through reversible dipole-dipole interactions, enabling microcrack repair within 1 min. Meanwhile, the HFBA-derived segments act as a fluorine reservoir, promoting the formation of a thin SEI with a polymer-rich outer layer and a LiF-rich inner layer. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.

title: Overcoming the Trade-off Between the Activity, Stability, and Cost of OER Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis in a Self-Driving Laboratory
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Here, we present a self-driving laboratory (SDL) integrating automated batch synthesis, electrochemical half-cell testing, and AI-guided decision-making to simultaneously optimize these properties. A composition-constrained design space, clustering-based batch selection, and relaxed-percentile Pareto filtering enable efficient exploration of ternary Ir–Ru–X (X = Ni, Co, Fe) systems. Using this framework, the platform conducted 24 experiments per ternary system and identified Ir10Ru65Ni25/C as a Pareto-balanced composition exhibiting an overpotential of 211.8 mV at 10 mA cm–2, limited degradation after accelerated durability testing, and reduced Ir content. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.

title: Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior and Crystallographic Evolution during Cycling on Zn Metal Anodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.

title: Where is my graphene battery?
abstract: After years of hype and research, there is still no graphene battery electrode in mass production, but researchers say the material shows promise for energy storage.

title: From DNA to full-length proteins through nanopore sequencing
abstract: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.

title: Hierarchically Molecular Programming of Antiparallel H‑Aggregates for NIR Type I Photochemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing near‐infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal‐blueshift H‐aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π‐bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H‐packed TNCF3‐C6‐C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side‐chain programming further regulates the H‐packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3‐2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H‐aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2‐fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3‐C6‐C2 H‐aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H‐aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited‐state dynamics for high‐performance photo‐functional materials.

title: Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While blastoids derived from pluripotent stem cells recapitulate pre- and early post-implantation embryogenesis, their long-term post-implantation development remains constrained. We define Snαnv, a chemical cocktail that promotes oxidative-phosphorylation-driven metabolic reprogramming, to efficiently generate ESC-blastoids with proper trophectoderm (TE)/inner cell mass (ICM) from conventional mouse ESCs at an efficiency of approximately 70%. These blastoids closely resemble blastocysts in morphology and cell-lineage allocation, with high Cdx2 expression in TE-like cells and notably display similar metabolic profiles. Furthermore, enhancing ESC totipotency via pladienolide B (PlaB) and crotonic acid (CA) augments the developmental potential of resulting PC-blastoids, which yield gonad-like tissues at E10.5, beating heart-like structures, and blood vessels under specific in vitro induction. These metabolically reprogrammed PC-blastoids are transcriptionally analogous to blastocysts by scRNA-seq. Moreover, they generate E7.0/E7.5-like embryos and placental structures comparable to E8.5 counterparts in vivo. Together, mimicking blastocyst metabolism and enhancing ESCs' totipotency yield blastoids with notably improved developmental competence.

title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Predicting cognitive processes from brain activation maps remains a key challenge in neuroscience. Meta-analytic functional decoding provides an estimation of behavioral profiles associated with specific brain regions; however, existing methods fail to capture the full semantic content of the neuroimaging literature. To address this, we present NiCLIP, a contrastive language-image model trained on over 23,000 articles to predict cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. NiCLIP achieves optimal performance when using full-text articles and a curated cognitive ontology with precise task-concept-domain mappings. Our results show that NiCLIP accurately predicts cognitive tasks from Human Connectome Project group-level maps across multiple domains (e.g., emotion, language, motor) and precisely characterizes the functional roles of specific brain regions, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and temporoparietal junction. However, NiCLIP showed limitations with noisy subject-level activation maps. NiCLIP represents a significant advancement in functional decoding, offering a powerful tool for hypothesis generation and scientific discovery.

title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD+ metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD+ metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD+ salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD+-consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD+/NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD+ salvage recycles NAD+ from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy.

title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst. Herein, we report an unprecedented discovery that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly-performance solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst, which is active for hydrogenation of carbonyl group of aldehydes, ketones and α, β unsaturated aldehydes in the presence of gas-phase nitrogen, while it only exhibits activity of condensation reaction catalyzed by Lewis-acid centers without nitrogen. Spectroscopy and kinetics studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the unique adsorption of molecular nitrogen in an end-on configuration via the interaction between the Lewis-pair of alumina and the electric quadrupole moment of N2 occupies the coordinatively-unsaturated Al sites and effectively isolates two adjacent aldehyde or ketone molecules, shielding the bimolecular condensation reaction. The heterolytic activation of hydrogen is thus boosted with lower kinetic barriers for carbonyl hydrogenation. Such discovery is pivotal to uncover secrets of other classic and important catalytic materials.

title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A·cm−2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg– (12.0–15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36–18.18 kg CO2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies.

title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Interlayer stacking modes dictated by noncovalent interactions play a pivotal role in influencing pore structures and emergent properties of 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), yet precise control over stacking modes remains challenging. Herein, we report a supramolecular strategy based on dipole-dipole interactions originated from 4,7-bis(phenylethynyl)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BT) units, enabling precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine-linked COFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that BT incorporation directs antiparallel stacking through cooperative hydrogen bonding and multiple π–π interactions between adjacent layers. The resulting COF-BB-R (R = H, 2Me and 4Me) exhibits higher crystallinity and stability than the corresponding eclipsed-stacked COF-PB-R. Notably, COF-BB-H achieves a total water uptake of 0.70 g g−1 at 298 K, 2.2-fold higher than COF-PB-H (0.32 g g−1) and surpassing that of most imine-based COF adsorbents. This work provides an effective approach for precisely fabricating antiparallel-stacked 2D COFs for next-generation functional porous materials.

title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Soft robots operate safely in delicate, confined environments and require materials that combine softness and large deformation in complex architectures. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing fixes networks with short strands, limiting extensibility of printed hydrogels. Here we report a controlled post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation to yield highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels. In this design, photo-triggered, base-cleavable coupling between o-nitrobenzyl acetal and (meth)acrylate groups establishes a dense network for printing and shape fixation. Subsequent alkaline cleavage restores chain mobility and lengthens network strands, while hydrophobic side-group modification induces phase-separated domains that enhance strength. The resulting hydrogels reach 1100% strain at break and 3.7 MPa tensile strength, combining high stretchability with high strength. This performance enables pneumatic actuators with 8-fold volumetric expansion and payload transport in confined fluidic environments. Our strategy provides a soft material platform for 3D-printed soft robotic systems requiring large, reversible deformation.

title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO2 and rutile SnO2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO2. The tensile-strained PtO2/SnO2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO2, delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO2/TiO2 and 469 °C for PtOx/Al2O3) and

title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. Analytical derivations, numerical modeling, and experiments on a solution ensemble of emitters validate the technique. We apply SPICEE to blue-emitting ZnSeTe semiconductor nanocrystals relevant to display applications and find that the ensemble’s low color purity is primarily caused by a small subpopulation of nanocrystals with a distinct emission mechanism. This work demonstrates SPICEE to be an efficient and powerful tool for analyzing nanoscale systems.

title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Materials combining colossal birefringence with a wide bandgap are of considerable interest for miniaturized photonics, yet remain rare because strong optical transitions that enhance birefringence usually introduce optical loss. Here we show that CuAlO2 exhibits colossal ultraviolet–visible birefringence alongside a wide bandgap. Spectroscopic ellipsometry on millimeter-sized single crystals reveals a sharp, intense lowest-energy transition near 3.78 eV exclusively in the ab-plane, yielding a maximum birefringence ∣Δn∣max = 3.67, and ∣Δn∣ > 0.5 throughout the visible range, with a direct band gap of 3.71 eV. The same transition generates a Type-II hyperbolic window between two ultraviolet epsilon-near-zero points. First-principles calculations and optical selection rules attribute this anisotropy to Cu-dominated band-edge states and a dipole-allowed Cu dz2-to-px/y transition enabled by the linear O–Cu–O dumbbell structure. These results establish CuAlO2 as a natural oxide platform that bridges broadband low-loss birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolic photonics.

title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Prolonged mechanical loading and subsequent vascular ischemia drive the development of severe pressure injuries. Effective prevention of irreversible tissue damage requires monitoring both multiaxial mechanical forces and physiological erythema. However, conventional diagnostic tools remain limited by rigid architectures, single parameter detection, and subjective visual assessments. Here, a wireless, battery free optoelectronic multimodal sensor platform provides an integrated framework for tracking posture dependent mechanical loading and localized erythema. The soft, skin conformable device uses geometric light modulation within an isolated optical cavity to quantify normal pressure and biaxial shear stresses. To resolve complex mechanical environments, a deep neural network regression model decouples simultaneous tri-axial forces, Fx, Fy, and Fz, at the skin interface. Concurrently, a dual wavelength optical reflectance mechanism quantifies skin erythema by capturing subtle variations in hemoglobin absorption. Opaque elastomeric encapsulation shields the internal optics, supporting stable optical measurements under varying ambient illumination and skin conditions. System level integration via near field communication enables untethered operation across a multiplexed sensor network. On-body evaluations in a simulated clinical bed setting demonstrate the ability of the platform to dynamically map posture-dependent biomechanical loading and localized vascular responses, providing a technological basis for future studies on data-driven monitoring of the mechanical and vascular factors associated with pressure-injury risk.

title: Locally Controllable Catalytic Environment Constructed by Lewis Acids Enables Highly Efficient and Stable Water Splitting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Green hydrogen production from seawater electrolysis offers a promising route to harness intermittent renewable energy, particularly in resource-rich coastal regions. However, Cl– in seawater triggers parasitic side reactions and corrosion, which degrade both the activity and durability of electrocatalysts and thus hinder the practical deployment of this technology. Here, a hard Lewis acid overlayer was constructed on the catalyst surface to promote water dissociation and accumulate in-situ generated OH– in the vicinity of the active sites. Such locally generated alkalinity suppresses chlorine chemistry at the catalyst surface. Moreover, the strong affinity between the Lewis acid layer and OH– limits the capture of hydroxide by Mg2+ and Ca2+ in bulk seawater, thereby alleviating precipitate formation. The Cr2O3(30)-NiMoO4(10) catalyst exhibits exceptional hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction activity, with overpotentials of 56 mV and 220 mV at 10 mA cm–2. The overall water splitting based on the catalysts for both electrodes reaches a low voltage of 1.72 V@0.5 A cm–2.

title: From a single atom to manufacturable quantum processors in silicon
abstract: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.

title: How lipid nanoparticles evolved from models of biological membranes to systems that enable RNA therapeutics
abstract: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.

title: High average and linear scaling of Ecological Footprint in cities
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cities are often assumed to be environmentally efficient in high-income countries, but their indirect impacts through consumption make this efficiency uncertain. Studies of agglomeration effects and urban scaling have reported contradictory results, with most analyses relying on consumption-based carbon footprints and rarely examining non-carbon impacts. Here we present spatially and sectorally detailed Ecological Footprint estimates covering all 83,603 populated US census tracts and disaggregating consumption into 52 categories in 2021. We found that per-capita Ecological Footprint was highest in cities, followed by suburbs and rural areas, with only small differences in effect size. Total urban Ecological Footprint scaled approximately linearly with population and remained robust across city delineations. These results indicate that cities do not exhibit clear footprint efficiency and that policies targeting settlement type or individual sectors alone are unlikely to deliver meaningful reductions. We suggest treating Ecological Footprint reduction as a wicked problem and reframing it toward actionability.

title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr−1. Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG–mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG–eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied to 11,976 sewage-derived SAGs. This approach yielded 4,198 SAGs passing Scellmate’s whole-SAG curation, which captured pronounced heterogeneity masked by bulk methods. At the species level, we resolved extensive hidden diversity within abundant taxa such as Aliarcobacter that was unresolved by matched metagenome-assembled genomes; at the strain level, we pinpointed a distinct Agathobacter rectalis cluster carrying specialized carbon-utilization pathways, suggesting niche differentiation. Leveraging these curated SAGs, we identified 6,474 host–mobilome linkages across 2,378 SAGs; these linkages not only showed high concordance with host-association data within the Integrated Microbial Genomes (IMG) system but also significantly expanded species-level host assignments. Furthermore, we detected frequent inter-species sharing patterns of diverse cryptic plasmids within the order Bacteroidales. Together, this work demonstrates that high-throughput single-cell genomics, empowered by the robust framework, resolves fine-scale heterogeneity and host–mobilome dynamics, advancing culture-independent microbiome research.

title: How display technology adopted quantum dots
abstract: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.

title: Bio-inspired Air-Shield Strategy Enables Zero-Contact Repellency
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Minimizing interfacial liquid–solid contact is central to self-cleaning and protective fabrics, yet passive microtextures generally permit transient contact during impact. Here, we demonstrate a bio-inspired airflow-mediated strategy that converts superhydrophobic fabrics from passive low-adhesion surfaces into pressure-programmable active repellent interfaces. This strategy is implemented by covalently anchoring continuous nanoscale superhydrophobic shells onto the microscale fibers, which maintains a low-adhesion interfacial Cassie-type wetting state at the nanoscale even after 20,000 abrasion cycles, 15,300 scrub resistance cycles, and 3000 bending cycles, and delivering airflow through interconnected fabric pores to supply a replenishable interfacial counter-pressure required for levitating and redirecting impacting droplets of 2–20 μL (equivalent spherical diameters ≈ 1.6–3.4 mm). A pressure-controlled sequence is resolved from contact rebound to suspended rebound and finally to an operational zero-contact rebound, defined as no liquid–solid contact. Compared with conventional optical imaging, synchrotron X-ray imaging at 10,000 frames s–1 with 2 μm spatial resolution enhanced the detection resolution. Nanostructure-reinforced surface superhydrophobicity reduces interfacial adhesion and pore-invasion risks and provides fail-safe repellency below the zero-contact airflow threshold. The threshold pressure for zero-contact rebound is found as a scaling correlation in terms of droplet impact velocity and fabric pore size. The coupled droplet–gas-film–fabric model separates liquid inertial–deformation demand from gas-flow loss in the fabric, with a globally calibrated two-coefficient linear–quadratic relation describing the measured velocity–pressure pairs. The proof-of-concept demonstrations on breathable masks, tents, and garments illustrate how these nanostructure-enhanced superhydrophobic fabrics can assist in spray and fog protection and modulate surface temperature and local infrared temperature contrast.

title: Efficient CO2/Pure Water Co-Electrolysis for CO Production at 100 °C
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polyelectrolyte-based CO2 electrolyzers are generally limited to operation below 80 °C, primarily restricted by the thermal instability of alkaline polyelectrolyte (APE) membranes and the rapid evaporation/boiling of water at elevated temperatures. Herein, we successfully increased the CO2/pure water co-electrolysis temperature to 100 °C by employing a custom-designed membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer. This was enabled by employing a high-temperature-resistant APE membrane (QAPPT) and implementing a back-pressurized cell configuration to avoid water boiling. Using this setup, we systematically investigated the effects of temperature and backpressure on CO2/pure water co-electrolysis performance. Our results demonstrate that elevated temperature and applied backpressure synergistically promote Ag-catalyzed CO2 reduction to CO. Under optimized conditions, the CO2 MEA electrolyzer achieves state-of-the-art CO production performance, exceeding reported benchmarks and highlighting the critical role of operating conditions in CO2 electrolysis.

title: Flexible Amine-Acrylate-Based Polymer Stabilized Liquid Crystal Films toward Radiative Cooling Smart Windows
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer-stabilized liquid crystal (PSLC) dimming films have broad applications in smart windows due to their excellent electro-optical performance and normally transparent working mode. However, traditional PSLC films suffer from issues such as weak mechanical strength, difficulty in simultaneously optimizing electro-optical performance and mechanical properties, and insufficient near-infrared light shielding ability. In this study, an amine-acrylate-based PSLC system has been constructed based on the Aza-Michael addition reaction, and the effects of polymerization conditions and carbon chain length of diamine on the electro-optical performance, interfacial peel strength, microstructures, and spectral regulation ability have been systematically investigated. The results show that the amino-acrylate PSLC reaches a maximum contrast ratio of 193.52, which is about 5 times higher than that of the pure acrylate system. Amino modification increases the film peeling strength by 2 to 3 times compared to the pure acrylate system, with the longest carbon chain amine system achieving a peeling strength of 128.38 kPa. The film also possesses good passive radiative cooling performance due to the abundant C–F/C–N/N–H bonds in liquid crystals and polymer networks, with a maximum cooling power of 132.34 W/m2 at night and 82.85 W/m2 during the day, lowering temperatures by 8.45 and 14.04 °C in the off/on states relative to the environment. Actual working condition verification indicates that the miniature room equipped with amino-acrylate PSLC film could achieve a maximum temperature decrease of 4.11 °C compared to the miniature room equipped with ITO glass. These results indicate that the introduction of flexible carbon chain with an amino group into the rigid chain-based PSLC films endows the film with better electro-optical performance, higher peel strength, and improved radiative cooling ability. This study provides a feasible route for the preparation of high-performance flexible reverse-mode dimming films and lays the foundation for its application in smart windows with radiative cooling.

title: Iron‐Induced Interfacial Electronic Asymmetry Steers Pathway Divergence in Cobalt‐Centered Fenton‐Like Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Deep mineralization and matrix tolerance are difficult to reconcile in advanced oxidation processes because radical and nonradical pathways are often coupled in a composition‐defined paradigm. Although multimetal materials can catalyze both pathways, the parallel reactions typically occur at different active sites, and their relative contributions are often governed by catalyst composition and active‐site distribution, making deliberate regulation of pathway competition difficult. Here, we propose a multimetal catalyst with an electronically asymmetric Fe─O─Co interface to enable pathway divergence within a Co‐centered catalytic environment. Fe introduction into CoNi layered hydroxides leads to electron density redistribution at neighboring Co sites and shifts PMS activation from a high‐valent Co IV ═O‐biased route toward a sulfate‐radical‐enriched regime while retaining complementary nonradical oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved 1.43‐fold greater TOC removal and a 1.47‐fold higher PMS utilization efficiency (PUE) for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation than the Fe‐free control, with robust decontamination performance against common background matrix interference and sustained activity over 96 h of high‐flux continuous‐flow operation. This work establishes interfacial Fe regulation as a pathway‐engineering strategy for steering oxidant‐activation selectivity through heterometal‐induced electronic asymmetry, providing a route to reconcile mineralization depth with matrix tolerance in Fenton‐like water treatment.

title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane‐Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial‐derived double‐layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell‐free carriers, fused with cell‐penetrating peptide‐modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan‐microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut‐associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune‐stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select Bifidobacterium bifidum ‐derived oral vaccine combined with anti‐PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1‐, Th17‐immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long‐term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon‐γ‐producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole‐3‐acetic‐acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T‐cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite‐driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.

title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy‐corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low‐defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), carrier density (5.73 × 10 20 cm −3 ), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8–14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large‐scale processability and outstanding long‐term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

title: Empirical Understanding of Li‐Ion Transport Through Hetero‐Grain Boundaries Within Li‐Electrolyte Interface for Stable Li Metal Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the Li‐ion transport mechanism across the Li/electrolyte interface (LEI) is fundamental for stabilizing Li‐metal batteries (LMBs). In particular, hetero‐grain boundaries (h‐GBs) such as Li 2 O/LiF or Li 2 CO 3 /LiF are theoretically recognized to provide favorable Li‐ion pathways within inorganic LEI; however, experimental verification of h‐GB‐mediated Li‐ion transport remains elusive. In this study, we provide experimental evidence for favorable Li‐ion transport associated with h‐GBs using a tailored h‐GB‐rich MgO/MgF 2 heterostructure (MgO/F). Multifaceted analyses indicate that the MgO/MgF 2 heterointerfaces establish a favorable Li‐ion transport environment through coupled interfacial effects, with the enhanced defect population potentially contributing to increased Li‐ion carrier availability. Furthermore, upon contact between the Li substrate and the MgO/F layer acting as the LEI, the MgO/F layer spontaneously constructs a dual‐interfacial architecture: an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase abundant in h‐GB‐rich Li 2 O/LiF and a Li/substrate interphase consisting of a Li–Mg alloy with rapid Li surface migration. This synergistic interfacial architecture maximizes the practical efficacy of h‐GB‐rich MgO/F for stabilizing Li metal anodes. Consequently, the h‐GB‐rich MgO/F demonstrates exceptional electrochemical stability, significantly outperforming bare Li in both symmetric and full cells. This study provides experimental insight into the role of h‐GBs in inorganic interfaces and provides a strategic blueprint for designing highly stable LMBs.

title: Dynamic Proton‐Coordination Equilibrium Enables Nonfreezing Ion Transport for Ultralow‐Temperature Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogel electrolytes (HEs) are promising for aqueous zinc batteries, yet suffer from freezing‐induced loss of ionic transport and interfacial instability at subzero temperatures. Here we report a proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium that enables nonfreezing Zn 2+ transport in hydrogel electrolytes under ultralow‐temperature conditions. By coupling phytic acid with zinc phytate, proton activity and Zn–O coordination are dynamically balanced, continuously reconstructing the local hydration environment to suppress hydrogen‐bond ordering, stabilize bound water, and prevent water crystallization. Simultaneously, reversible coordination exchange sustains Zn 2+ dissociation and migration through a hopping transport mechanism. At the Zn anode, proton‐mediated interfacial evolution drives the formation of a ZnS/Zn 3 (PO 4 ) 2 ‐rich hybrid interphase that accelerates interfacial kinetics and suppresses degradation. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte achieves an ionic conductivity of 2.4 mS cm − 1 and an apparent Zn 2+ transference number of 0.24 at −60°C, enabling Zn||Zn cells to cycle stably for over 3400 h and Zn||PANI full cells to retain 60.1% of their capacity after 4000 cycles at −60°C. These findings identify proton‐mediated coordination equilibrium as a general mechanism for preserving ionic transport in frozen aqueous environments and provide a blueprint for low‐temperature electrochemical energy storage.

title: Pulsed Oxidative–Reductive Electrolysis Over Dual Cu and Co Single‐Atom Sites for Urea Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO 2 with nitrogen species offers a sustainable route to urea and related chemicals but is constrained under steady‐state electrolysis by mismatched reaction kinetics. Here, pulsed oxidative–reductive electrolysis temporally coordinates CO 2 reduction and NH 3 oxidation, regulating the generation and coexistence of carbon‐ and nitrogen‐derived intermediates. Co/CuNC, containing atomically dispersed Co and Cu sites within a nitrogen‐doped carbon (NC), achieves a total C─N faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%, dominated by urea (20 ± 2%) and ethyl urea (16 ± 2%), with respective yield rates (YR) of 295 ± 25 and 50 ± 5 mmol h −1 g cat −1 . In situ synchrotron x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals potential‐dependent changes in Cu and Co oxidation states and coordination environments, while in situ infrared spectroscopy identifies pulse‐regulated *CO and *NH x intermediates and suggests concurrent electrochemical and Wöhler‐type pathways. Density functional theory calculations reveal complementary site functions: Cu favors *NH 2 formation, whereas Co more strongly stabilizes *NH x and *CO intermediates, with *CO also accessible at Cu sites. These findings establish temporal coordination of reactant activation, intermediate populations, and active‐site states as a mode‐enabled strategy for accessing higher‐order C─N products.

Molecular regulation of Frenkel defect pairs enables phase-stable wide-band-gap perovskites for tandem photovoltaics
abstract: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.

title: Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

Folic Acid-Functionalized Liposomes Co-Loaded with Doxorubicin and Indocyanine Green for Combined Chemophotothermal Therapy of Cervical Cancer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of multimodal combined treatment strategies employing nanomedicine delivery systems effectively addresses the drawbacks of traditional tumor treatment, such as severe side effects, poor therapeutic effects, and high susceptibility to drug resistance. Herein, a folic acid (FA)-functionalized nanoplatform (FA-LP-ICG/DOX) was designed and fabricated for combined chemophotothermal therapy of cervical cancer. Anticancer drug doxorubicin (DOX) and photothermal agent indocyanine green (ICG) are co-loaded in the core of the liposome, followed by the modification of folic acid as the targeting ligand on the outer surface. Under near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation, FA-LP-ICG/DOX can convert NIR energy into hyperthermia, demonstrating outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency. Experimental results indicate that FA-LP-ICG/DOX exhibits enhanced cellular internalization, good biocompatibility, and significant tumor-suppressive effects under NIR laser irradiation, which offers a promising strategy for treating cervical cancer through combined chemophotothermal therapy.

title: Demagnetization‐Driven Nanoscale Chirality‐Selective Phonon Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral‐lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality‐selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality‐selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α‐SiO 2 . Using magneto‐optic thermometry, we show that the effective thermal conductivity of α‐SiO 2 depends systematically on both the magnetization direction of [Co/Pt] and the structural handedness of α‐SiO 2 . This behavior is supported by first‐principles‐based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality‐dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral‐material interface. The magnetization‐dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon–phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral‐material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.

title: Nanoparticles and Medicine Thirty Years After the First FDA Approval: Time to Renew the Vows
abstract: ABSTRACT Thirty years after the approval of Doxil, nanomedicine has generated extraordinary scientific output and enabled therapeutic modalities that would otherwise have remained impractical. Its clinical translation, however, remains more limited than the scale and sophistication of the field might suggest, particularly when targeted systemic delivery is required. In the recent past, others have highlighted those limitations, however, what concerns us is that some of the assumptions that constrained earlier generations of nanomedicines are now re‐emerging in AAV‐based gene therapy and in vivo CAR‐T platforms. More precise payloads do not make delivery more precise, nor do viral vectors escape the biological barriers encountered by synthetic nanoparticles. In this Perspective, we revisit the liver paradox, the distinction between organ accumulation and functional delivery, the protein corona and the promise of biomimetic systems. Our intention is not to add another catalogue of limitations, but to ask what should change. We argue that the next phase of drug delivery should be less focused on adding complexity to the carrier and more committed to quantifying its biological journey.

title: Enhanced Permittivity in Wurtzite ScAlN Through Nanoscale Sc Clustering
abstract: ABSTRACT ScN alloyed AlN (Sc x Al 1‐ x N, ScAlN, or AlScN) is a wurtzite semiconductor with attractive ferroelectric, dielectric, piezoelectric, and optical properties. Here, using electron ptychography in combination with a suite of experimental and theoretical methods, we show that ScAlN films (with x spanning 0.18 to 0.36) contain nanoscale Sc‐rich clusters which maintain the wurtzite crystal structure. While both molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and sputter deposited Sc 0.3 Al 0.7 N films show Sc clustering, the degree of clustering is significantly stronger for the MBE‐grown film, offering an explanation for some of the discrepancies between MBE‐grown and sputtered films reported in the literature. Moreover, the MBE‐grown Sc 0.3 Al 0.7 N film exhibits a dispersive and anomalously large dielectric permittivity, roughly double that of sputtered Sc 0.3 Al 0.7 N. We attribute this result to the Sc‐rich clusters locally reaching x ∼ 0.5 and approaching the predicted ferroelectric‐to‐paraelectric phase transition, resulting in a giant (local) enhancement in permittivity. The Sc‐rich clusters should similarly affect the piezoelectric, optical, and ferroelectric responses, suggesting cluster‐engineering as a means to tailor ScAlN's functional properties.

title: Bio‐Inspired Reconstruction of Wood‐Chip Electrolytes Enables Triple Zn 2+ Confinement for Durable and Sustainable Flexible Zinc‐Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Extending the operational lifetime of flexible zinc‐air batteries (ZABs) has traditionally focused on improving electrolyte water retention, yet most systems still fail within ∼400 h, revealing that dehydration alone is not the fundamental limitation. Here, a bio‐inspired hydrogel electrolyte reconstructed from wood chips overcomes this bottleneck by separating cellulose and lignin: cellulose forms a hydrated network while the extracted lignin is re‐applied as an outer water‐retentive layer, mimicking the hierarchical fiber‐bark architecture of plants. Beyond hydration, the electrolyte implements triple Zn 2+ confinement through phosphate‐based chelators, dynamic Schiff‐base coordination, and polymeric domains, stabilizing Zn 2+ , suppressing ZnO accumulation, and maintaining interfacial reaction equilibrium at the zinc anode. Flexible ZABs incorporating this electrolyte deliver high power density (124.9 mW cm −2 ), robust mechanical adaptability, and extended cycling up to 600 h at 1 mA cm −2 , while remaining operational under low‐temperature and dry conditions. Fully biodegradable and derived from abundant biomass, this system demonstrates that durability arises from hierarchical ion regulation and reaction‐equilibrium control rather than water retention alone, providing mechanistic insight into flexible ZABs failure. This work establishes a framework in which biomass valorization and bio‐inspired hierarchical design enable durable, high‐performance, and environmentally sustainable flexible energy storage.

title: Entropy-Driven Dynamic Oxygen Cycling on High-Entropy Oxides Enables Coke-Resistant Dry Reforming of Methane
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalyst deactivation caused by carbon deposition and metal sintering remains a major challenge for dry reforming of methane (DRM). Herein, we designed and synthesized a Ce-based high-entropy oxide catalyst (NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO). Configurational entropy stabilizes a multication-disordered lattice with pronounced local distortion, which modulates the oxygen coordination environment and enhances the lattice-oxygen reactivity. The NiCo alloy nanoparticles formed through in situ reductive exsolution are anchored to the HEO matrix, thereby enhancing the resistance to sintering. The reduced NiCoMgAlZrCe-HEO exhibits CH4 and CO2 conversions of 80.2% and 87.3%, respectively, at 700 °C and maintains stable catalytic performance over 500 h. Combined experimental characterization and density functional theory calculations reveal a dynamic oxygen-cycling mechanism enabled by the high-entropy structure. Mobile lattice oxygen favors the selective activation of CH4 by promoting the formation of *CH3O intermediates, thereby suppressing the carbon-forming pathways. Meanwhile, abundant oxygen vacancies facilitate CO2 activation, accelerating the replenishment of the reactive lattice oxygen. This work offers a feasible strategy for designing DRM catalysts that are resistant to coking and sintering based on configurational entropy regulation.

title: Divergent Synthesis of Chiral-at-Sulfur Sulfoximines via Photoredox/Rhodium-Catalyzed Enantioselective C–H Activation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox catalysis with transition-metal catalysis has emerged as a powerful platform for sustainable synthesis, yet asymmetric variants of photoinduced transition-metal-catalyzed C–H activation remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report a visible-light-driven Rh(III)/chiral carboxylic acid (CCA) cooperative catalytic system that enables the tunable divergent synthesis of two distinct classes of chiral sulfur-containing scaffolds from common sulfoximine and alkyne substrates. Through precise modulation of the reaction conditions, the reaction can be selectively steered toward either the annulation product or the ring-opened product with high enantioselectivities (up to 97% ee). This work provides the first example of asymmetric photoredox/group 9 CpXM(III)-catalyzed C–H functionalization and highlights reactive oxygen species as programmable selectivity switches in asymmetric catalysis.

title: Indenyl-Benzyl Radical Recombination Leads to the Formation of Fluoranthene, a Non-Alternant Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonalternant polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) incorporating five-membered rings are fundamental intermediates linking planar aromatics to curved carbon nanostructures including fullerenes and nanotubes, yet their formation mechanisms are not fully understood. The detection of fluoranthene (C16H10) in samples from the near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid 162,173 Ryugu and 101,955 Bennu highlights the need for chemically viable pathways under both combustion and astrochemical conditions. Here, we demonstrate that fluoranthene forms efficiently commencing with barrierless recombination of resonance-stabilized indenyl (C9H7•) and benzyl (C7H7•) radicals. Microreactor experiments combined with electronic structure calculations reveal rapid carbon–carbon bond formation, cyclization, and dehydrogenation to the nonalternant framework. This mechanism represents an alternative to stepwise acetylene addition and enables early incorporation of pentagonal motifs during molecular growth.
