These findings establish radical–radical recombination as a versatile route to nonalternant PAHs, providing a unified framework for their formation in high-temperature combustion systems and carbon-rich astrophysical environments like circumstellar envelopes of carbon stars and planetary nebulae as their descendants.

title: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

title: Integrated Solid/Solution NMR Assignment Enables Mapping of Dynamics and Ligand Binding in a 134 kDa Enzyme
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding enzyme function requires characterizing not only the static structure but also dynamics and ligand interactions. NMR spectroscopy provides this insight at atomic resolution, yet for large proteins, the difficulty of resonance assignment has largely confined such studies to systems below ∼50 kDa, or to observing only methyl groups. Here, we present an integrated magic-angle spinning (MAS) and solution NMR study of the 134 kDa tetrameric malate dehydrogenase from Ignicoccus islandicus (IiMDH), an enzyme of particular interest as an evolutionary intermediate between allosteric lactate dehydrogenases and nonallosteric malate dehydrogenases. By combining high-dimensional (up to 4D) MAS NMR experiments on sedimented protein with solution NMR, we achieved 92% backbone heavy-atom assignment and 91% assignment of all Ile-δ1, Leu-δ1/-δ2, Val-γ1/-γ2, Met-ε, and Thr-γ methyl groups. Building on these assignments, we used various probes of backbone and side-chain dynamics: elevated MAS NMR 15N rotating-frame relaxation (R1ρ) points to slow motions in functionally critical regions, including the catalytic loop and the mobile surface loop. Complementary methyl-axis order parameters from solution NMR identified additional flexible sites in the hydrophobic core. Chemical shift perturbation experiments upon addition of the substrate analogue oxamate, monitored via backbone 1H–15N TROSY, revealed both active-site contacts and responses in helices α2F and α3G, regions associated with signal transmission in allosteric homologues. The integrated approach demonstrated here exploits the distinct strengths of MAS and solution NMR and provides a comprehensive view of structure, dynamics, and substrate interactions in a large oligomeric enzyme that neither technique could provide alone.

title: Probing the Conformational Behavior of a Seven Hetero-Spin Supramolecule
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis and crystal structure of a 7-spin supramolecular poly-rotaxane is reported. The [4]rotaxane structure involves a trigonal thread centred on a {CrNi2} core, with each of the three arms terminated by Cu(II) centres and bearing a {Cr7Ni} metallocycle. The macromolecule brings together three distinct electron spin centers. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirms the molecule remains intact in solution, with the three types of spin center each uniquely addressable. Orientation-selective Double Electron Electron Resonance (DEER) and Relaxation Induced Dipolar Modulation Enhancement (RIDME) spectroscopies are used to selectively probe the different spin-spin interactions in the frozen solution phase and to define differences from the solid-state crystal structure.

title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic analysis of hydrogen-based ship propulsion concepts in light of future regulatory environments
abstract: The shipping sector faces ongoing challenges in developing pathways to net-zero emission concepts. Hydrogen as an energy carrier offers the opportunity to provide a low- to zero-emission solution, depending on the fuel production pathway. However, high production costs as well as logistical challenges in transporting the fuel globally hinder the economic competitiveness compared to current fossil fuel alternatives. To enable a faster adoption of zero-emission concepts, regulators such as the European Union and the International Maritime Organization have developed mechanisms that provide financial incentives and regulatory specifications. This paper investigates hydrogen-based propulsion concepts for the use case of a short-sea RoPax ferry and a deep-sea liquid hydrogen carrier. System models of different propulsion concepts are used to model their techno-economic performance under different well-to-tank hydrogen production and supply pathways. The proposed IMO GHG Fuel Intensity standards and corresponding penalties/incentives are included in the techno-economic comparison. Results are compared to a fossil-fueled baseline case and a battery-electric benchmark.

title: Substrate Length Controls Atropopeptide Complexity and Triggers Excision-Driven Scaffold Hop to Diketopiperazine Alkaloids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Atropopeptides are a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that share conserved cross-link-forming amino acids in their core peptides, yet adopt architectures ranging from simple monocyclic to complex polycyclic structures with intriguing three-dimensional shapes. These complex architectures arise from multiple C–C and C–N cross-links that are installed by a single cytochrome P450 enzyme, but the factors governing these divergent cross-linking patterns and resulting structural complexities have remained elusive. Recent studies on RiPP biosynthesis have revealed a form of substrate-controlled catalysis, in which the precursor sequence, rather than the modifying enzyme, dictates the reaction course. Here, we describe a distinct form of substrate-controlled catalysis in atropopeptide biosynthesis, demonstrating that core peptide length, rather than sequence, determines the cross-linking pattern installed by an atropopeptide-forming cytochrome P450. We further uncover an unusual proteolytic excision of an internal amino acid in mature atropopeptides, generating peptides that spontaneously convert into pyrroloindoline-containing diketopiperazines (DKPs) and thereby effecting a nonenzymatic scaffold-hop from atropopeptides to DKP-derived alkaloids, for which we provide mechanistic insight. Both the atropopeptide and the corresponding DKP exhibit antiviral activity, and their structural diversity can be further expanded through precursor engineering. Our work reveals substrate length as a key determinant of atropopeptide complexity, provides insights into the catalysis of a multicross-link-forming P450, and establishes an unprecedented route connecting atropopeptides to pyrroloindoline DKP alkaloids.

title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

title: Artificial Light-Harvesting Nanotubes: Intermolecular Charge Transfer beyond the Exciton Model
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Self-assembled nanotubes of C8S3 cyanine dyes have been widely investigated as model systems for light-harvesting complexes. Recently published data point to a brick-layer molecular arrangement in the nanotubes, in contrast to the herringbone structure previously adopted to explain the absorption and linear dichroism data within the exciton model. Here we solve this conundrum by showing that, relying on the brick-layer structure as extracted from cryo-EM, the exciton model can properly account for the observed spectral features, provided it is extended to account for intermolecular charge-transfer interactions.

title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

title: Migratory Hydroamination of Alkenes via Iron-Hydride Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The renaissance of catalytic metal hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) offers advanced tools for hydroamination of alkenes. Despite these merits, state-of-the-art MHAT hydroamination protocols are largely limited to intermolecular coupling or intramolecular cyclization, thereby necessitating new catalytic platforms to explore MHAT reactivity and access unexplored hydroamination reaction pathways. Herein, we report an iron hydride-catalyzed migratory hydroamination of allylamines, enabled by a sequential MHAT process with finely tuned 1,2-amino migration. This strategy converts readily accessible allylamines into structurally diverse alkylamines and β-amino acids through a three-step radical cascade. This protocol features a broad tolerance toward a range of functional groups, encompassing complex drug and natural product derivatives. Beyond providing an efficient approach to medicinally relevant amine scaffolds, this work establishes a new paradigm for MHAT-enabled molecular editing through radical functional group migration, thereby expanding the synthetic repertoire of alkene hydroamination.

title: Fano‐Engineered Au@Se Core–Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual‐Mode Structural Color
abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate‐free and solution‐processable, but single‐component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core–shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible‐range Mie‐resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano‐like interference between the broad electric‐dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au‐core electric‐dipole response. The hybrid mode yields Q factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single‐component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)‐curable resins and writing inks for 254‐ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization‐selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive‐index coating.

title: Ferrocene‐Based Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enable Ultra‐High Specific Detectivity in Perovskite Photodetectors
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular design of self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) for perovskite photodetector (PD) applications has largely been inherited from photovoltaics, where molecules have been designed to maximize charge extraction rather than to minimize dark current density ( J d ). Here, we move beyond conventional carbazole‐core SAMs and introduce ferrocene (Fc)‐based SAMs (Fc‐SAMs) as hole transport layers specifically designed for PD operation. These Fc‐SAMs enable a unique energy alignment strategy where the work function of ITO is modified to misalign with the valence band maximum of an adjacent metal halide perovskite. In doing so, interfacial band bending is reduced, suppressing thermally activated charge injection. Simultaneously, the Fc moiety passivates interfacial defects, lowering defect density two‐fold when compared to a benchmark SAM. These effects enable an ultralow J d of 2.52 × 10 −10 A cm −2 and a noise current of 3.80 × 10 −15 A Hz −1/2 , which generates a state‐of‐the‐art specific detectivity ( D *) of 2.56 × 10 13 Jones at 680 nm and −0.5 V. We also establish that Fc‐SAM performance is independent of alkyl chain length (0 ≤ n ≤ 6), contrasting established SAM design rules. Moreover, Fc‐SAM devices exhibit excellent operational stability, supporting LiFi communication rates exceeding 1 Mbps and highlighting their potential for commercial optoelectronic applications.

title: Molecularly Modulated Charge Retention Enables Post‐Illumination H 2 O 2 Production in Imine‐Linked Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling photocatalytic solar fuel generation from continuous illumination is a prerequisite for practical off‐grid applications, yet demands precise control over photogenerated charge retention and dark‐phase utilization. While persistent charge availability post‐light cutoff is central to dark‐state catalysis, a quantitative structure‐dynamics‐function relationship linking molecular design to charge‐retention kinetics and post‐illumination reactivity remains unestablished. Here, we report a molecular tuning strategy of the central amine‐derived units that systematically regulates charge separation, retention timescales, and dark‐state H 2 O 2 production in imine‐linked polymer networks. Systematic evaluation of the series reveals a direct correlation between charge lifetime and dark activity. Compared with the N‐centered reference, the C 3 N 3 ‐centered analogue exhibits drastically prolonged electron‐associated transient lifetime, with a ∼27‐fold longer decay timescale at the picosecond scale and a ∼3‐fold increase at the nanosecond scale. This enhanced charge retention corresponds to a dark‐state H 2 O 2 production of 4941 µmol g −1 within 40 min, ∼1.5‐fold higher than that of the N‐centered counterpart. Density functional theory calculations reveal distinct electronic structures associated within the C 3 N 3 ‐centered framework, providing a favorable electronic environment for electron localization and subsequent utilization. These results establish a molecular structure‐charge retention‐dark reaction relationship for photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production beyond the illumination period.

title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI‐driven techniques, and other high‐tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross‐contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal‐ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1‐Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene‐containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1‐Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape‐changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1‐Ru1 can be recycled via a one‐pot, cross‐contamination‐free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high‐tech applications.

title: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.

title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.

title: AC OPF learning via modular decomposition and adaptation to topology changes
abstract: We propose a novel framework for efficiently solving the AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem under varying grid topologies. Traditional learning-based approaches to OPF often retrain entire models when the network topology changes, leading to high computational cost and limited generalization. The proposed approach exploits the fact that different components of the OPF problem respond to topology changes to varying degrees: device-level operating limits remain largely unaffected, the network equations are modified locally around a tripped line, whereas the resulting optimal operating point may change throughout the network. It consists of two complementary training phases. In Phase I (modular pretraining), the OPF learning task under the intact grid topology is decomposed into three sequential subtasks (voltage setpoint prediction, power generation estimation, and generation cost computation) representing distinct functional mappings. In Phase II (adaptive learning), these pretrained modules are jointly fine-tuned for new topologies using a composite loss that combines supervised objectives with physics-informed regularization for branch-flow accuracy, nodal power balance, and operational constraint satisfaction. Extensive evaluations on benchmark grids demonstrate accurate predictions for the intact grid as well as for grids with seen and unseen contingencies. In our numerical experiments, at most 60 N − 1 contingency topologies are used for adaptation, and the largest mean prediction error among the reported variables under unseen topologies is approximately 3.1%.

title: Marine Carbonate System Observing and mCDR: New Processes, Needs, and Systems
abstract: Abstract Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.

title: Bridging deterministic and stochastic scheduling: Learning risk-aware forecast adjustments for PV-BESS operation
abstract: The participation of hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) installations in electricity markets requires modeling multi-temporal forecast uncertainty via temporal trajectories and integrating this information into bidding optimization frameworks. Most state-of-the-art approaches rely on stochastic or robust optimization methods, which are computationally intensive and offer limited interpretability to decision-makers. Consequently, deterministic optimization approaches remain the industry standard in practical market applications. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel learning-to-optimize framework that combines a deterministic mixed-integer linear programming formulation with a context-aware artificial neural network policy trained through reinforcement learning. The policy operates as a learned cost function approximation , translating probabilistic forecast metrics into time-dependent multiplicative forecast adjustment parameters. This approach preserves the simplicity and industry acceptance of deterministic optimization while effectively embedding information related to forecast uncertainty and risk-awareness into the day-ahead bidding and scheduling process for hybrid PV-BESS systems. For a real-world electric vehicle charging station case study in Portugal, equipped with 375 kWp of PV generation and a 1.258 MWh BESS, the proposed learning-to-optimize framework substantially outperforms the deterministic baseline. Specifically, it captures 39.27% and 27.26% of the maximum theoretical cost-saving potential achievable under perfect forecasts during autumn and summer peak periods, respectively. At the intraday level, the learned policy effectively mitigates systematic forecast errors, reducing the cumulative daily negative imbalance volume by 48.22% under standard operating conditions. Moreover, the framework maintains a robust operational safety margin, reducing imbalance exposure by 10.02% during large unforeseen PV generation drops caused by clouds.

title: Theory-guided lightweight decomposition for efficient and robust day-ahead electrical load forecasting
abstract: Accurate electrical load forecasting is important for operational planning and dispatch in modern power systems, yet existing models often face a trade-off among predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to imperfect exogenous inputs. To address this challenge, we propose a Theory-guided Lightweight Efficient Decomposition (TgLED) framework with a Structured Temporal–Exogenous Mixer (STEM) for day-ahead electrical load forecasting. TgLED transforms raw load data into a normalized load-ratio series and decomposes it into a transferable dimensionless trend and a local fluctuation component. The trend captures stable structural patterns through domain knowledge, whereas the fluctuation is learned by STEM, a lightweight dual-path architecture that separately models temporal inertia and exogenous drivers using efficient feedforward operations. Four-fold cross-validation on hourly load and weather data from 12 districts in Beijing shows that TgLED achieves an average MSE of 0.056, reducing the error by 9.8% compared with the previous theory-guided baseline TgDLF. Compared with recently proposed lightweight time-series forecasting baselines, TgLED achieves evident superiority in forecasting performance. On the same RTX 4090 platform, TgLED reduces the training time from 768.66 s to 6.85 s and the inference time from 19.25 s to 1.91 s, indicating its practical value for frequent retraining and multi-district day-ahead forecasting. Additional noise-injection experiments on weather inputs show slower performance degradation, indicating stronger robustness to exogenous-input uncertainty and weather forecast errors. These results demonstrate that TgLED provides an efficient and interpretable approach to electrical load forecasting under limited computational budgets and imperfect exogenous information.

title: Transport characteristics and formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in 200-cell PEMFC stack: Numerical reconstruction and experimental investigation
abstract: Due to the difficulty in directly observing and resolving internal mass transport in multi-cell proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks, current studies on stack voltage inconsistency remain largely confined to macroscopic performance analysis. Consequently, the mechanisms responsible for voltage inconsistency remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, this study develops a framework integrating offline pressure testing, pressure boundary extraction, and grouped numerical reconstruction to investigate internal transport processes and clarify the formation mechanism of voltage inconsistency in large-scale multi-cell stacks. In this framework, pressure data measured at different stack positions are used as boundary conditions to reconstruct the transport behavior of representative cells and analyze stack mass transport characteristics. The reconstructed results are then combined with sensitivity analysis of the experimental data to identify the dominant factors governing stack voltage nonuniformity. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to reproduce the development of low-voltage cells and further verify the proposed mechanism. The results show that the maximum oxygen concentration difference among cells at different stack positions is only 0.4 mol/m 3 , indicating that oxygen distribution differences alone are insufficient to cause significant performance variations. Correlation analysis further indicates that liquid water accumulation at the bottom of the stack is the dominant factor responsible for voltage reduction in the bottom cells. Water-rich simulations demonstrate that increased liquid-water loading in the bottom cells can obstruct oxygen transport and cause voltage decay. This study provides an effective numerical reconstruction method for resolving internal transport processes in multi-cell PEMFC stacks and offers guidance for improving stack cell-voltage consistency.

title: Coordinated planning and operation of SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is making modern data centers increasingly energy-intensive and reliability-critical. This trend not only raises electricity expenditure but also amplifies the economic impact of power interruptions, motivating coordinated planning of power infrastructure and computing resources. Against this background, solid-state transformer (SST)-based DC supply architectures are emerging as a promising direction for next-generation data centers because they provide a controllable interface for integrating diverse energy and computing resources. Under this architectural setting, this paper proposes a coordinated planning and operation framework for SST-based DC data centers with tiered workload flexibility. The framework incorporates nonlinear SST losses into long-term capacity planning, treats tiered workload flexibility as a planning resource, and coordinates energy storage and diesel generators for backup supply during utility outages. An annual bi-level model is formulated to jointly determine the capacities of SST conversion stages, renewable generation, energy storage, diesel generators, and heterogeneous computing servers, together with their scenario-dependent operating decisions. Piecewise linear approximation is used to reformulate the SST loss model, and an enhanced Benders decomposition algorithm is developed to solve the resulting multi-scenario mixed-integer problem. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces total annual cost while satisfying workload service constraints. Further analysis shows that nonlinear SST losses influence capacity configuration, whereas tiered workload flexibility reshapes server deployment and backup resource requirements.

title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively. To address this issue, a downside-risk pre-positioning framework is developed for the DOEH-IES that converts physical FOWT power reductions into actionable scheduling decisions. First, a wind power correction model for FOWTs is established by considering wave, floating-platform motion, and air density variation. A dynamically asymmetric envelope is then constructed to extract the time-varying downside exposure during a typhoon and further develop a downside risk indicator. Subsequently, driven by the risk indicator, BESS capacity is reserved in advance of the onset of high-risk periods. Case studies based on typhoon reanalysis data from the South China Sea show that the proposed dynamic asymmetric envelope achieves risk-oriented boundary characterization without increasing weekly average envelope conservatism, with a pre-typhoon average envelope width of 2.69 MW and a maximum downside deviation of 150 MW during peak disturbance. Relative to the comparison case without risk-informed pre-positioning, the proposed framework eliminates electrical load shedding and reserve insufficiency, increases pre-disturbance available stored energy by 72.5%, and reduces natural gas consumption by 15.0% with only a 2.09% cost increase. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively translate the risk into pre-positioning actions, safeguarding supply and equipment continuity.

title: A methodology for long-term hourly electricity demand forecasting driven by GDP and invariant load profiles
abstract: Long-term electricity demand forecasting is necessary for grid and operations planning, as well as for the analysis and planning of energy transition strategies. However, accurate long-term load forecasting with high temporal resolution remains a challenge as most existing approaches focus on aggregated forecasts, which require accurate prediction of many other variables. This study proposes a parsimonious methodology that uses t-tests to verify the temporal invariance of historical load profiles and the correlation of load with gross domestic product (GDP) to arrive at a long-term hourly load forecast. Applying this methodology first to a controlled benchmark analysing Singapore’s isolated grid, and of multi-year historical data (2004–2022) reveals that its relative hourly load has remained statistically invariant, with an overall percentage deviation of 4.24% across seasonality indices. Utilizing these invariant historical load profiles, five-year-ahead total yearly forecasts were generated using GDP as a predictor, and the hourly loads were then forecasted using hourly seasonality index fractions. The maximum Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) across multiple experiments of six years ahead forecasts was only 6.87%. To systematically evaluate the generalizability and macroeconomic limitations of this top-down methodology beyond Singapore, the methodology was subsequently tested across six European countries. Results show that the methodology achieves high accuracy (MAPE < 8%) for economies with strong GDP-load correlations (Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Spain) but exhibits some performance degradation in decoupled economies where macroeconomic growth no longer drives electricity demand expansion linearly (Germany, UK). Additionally, invariant seasonality metrics were incorporated into a short-term forecasting model based on exponential smoothing (ES), demonstrating comparable or improved accuracy relative to existing machine learning-based methods. The findings show that parsimonious approaches can be effective in arriving at long-term, high resolution forecasts.

title: Variational Bayes-based multiple neural network method for battery SOC estimation
abstract: Accurate estimation of battery state of charge (SOC) under complex and varying operating conditions remains challenging. This paper proposes a variational Bayes-based multiple neural network (VBMNN) method for battery SOC estimation. Within the proposed algorithm, a hierarchical probabilistic model based on Dirichlet and categorical distributions is constructed to characterize the model indicator vector and model probability vector. Variational Bayesian inference is employed to obtain approximate posterior distributions of the state, model indicator, and model probability vector. The posterior expectation of the model indicator serves as the fusion weight to combine the information provided by different models, thereby forming a single state posterior distribution. Through a pseudo-measurement formulation, neural networks trained under different operating conditions are incorporated into recursive state estimation as measurement models. In addition, a Student’s t noise model with a latent Gamma variable is introduced to mitigate the effects of outliers and non-Gaussian measurement noise. Experimental results obtained from the tested battery show that VBMNN achieves root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 0.40%, 0.49%, and 0.49% under three driving cycles not used for training. After artificial non-Gaussian noise is introduced, the corresponding RMSEs remain below 0.60%, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed algorithm. Additional tests at different temperatures and cross-cell validation further demonstrate its adaptability to operating conditions not encountered during training and to cell-to-cell variations.

title: Screening-based siting and metocean-aware O&M routing for floating offshore wind farms
Using cross-regional grid interconnection to relieve growing energy storage demand in renewable energy integration: A case study from China
abstract: With the rapid growth of wind and solar generation, power systems face increasing balancing and energy storage needs. Cross-regional interconnection provides spatial flexibility through tie-line power exchange, yet the implications of tie-line scheduling flexibility for capacity planning remain insufficiently understood. This paper uses the Gansu–Shandong–Zhejiang interconnected system in China to quantify how tie-line scheduling timescales affect storage requirements for bulk energy shifting and system balancing. Within a common capacity planning and dispatch optimization framework, three stylized tie-line scheduling strategies are compared: Daily Fixed, Monthly Fixed, and Annual Fixed, representing decreasing levels of scheduling flexibility. Results show that greater tie-line scheduling flexibility changes the optimal capacity configuration, particularly the required battery energy storage (BES) capacity. Compared with Annual Fixed, Daily Fixed reduces BES capacity additions by 59.2% and total system cost by 22.8%. Sensitivity analyses further show that this advantage remains robust to variations in storage parameters and tie-line capacity. These findings indicate that the planning value of cross-regional interconnection depends substantially on its operational flexibility.

title: Unlocking the green power of the North Sea: Identifying key energy infrastructure synergies for 2030 and 2040
abstract: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze and compare three key integration options and their preferred siting (onshore vs. offshore): grid expansions, electricity storage, and the production, storage and transport of low-carbon hydrogen. We focus on their potential to reduce emissions and energy system costs – individually and in combination with each other. Additionally, we study the consequences of constraints on their implementation. We analyze the years 2030 and 2040, starting from the projections of installed energy infrastructure and demand from the Ten Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2022 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators (ENTSO-E). Results show that cross-border electricity grid expansions across the North Sea are a no-regret measure, resulting in significant reductions in system costs and emissions compared to national grid expansions. By comparison, the production, storage and transport of hydrogen have a lower cost and emission reduction potential. In both the short and long term (2030 and 2040), electricity storage can help to reduce emissions, but it is not cost competitive unless emission reduction targets are enforced. Combining the three integration measures at optimal capacities provides additional benefits. Overall, the highest emission reductions can be achieved by combining electricity storage with an expansion of the grid, while the highest economic benefits can be achieved with a combination of grid expansions and hydrogen production for direct use in industry.

title: Regeneration-aware online SOH estimation framework for liquid metal batteries based on fragmented data
abstract: Liquid metal batteries (LMBs) are regarded as a promising candidate for grid energy storage, owing to their long lifespan and high safety. However, their accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is significantly hindered by the prevalence of fragmented data and the pronounced capacity regeneration phenomena observed during their high-temperature operation. To address these dual challenges, a hybrid modeling method that fuses physical prior knowledge with data-driven techniques is proposed. The framework is structured into two stages. In the first stage, to tackle data fragmentation, a curve reconstruction model based on a weak physics-informed neural network (W-PINN) augmented CNN-BiLSTM architecture is constructed. This model is capable of reconstructing complete LMB profiles from arbitrary sparse segments covering only 7% of the discharge range and remains robust under continuous and aging-biased data loss, effectively mitigating the physical distortion issues inherent in purely data-driven reconstruction models. In the second stage, to specifically address the capacity regeneration observed over the ultra-long lifecycle, a robust online SOH estimation strategy is developed. Based on the reconstructed curves, eight base health features are enhanced via canonical correlation analysis (CCA) and then processed by an online sequential extreme learning machine (OSELM) with prediction-based capacity-memory temporal features, enabling accurate SOH tracking under a strictly leak-free sequential inference protocol. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a reconstruction root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0898 Ah and an SOH estimation RMSE of 0.1443% under fragmented input conditions with 20% reconstructed curves, exhibiting superior performance compared to existing baselines. Further evaluation on a 50 Ah LMB dataset validates the scalability of the complete two-stage framework, while the Oxford lithium-ion battery dataset provides supplementary evidence for the cross-chemistry adaptability of the Stage-1 reconstruction methodology. Ultimately, this work offers a practical and reliable solution for health monitoring of LMB-based energy storage systems (ESSs).

title: Life cycle environment and direct operating cost assessment of coal to polyolefin integrated with coke oven gas, membrane separation and CO2 utilization
abstract: Coal to polyolefin (CTP) is an important route for polyolefin in China, but its manufacturing process is associated with serious environmental issues. In this study, life cycle assessment (LCA) coupled with direct operating cost analysis methods were employed to compare the CTP route with petroleum, biomass, and waste plastic polyolefin production routes. On the basis, Dual gas feed (coal gas with coke oven gas, CTP-DGF), heat exchanger network optimization (CTP-HEN), externally and internally coupled membrane distillation (CTP-EMEM, CTP-MEM) and CO 2 utilization (CTP-CCU) technologies were respectively proposed and evaluated to improve the performance of traditional CTP route. Finally, the optimal integrated route (CTP-INT) was established from CTP-DGF, CTP-MEM and CTP-CCU. The results indicated that, CTP showed the highest environmental impacts, in which coal gasification and methanol to polyolefin units were the main contributors. Among the five optimization technologies, CTP-DGF exhibits the optimal environmental performance. Compared with CTP, CTP-INT reduced the global warming potential and direct operating cost by 49.7% and 19.0%. In the future, the environmental impact of CTP-INT route could be reduced by 50.0% considering the low-carbon power grid. This study aims to provide practical insights into improving the cradle-to-gate environmental and direct operating-cost performance of the CTP route.

title: Optimal design of pumped hydro compressed air energy storage considering air–water coupling characteristics
Impact of sub-hourly wind dynamics on green hydrogen yield and electrolyser lifetime
abstract: Direct wind-to-hydrogen systems, in which a wind farm supplies power to an electrolyser without a firm grid connection, must accommodate the full variability of the wind resource, yet many existing techno-economic and design studies rely on input data with temporal resolutions of several minutes to one hour. This coarse averaging can mask short-term power fluctuations that drive electrolyser performance, cycling and degradation. This paper presents a novel wind-to-electrolyser model that synthesises effective wind speed suitable for a power curve wind model at 1 Hz, combining low-frequency trend variation, mesoscale wind speed changes and Kaimal turbulence, validated against aeroelastic simulations. The resulting power output is supplied to a PEM electrolyser model incorporating bank-level thermal dynamics and steady-state, cyclic and on/off degradation, enabling the effect of wind-power variability on long-term electrolyser performance to be quantified. Using 10-year simulations of a wind farm at a site in Orkney, Scotland, two scenarios are investigated: the effect of wind farm size (1–10 turbines) and input temporal resolution (1 s, 1 min, 10 min) on power variability, degradation and hydrogen production; and the effect of turbine configuration for a fixed installed capacity (three 5 MW turbines versus one 15 MW turbine). Results show that coarser temporal resolution substantially overestimates hydrogen production, particularly for small wind farms, where 10-minute-averaged data increase predicted output by up to 428% relative to 1 s data, primarily due to underestimated on/off and cyclic degradation. Aggregating turbines and, to a lesser extent, using larger rotors both smooth the power input and reduce this sensitivity, though the effect remains significant even for 10-turbine farms. These findings demonstrate that high-frequency wind power variability must be explicitly considered in the design and performance assessment of wind-to-hydrogen systems.

title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. In this study, ground-based high-resolution spectroradiometer measurements (213 channels, 350–1052 nm) are exploited as an input to short-horizon PV forecasting for the first time, and the gain is quantified across two climates and multiple years using data from the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS). A SpectralEncoder is introduced, a lightweight 1-D convolutional network applied along the wavelength axis, combined with a physically motivated spectral-ratio representation that decouples spectral shape from broadband magnitude. Performance is evaluated under a dual-dimension framework crossing ramp/non-ramp conditions with clear/intermediate/overcast regimes defined by the clear-sky index. At the primary German site (temperate oceanic; trained 2018–2021, tested 2023), overall RMSE is reduced by 4.4% with spectral inputs, with the largest gain (+9.4%) under overcast ramp conditions, the regime most damaging to grid balancing. At the Australian site (hot desert; trained 2018–2020, tested 2022) the gain is 2.7%, of the same sign as at the German site. A noise-replacement control confirms the gain is driven by genuine spectral structure rather than dimensionality. The contribution is positively signed across forecast horizons from 15 to 90 min, holds across three model families (TCN, LSTM, LightGBM), and is statistically significant under day-block bootstrap ( p < 0.001 ). Post-hoc wavelength-importance analysis localises the signal to visible and near-infrared channels coinciding with known atmospheric absorption features, with cross-site Pearson correlation r = 0.69 . As market clearing intervals shrink and PV penetration rises, ground-based spectral irradiance, already collected at BSRN and collaborative PV testing networks worldwide, is a low-cost, deployable input feature for intra-hour forecasts.

title: Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe
Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: A probability-box framework for quantifying office building air conditioning flexibility under multi-source uncertainty
abstract: Air conditioning systems are important flexible resources in buildings. However, their flexibility potential is highly uncertain due to unpredictable load disturbances caused by weather and occupancy variations. These uncertainties often lead to inconsistent load reduction outcomes, even when identical operating strategies are applied. To address the challenge of accurate quantification, this study proposes a probability box (P-box) model to characterize such potential under uncertainty. After defining the perturbation ranges and probability distributions of uncertain parameters, a stochastic load scenario generation method is employed, combining Monte Carlo sampling with Savitzky-Golay filtering to simulate multi-source disturbance conditions. The proposed P-box model is then evaluated for its prediction accuracy and adaptability based on these scenarios. The method is demonstrated using a calibrated office-building model in Tianjin under summer cooling conditions. Results show that under temperature reset and precooling strategies, the P-box model yields remarkably low prediction errors, the Wasserstein-based prediction achieves relative errors of 9.22% and 4.58% with respect to load reduction simulated under field-measured inputs, compared with 16.98% and 7.90% for the traditional deterministic methods. Moreover, the 100% P-box interval enveloped all evaluated samples, while narrower confidence intervals provided risk-dependent coverage, which accurately delineates the adjustable load range of buildings under multi-source disturbance conditions. This provides a reliable representation method for flexible resource scheduling and demand response strategy formulation.

title: Enzyme- or Au Nanoparticle-Loaded Fe3+-Ion-Cross-Linked Carboxymethyl Cellulose Hydrogel Microcapsules: Functional Frameworks for Enhanced Catalytic and Enantioselective Transformations
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of catalytic nanoassemblies or microassemblies emulating native enzymes attracts scientific interest. Here, we introduce the synthesis and characterization of Fe3+-bridged methacrylate carboxymethyl cellulose, Fe3+-MACMC, microcapsules (MCs) as catalytic carriers emulating native peroxidase activities. These are reflected by the H2O2-catalyzed oxidation of tetramethylbenzidine, TMB, to TMB+• or the H2O2-catalyzed oxidation of dopamine to aminochrome by the Fe3+-MACMC MCs. Integration of glucose oxidase (GOx) or Au nanoparticles (AuNPs, 1.9 ± 0.5 nm) into the MC boundaries enables the operation of oxidase/peroxidase biomimetic cascades by the engineered MCs. In these systems, aerobic oxidation of d-glucose by GOx, or of d-/l-glucose by AuNPs, yields gluconic acid and H2O2. The resulting H2O2 mediates the Fe3+-MACMC MC-catalyzed oxidation of TMB to the colored TMB+• (λ = 652 nm), providing a colorimetric signal for probing the catalytic cascades. By molecular imprinting of d- or l-glucose binding sites into the MC boundaries, enhanced aerobic oxidation of d-glucose by the GOx-functionalized MCs, or of d-/l-glucose by the AuNP-modified MCs, is accomplished. The enhanced activities of the molecular imprinted MCs are attributed to enhanced binding of the reactive substrate to the imprinted sites (“molarity effect”). In addition, imprinting of d- or l-glucose sites into the MC boundaries yields chiral binding sites, enabling the chiroselective-cascaded oxidation of d- or l-glucose by the imprinted MCs. Furthermore, imprinting of l- or d-DOPA sites into the Fe3+-MACMC MC boundaries enables the H2O2-mediated, enantioselective oxidation of l-/d-DOPA to dopachrome by the peroxidase-mimicking Fe3+-MACMC MCs.

title: Crystallographic Parity and Inverse Area Scaling in Two-Dimensional Perovskite Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for next-generation high-density non-volatile memory; however, conventional polycrystalline oxide FTJs face issues with defect-induced leakage and degraded ferroelectricity at nanometer scales. Here, we demonstrate atomically defined nanocrossbar FTJs based on single-crystalline two-dimensional (2D) Dion–Jacobson perovskite nanosheets designed to address these scaling challenges. Electrical transport measurements reveal crystallographic-parity-dependent switching behavior: odd-layered (m = 3, 5) homologs exhibit hysteretic switching consistent with ferroelectric tunnel barriers, whereas even-layered (m = 4, 6) homologs show non-switching behavior consistent with paraelectric controls. Simmons-model analysis supports direct tunneling as the dominant transport mechanism through the atomically uniform nanosheet barriers, even at the smallest junction area of 520 nm2. Notably, the tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio increases as the junction area decreases, reaching approximately 35, consistent with the suppression of defect-induced OFF-state current inhomogeneity under nanoconfinement. These FTJs show strong non-volatile retention (extrapolated to 10 years) and reliable switching endurance (100 cycles) at room temperature. These results highlight that crystallographic layer parity and nanoconfinement-enabled defect avoidance serve as key design principles for scalable 2D ferroelectric tunnel devices and facilitate pathways toward ultra-dense post-Moore memory and neuromorphic computing architectures. This favorable scaling behavior aligns lateral miniaturization with improved memory contrast and, together with the metal-electrode nanocrossbar architecture, provides a promising basis for high-density integration if wafer-scale nanosheet assembly and reproducible interface control can be established.

title: Ultrastable Cycling of Sodium Metal Battery at Rates Exceeding 20 C Achieved with a NaB3H8-SiO2 Composite Solid Electrolyte
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Solid-state sodium metal batteries are promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage due to their inherent safety and low cost. However, the development of solid electrolytes that support high-rate (>20 C) cycling for fast-charging applications remains a major challenge. Herein, we explore how adding SiO2 affects the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression of NaB3H8, to develop superior solid electrolytes for high-rate batteries. The composites featuring an amorphous passivating layer with B–O bonds were fabricated via ball milling. Among them, NaB3H8-40%SiO2 exhibits the best conductivity, reaching 0.62 mS cm–1 at 25 °C, 2 orders of magnitude higher than that of pristine NaB3H8. Crucially, by reducing electronic conductivity and enhancing mechanical strength, it possesses a high critical current density of up to 6.5 mA cm–2, significantly higher than that of other reported hydridoborates. The Na/NaB3H8-40%SiO2/TiS2 batteries exhibit superior rate capability (216.4 mAh g–1 at 1 C and 143.1 mAh g–1 at 20 C) and long-term cycling stability (nearly 100.0% capacity retention after 2000 cycles at 20 C) at 30 °C. This work offers a promising approach for the development of innovative solid electrolytes in fast-charging or high-power-density sodium metal batteries.

title: One-Step Preparation of a Self-Standing LiFePO4 Cathode with an In Situ SiO2 Coating via Modified Coaxial Electrospinning for Advanced Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract LiFePO4 cathodes have gained much attention for Li-ion batteries due to their superior electrochemical and economic features. However, their practical applications are limited by poor electronic conductivity, sluggish lithium-ion diffusion, and unstable cathode/electrolyte interfaces. Conventional approaches require separate electrode fabrication and surface coating steps, increasing process complexity. Herein, a modified coaxial electrospinning method was developed to prepare a free-standing LiFePO4 cathode with a simultaneous in situ SiO2 coating. The core solution consists of LiFePO4 and polyacrylonitrile, while the shell solution consists of ethanol and tetraethyl orthosilicate. The modified coaxial electrode (CE-LFP@SiO2) exhibits a more uniform and smaller average fiber diameter (200 nm) compared to the single electrospinning electrode (E-LFP). Results confirm the formation of a thin SiO2 surface coating. The discharge capacity at 0.1 C reaches 166.3 mAh g–1, compared with 160.0 mAh g–1 for E-LFP and 150.0 mAh g–1 for a conventional LiFePO4 electrode (LFP). CE-LFP@SiO2 provides a capacity retention of 89% after 300 cycles, compared with 78 and 74% for E-LFP and LFP, respectively. The lithium-ion diffusion coefficient increases to 4.70 × 10–13 cm2 s–1, compared with 5.43 × 10–14 cm2 s–1 for LFP. This work demonstrates a simple one-step strategy for simultaneously fabricating and coating free-standing LiFePO4 cathodes.

title: Next-Generation Autocatalysis-Integrated Antibody-Bioorthogonal Catalyst Conjugates for Amplified Cell-Surface Antigen Imaging and Targeted In Situ Prodrug Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Immunoassays and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) rely on specific antigen–antibody recognition for biomarker detection and targeted cancer therapy; however, their practical performance is often hampered by low antigen abundance, which yields weak readout signals or insufficient local drug concentrations. Autocatalytic bioorthogonal reactions offer an attractive route to achieve exponential signal amplification, but existing CuAAC-based autocatalytic systems suffer from slow multistep ligand assembly and fluorophore self-quenching that degrade signal-to-background ratios. Herein, we report a next-generation autocatalysis-integrated bioorthogonal catalyst-linked immunosorbent assay (BCLISA) employing bis(triazolylmethyl)aminopropyne (DTTA) as a key autocatalytic precursor. Unlike the prior tripropargylamine (TPA) system that demands three successive CuAAC events for ligand formation, DTTA assembles active tris(triazolylmethyl)amine ligands via only one single CuAAC reaction with 7-azidocoumarin (7AC), incorporating merely one coumarin moiety per ligand to mitigate fluorescence self-quenching. Benefiting from accelerated kinetics and suppressed self-quenching, DTTA-mediated autocatalysis enables sensitive in vitro detection of recombinant HER2 and BK polyomavirus VP1 antigens, outperforming commercial ELISA kits. Functionalized with n-octyl lipid tails, DTTA-C8 anchors autocatalytic cascades onto living cell membranes, allowing confocal imaging and quantitative measurement of low-abundance cell-surface antigens free from endogenous enzyme interference. Furthermore, autocatalytically generated copper catalytic centers drive local CuAAC-mediated prodrug cyclization to produce cytotoxic agents. Distinct from conventional ADC approaches that pursue high drug-to-antibody ratios, our strategy achieves targeted in situ drug activation without heavy antibody modification, retaining native antibody-binding capacity and eliciting antigen-selective cancer-cell death. This work illustrates the utility of rationally optimized autocatalytic bioorthogonal cascades to couple antibody-based molecular recognition with exponential chemical amplification for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

title: Nickel Nanoparticles Anchored by Nano-ZrO2 on SiO2 for CO2 Methanation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract ZrO2 is an effective support for CO2 methanation, but its low surface area limits the dispersion and thus activity and stability of the Ni/ZrO2 catalyst. Herein, a ZrO2/SiO2 support was constructed by dispersing nano-ZrO2 on high-surface-area SiO2 to improve the activity and anti-sintering capability of the Ni catalysts. The results showed that SiO2 stabilized the nano-ZrO2, which further provided favorable sites for dispersing and stabilizing Ni species. Ni/0.4ZS exhibited decent performance among the Ni/xZS catalysts (x was the mass ratio of ZrO2 to SiO2) due to the increased dispersion of Ni. Moderate CeO2 promoter addition further improved the activity and resistance to deactivation due to the increased dispersion of Ni NPs and the enhanced adsorption of CO2. XPS and DFT results indicated that the composite support strengthened the electronic interaction between Ni species and the support. Furthermore, based on the experimental and DFT results, it is proposed that additional geometric stabilization of Ni species may be provided by the spatially constrained sites between adjacent nano-ZrO2 particles. These findings demonstrated that constructing nano-ZrO2 on SiO2 was an effective strategy for developing active and stable Ni-based catalysts for CO2 methanation.

title: Molecularly Aligned Insoluble Nanoaggregates for Ah‐Level Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving stable Ah‐level aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) remains a critical challenge due to severe water decomposition and dendrite growth. Conventional aqueous electrolytes adopt soluble ligands to stabilize the interfaces, yet these species are insufficient to isolate interfacial water contact owing to their intrinsic hydrophilicity. Herein, we design a molecularly aligned electrolyte (MAE) that incorporates insoluble ligands in aqueous solutions to stabilize both electrodes. By utilizing the π−π stacking between benzylideneacetone (BA) and 2‐naphthol polyoxyethylene (NPE), insoluble BA molecules form nanoaggregates with NPE and are stably dispersed within the aqueous electrolyte. At both interfaces, the BA−NPE nanoaggregates form hydrophobic interfacial layers that prevent water attack, thereby effectively suppressing side reactions. In addition, BA−NPE nanoaggregates substantially increase the nucleation overpotential and form a fluorine‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), promoting dendrite‐free Zn plating/stripping. Consequently, the Zn//Zn cell exhibits stable cycling for over 4500 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . More impressively, the Zn//NH 4 V 4 O 10 pouch cell delivers capacities exceeding 1.3 Ah for over 900 cycles with a retention rate of 81.8%, validating the significance of the insoluble ligand strategy under practical conditions.

title: Rational Solvent Fluorination Design for Solvation Regulation Enabling Stable Interfaces in High‐Voltage Li‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Fluorinating electrolyte solvents is an effective strategy to enhance the interfacial stability of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) under high‐voltage conditions, where severe interfacial side reactions typically undermine the long‐term performance. However, the influence of both the number and positional arrangement of fluorinated groups on solvation structure remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically investigate how trifluoromethyl group number and substitution position in diethyl carbonate (DEC) derivatives affect Li + solvation behavior. It is revealed that the introduction of a DEC‐based solvent with symmetric two trifluoromethyl groups tends to regulate the solvation structure enriched with anions and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). This optimized solvation structure facilitates the formation of a robust cathode‐electrolyte interphase derived from both anions and FEC. Consequently, Ni‐rich LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathodes with a high loading mass of 10.5 mg cm −2 achieve stable cycling at 4.6 V, retaining 80% of their capacity after 300 cycles. These findings provide fresh insights into the rational design of fluorinated solvents for high‐voltage LIBs.

title: Dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles
abstract: Unlike passenger electric vehicles, heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles operate for long periods under high-load conditions. The continuous heat rejection of the engine-generator set through the engine high-temperature coolant loop makes fan/pump power directly interact with the direct-current (DC) bus power balance and generator–battery power split. Therefore, cooling power scheduling is part of energy management, rather than only a thermal-protection task. This paper proposes a dual-time-scale predictive hierarchical electro-thermal coordination strategy, termed DTP-HETC, for thermal-load reshaping in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles. A shared-encoder dual-head bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) predictor is used to capture short-horizon traction fluctuations and long-horizon engine-loop thermal evolution. The predicted thermal risk is quantified as thermal debt and converted into thermal buffer intensity B T k , which further adapts the thermal-load-shaping weights and the control-grid resolution of dynamic programming-based model predictive control (DP-MPC). By using this information, DTP-HETC advances part of the cooling effort from boundary-triggered response to thermal-risk formation intervals, smoothing cooling-induced DC-bus disturbances and coordinating fan/pump power with generator–battery power allocation. Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 220-ton series hybrid mining truck show that, under sustained heavy-load uphill operation, DTP-HETC reduces equivalent fuel consumption by 12.16% and lowers peak engine-loop coolant temperature by 2.53 °C compared with a rule-based baseline. The mean execution time is 33.7 ms, confirming controller-level real-time feasibility. These results indicate that DTP-HETC provides an effective thermal-load reshaping approach for improving energy efficiency and thermal reliability in heavy-duty electric-drive hybrid vehicles.
